Example 3.2.1.5
.

The
1
-framed stratified bundle
f:{E}\to{B}
from Example
3.1.0.15

is a stratified fibre bundle and each fibre is a closed
n
-mesh.
However the subset of singular points is not closed in
{E}

and therefore
f
is
not
a closed
1
-mesh bundle.
Meshes are in many respects similar to cell decompositions in o-minimal geometry, but impose more stringent requirements on how the cells
fit together: the strata of
{E}
do form a semi-algebraic
cell decomposition.

Observation 3.2.1.6
.

Closed
1
-mesh bundles are closed under isomorphism of
1
-framed stratified bundles.

Lemma 3.2.1.7
.

Let
\xi:{X}\to{B}
be a
1
-framed stratified bundle
that satisfies:

(1)

\xi
is a stratified fibre bundle.

(2)

For every
b\in{B}
the fibre
\xi^{-1}(b)
is a closed
1
-mesh.

(3)

\xi
is essentially tame.

(4)

{X}
satisfies the frontier condition.

(5)

The framing map
\operatorname{fr}(\xi):\operatorname{U}({X})\hookrightarrow\mathbb{R}^{1}\times\operatorname{U}({B})
is a closed embedding.

Then
\xi
is a closed
1
-mesh bundle.

Proof.

Up to isomorphism of
1
-framed stratified bundles we can assume that

\xi
is tame. Because
{B}
has a locally finite triangulation,
we can consider
{B}
as a stratified subset of some
\mathbb{R}^{m}
.
Moreover, we can assume that the underlying map
\operatorname{U}(\xi)
is the
restriction of the projection map
\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^{m}\to\mathbb{R}^{m}
and therefore
linear.
We pick a linear triangulation of
{X}
.

Suppose for the purpose of contradiction that
\textup{sing}({X})
is not closed.
Then the must be a regular stratum
r\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})
and a singular
stratum
s\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})
such that
{X}_{r}
intersects
the closure of
{X}_{s}
.
By the frontier condition this implies that
{X}_{r}
is contained
within the boundary of
{X}_{s}
.
Because regular strata of a closed
1
-mesh have more than one point,
there must exist points

x_{0},x_{1}\in{X}_{r}
and
x_{2}\in{X}_{s}

such that
\xi(x_{0})=\xi(x_{1})
,

x_{0}\neq x_{1}

and
\sigma(t_{0},t_{1},t_{2})=t_{0}x_{1}+t_{1}x_{1}+t_{2}x_{2}

defines a stratified
2
-simplex
\sigma:\|\Delta[2]\|\to{X}

in the chosen linear triangulation of
{X}
.
We let
\gamma_{02},\gamma_{12}:\|\Delta[1]\|\to{X}

denote the exit paths obtained from
\sigma
via

\gamma_{02}(t)=\sigma(1-t,0,t)
and
\gamma_{12}(t)=\sigma(0,1-t,t)
.
By linearity of the map
\xi
we have

(\xi\circ\gamma_{02})(t)=(1-t)\xi(x_{0})+t\xi(x_{2})=(1-t)\xi(x_{1})+t\xi(x_{2})=(\xi\circ\gamma_{12})(t).

Since the stratum containing
\gamma_{02}(1)=\gamma_{12}(1)
is singular,
the assumptions (1) and (2) together imply that
\gamma_{02}(t)=\gamma_{12}(t)

for all
0<t\leq 1
.
But then by continuity we must have
x_{0}=\gamma_{02}(0)=\gamma_{12}(0)=x_{1}
,
contradicting our choice that
x_{0}\neq x_{1}
.
∎

Lemma 3.2.1.8
.

Closed
1
-mesh bundles are stable under base change.

Proof.

Let
\xi:{X}\to{B}
be a closed
1
-mesh bundle and

\varphi:{A}\to{B}
a map of stratified spaces.
We then take the pullback of
\xi
along
\varphi
in the category of
stratified spaces:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}\times_{{A}}{B}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{A}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi^{*}\varphi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi^{*}\xi}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi}

The map
\varphi^{*}\xi
is equipped with the induced
1
-framing.
Since stratified fibre bundles are closed under pullback,
the map
\varphi^{*}\xi
is again a stratified fibre bundle.
For every point
a\in{A}
, the fibre of
\varphi^{*}\xi
over
a
agrees
with the fibre of
\xi
over
\varphi(a)
by the pullback pasting lemma:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\xi^{-1}(\varphi(a))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}\times_{{A}}{B}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{*}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{A}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi^{*}\varphi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi^{*}\xi}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces a}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi}

Therefore
(\varphi^{*}\xi)^{-1}(a)\cong\xi^{*}(\varphi(a))
is a closed
1
-mesh
and a point
x\in{X}\times_{{A}}{B}
is singular if and only
if
(\xi^{*}\varphi)(x)\in{X}
is singular.
Hence, the subspace of singular points in
{X}\times_{{A}}{B}

is the preimage of the subspace of singular points in
{X}

via the continuous map
\xi^{*}\varphi
and therefore closed.
∎

When
\xi:{X}\to{B}
is a closed
1
-mesh bundle and

\gamma:{|\Delta[1]|}\to{B}
is a stratum preserving path,
the fibres
\xi^{-1}(\gamma(t))
for all
0\leq t\leq 1
have the same number of
singular strata whose positions in
\mathbb{R}
vary continuously.
Since the line
\mathbb{R}
allows for no space for the singular strata to change position,
the restriction of
\xi
over any stratum of
{B}
is determined uniquely
by the number of singular strata.
When
\gamma:\|\Delta[1]\|\to{B}
is an exit path between different
strata of
{B}
, the singular strata of the closed
1
-meshes

\gamma^{-1}(0)
and
\gamma^{-1}(1)
are related as follows.

Lemma 3.2.1.9
.

Let
\xi:{X}\to{B}
be a closed
1
-mesh bundle.
Then the composite map

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}(\textup{sing}({X}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Exit}(\xi)}

is a right covering map.

Proof.

We need to construct lifts for right horns

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Lambda^{i}[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}(\textup{sing}({X}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}

with
0<i\leq k
and show that they are unique.
By adjunction this is equivalent to constructing unique lifts of the form

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Lambda^{i}[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}

where the image of
\tau
lies within
\textup{sing}({X})
.
Via base change along
\|\Delta[k]\|\to{B}
we can reduce to the case that

{B}=\|\Delta[k]\|
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Lambda^{i}[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\tau}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
id
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\hat{\tau}}

We let

\tau_{k}:\|\Lambda^{i}[k]\|_{k}\to{X}
be the restriction to the
k
th
stratum.
Using the trivialisation of
\xi
over the
k
th stratum
\|\Delta[k]\|_{k}
there must be a unique
lift in the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Lambda^{i}[k]\|_{k}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|_{k}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\tau_{k}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\hat{\tau}_{k}}

For every
b\in\|\Delta[k]\|
there must be at least one point

x\in\textup{cl}(\textup{im}(\hat{\tau}_{k}))

such that
\xi(x)=b
.
Suppose that
x_{1},x_{2}\in\textup{cl}(\textup{im}(\hat{\tau}_{k}))
with
\xi(x_{1})=\xi(x_{2})=b

then every point
x\in\xi^{-1}(b)
with
x_{1}\leq x\leq x_{2}
in the fibrewise ordering must also be contained in
\textup{cl}(\textup{im}(\hat{\tau}_{k}))
.
If
x_{1}\neq x_{2}
, a regular stratum would intersect the closure of a singular stratum, which would contradict the assumption that the singular strata form a closed subspace of
{X}
.
Therefore,
\hat{\tau}_{k}
uniquely extends to a lift
\hat{\tau}
as required.
∎

Construction 3.2.1.10
.

Let
\xi:{E}\to{B}
be a closed
1
-mesh bundle.
Lemma
3.2.1.9
implies that there is a pullback square of simplicial sets

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}(\textup{sing}({E}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{FinSet}_{*}^{\textup{op}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{FinSet}^{\textup{op}}}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}

where
\textup{FinSet}_{*}\to\textup{FinSet}
is the functor from pointed finite sets to finite sets
which forgets the distinguished point.
The functor
\textup{Exit}({B})\to\textup{FinSet}^{\textup{op}}
sends a point
b\in{B}
in the base space to the set of singular points in the fibre
\xi^{-1}(b)
.
The fibres of
\xi
are each embedded into
\mathbb{R}
and thus inherit a canonical order.
Because singular strata can not intersect each other
and each fibre has at least one singular stratum,
we obtain a pullback square

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}(\textup{sing}({E}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta_{*}^{\textup{op}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{\textup{op}}}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}

We denote the functor
\textup{Exit}({B})\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
by
\textup{sing}(\xi)
.

Definition 3.2.1.11
.

We denote by
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
the simplicial set whose
k
-simplices
consist of a closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi:{X}\to\|\Delta[k]\|
.
An order-preserving map
[k^{\prime}]\to[k]
acts by pullback along the
induced map
\|\Delta[k^{\prime}]\|\to\|\Delta[k]\|
.
There is a map of simplicial sets
\textup{sing}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}\to\Delta

which sends a
k
-simplex given by
\xi:{X}\to\|\Delta[k]\|

to the composite

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Delta[k]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Exit}(\|\Delta[k]\|)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Delta^{\textup{op}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{sing}(\xi)}

Example 3.2.1.12
.

A
1
-simplex of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
is a closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi
over the
stratified
1
-simplex
\|\Delta[1]\|
.
The map of simplicial sets
\textup{sing}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
then sends

\xi
to a
1
-simplex of
\Delta^{\textup{op}}
, i.e. an order preserving map between
finite non-empty ordinals.
For the closed
1
-mesh bundles
\xi_{1}
,
\xi_{2}
and
\xi_{3}
from Example
3.2.1.3
this order-preserving map turns out as follows:

\displaystyle\textup{sing}(\xi_{1})

\displaystyle=\langle 1,2\rangle:[1]\to[2]

\displaystyle\textup{sing}(\xi_{2})

\displaystyle=\langle 0,0\rangle:[1]\to[0]

\displaystyle\textup{sing}(\xi_{3})

\displaystyle=\langle 0,2\rangle:[1]\to[2]

Proposition 3.2.1.13
.

The map of simplicial sets

\textup{sing}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
is a trivial fibration.
In particular
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
is a quasicategory so that

\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}\simeq\Delta^{\textup{op}}
.

Proof.

Suppose we have a lifting problem

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{\textup{op}}}}
sing

(3.1)

When
k=0
the map
\Delta[0]\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
is a finite non-empty ordinal
[m]
.
Then we can construct a closed
1
-mesh bundle

\xi
over
\|\Delta[0]\|
with
\textup{sing}(\xi)=[m]
by arranging

m+1
singular strata in a line, providing the lift for (
3.1
).
When
k>0
we are given a
k
-simplex
\sigma:\Delta[k]\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}

and the map
\partial\Delta[k]\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
corresponds to
a closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi^{\prime}:{X}^{\prime}\to\partial\|\Delta[k]\|
.
Moreover, the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}(\partial\|\Delta[k]\|)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{\textup{op}}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{sing}(\xi^{\prime})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma}

commutes.
To extend
\xi^{\prime}
to a closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi:{X}\to\|\Delta[k]\|

we specify the heights of the singular strata over the points of
\|\Delta[k]\|

compatible with those in
\xi^{\prime}
.

Let
x\in{X}^{\prime}
be a singular element with
\xi^{\prime}(x)=k\in\|\Delta[k]\|
and let
i\in\textup{sing}(\xi^{\prime})(k)
be its index.
The forgetful map
\Delta_{*}^{\textup{op}}\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
is a right covering map,
and so we get a unique lift

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\{k\}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta_{*}^{\textup{op}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{\textup{op}}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\hat{\sigma}}

Denote by
\partial\hat{\sigma}
the restriction of
\hat{\sigma}
to the boundary
\partial\Delta[k]
.
Then the universal property of the pullback determines a unique map

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}(\textup{sing}({X}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta_{*}^{\textup{op}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}(\partial\|\Delta[k]\|)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{\textup{op}}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\partial\hat{\sigma}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{sing}(\xi^{\prime})}

and therefore a section
s^{\prime}:\partial\|\Delta[k]\|\to{X}^{\prime}
of
\xi^{\prime}
so that the image of
s^{\prime}
consists of singular points and
s^{\prime}(k)=x
.
By interpolating the heights in the framing over the interior of
\|\Delta[k]\|
, this provides the height of the
i
th singular stratum.
∎

Remark 3.2.1.14
.

The simplicial set
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
is not the nerve of a
1
-category,
but by Proposition
3.2.1.13
it is equivalent
as an
\infty
-category to the
1
-category
\Delta^{\textup{op}}
.
This raises the question if using quasicategories and
\infty
-categories
at this point is not needlessly extravagant;
algebraically we could just as well quotient closed
1
-mesh bundles by isotopy
to obtain an ordinary
1
-category.
We avoid the quotient to emphasise that the map
\textup{sing}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}

bridges between geometry and combinatorics, as a
k
-simplex of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
is a concrete geometrical object.
Over the course of this chapter we will extend this bridge to combinatorially capture higher-dimensional geometry.
For our theory of manifold diagrams in §
4
we will then use meshes
to explore geometries that are not homotopically trivial.
We found the framework of quasicategories to be the most convenient to formally
capture these ideas.

The simplices of the simplicial set
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
are closed
1
-mesh bundles
over the stratified simplices.
In general, we care about closed
1
-mesh bundles over more general stratified base spaces.
Via the following construction, each closed
1
-mesh bundle over an arbitrary stratified space

{B}
induces a map from
\textup{Exit}({B})
to
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
.

Construction 3.2.1.15
.

Suppose that
{B}
is a stratified space and

\xi:{X}\to{B}
is a closed
1
-mesh bundle.
Then for any stratified
k
-simplex
\sigma:\|\Delta[k]\|\to{B}

we can take the pullback of
\xi
along
\sigma
to obtain a closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi_{\sigma}
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{\sigma}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi_{\sigma}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma}

The closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi_{\sigma}
then defines a
k
-simplex of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
.
By sending any stratified simplex
\sigma
of
{B}
to
\xi_{\sigma}

the closed
1
-mesh bundle
f
induces a
classifying map

{\llbracket f\rrbracket}:\textup{Exit}({B})\longrightarrow\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}.

In general not every map
\varphi:\textup{Exit}({B})\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}

arises as the classifying map of a closed
1
-mesh bundle over the stratified
space
{B}
, even when
{B}
is a stratified
k
-simplex
\|\Delta[k]\|

with
k>0
.
However, as long as
{B}
is triangulable, we can ensure that
\varphi

is equivalent to a classifying map
in the space of functors
\textup{Cat}_{\infty}(\textup{Exit}({B}),\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})
.
We recall from §
2.3.2
that a stratified space
{B}
is triangulable
if there exists a simplicial complex
(V,S)
and a refinement map

\|(V,S)\|\to{B}
.
To make our arguments easier we will use the alternative characterisation:
a stratified space
{B}
is triangulable when there
exists a marked poset
S
so that
\|S\|^{+}\cong{B}
.

Lemma 3.2.1.16
.

Let
S
be a marked poset and
\varphi:S\to(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})^{\natural}

a map of marked simplicial sets.
Then there exists a unique closed
1
-mesh bundle

\xi
over
\|S\|^{+}

such that the following diagram commutes:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{S}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})^{\natural}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}^{+}(\|S\|^{+})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}}

Proof.

We first demonstrate this in the case that
S=(\Delta[k],T)
.
A map
\varphi:S\to(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})^{\natural}
then induces a

k
-simplex of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
and therefore a closed
1
-mesh bundle

\xi^{\prime}:{X}^{\prime}\to\|\Delta[k]\|
.
The map
\varphi
sends marked edges of
S
to equivalences in
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
,
which preserve the number of singular strata.
By Lemma
3.2.1.9
when the number of singular
strata is preserved, the heights of those singular strata in the fibre vary
continuously.
Therefore,
\xi^{\prime}
is the refinement of a closed
1
-mesh bundle

\xi:{X}\to\|S\|^{+}
so that
the classifying map
{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}
restricts to
\varphi
.

A marked poset
S
is the colimit in
\textup{sSet}^{+}
of its marked flags, i.e. the simplices
\sigma:(\Delta[k],T)\hookrightarrow S
arising
from strictly increasing sequences in
S
with the induced marking.
For such a marked flag, the composite map

\varphi\circ\sigma:(\Delta[k],T)\to(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})^{\natural}

corresponds by the first part of the proof to a closed
1
-mesh bundle

\xi_{\sigma}:{X}_{\sigma}\to\|(\Delta[k],T)\|^{+}
.
The marked stratified realisation functor
\|-\|^{+}
is a left adjoint
and therefore preserves colimits.
We glue together the closed
1
-mesh bundles
\xi_{\sigma}

for each proper flag
\sigma
of
S
to obtain a
1
-framed stratified bundle

\xi:{X}\to\|S\|^{+}
.

We claim that
\xi
is a closed
1
-mesh bundle.
For each
b\in\|S\|^{+}
the fibre
\xi^{-1}(b)
is the fibre
of the closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi_{\sigma}^{-1}(b)
for some marked flag
\sigma
.
The colimit that defines
{X}
is equivalently a quotient of the disjoint union

\coprod_{\sigma}{X}_{\sigma}

ranging over all marked flags.
The preimage via the quotient map

\coprod_{\sigma}{X}_{\sigma}\to{X}

of
\textup{sing}({X})
is the disjoint union

\coprod_{\sigma}\textup{sing}({X}_{\sigma})

and therefore closed.
Therefore,
\textup{sing}({X})
is closed in
{X}
with the quotient topology.
∎

Proposition 3.2.1.17
.

Let
{B}
be a triangulable stratified space and

I:{A}\hookrightarrow{B}

a closed triangulable stratified subspace.
Suppose that
\varphi:\textup{Exit}({B})\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
is a map
and
\xi^{\prime}
a closed
1
-mesh bundle over
{A}
such that

{\llbracket\xi^{\prime}\rrbracket}=\varphi\circ I
.
Then there exists a closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi:{X}\to{B}

together with an equivalence

\varphi\simeq{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}

relative to
{\llbracket\xi^{\prime}\rrbracket}
.

Proof.

It suffices to address the case where
I=\|i\|^{+}
for an
inclusion
i:R\hookrightarrow S
of marked posets.
By Lemma
3.2.1.16

there exists a unique closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi:{X}\to\|S\|^{+}

such that
{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket^{+}}
fits into the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}^{+}(\|R\|^{+})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}^{+}(\|S\|^{+})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces R}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces S}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})^{\natural}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})^{\natural}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\eta_{R}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\eta_{S}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi\circ\eta_{S}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Exit}^{+}(I)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi^{\prime}\rrbracket^{+}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket^{+}}}

Since both
{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}
and
\varphi
are solutions to the lifting problem

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}^{+}(\|R\|^{+})\sqcup_{R}S}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})^{\natural}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}^{+}(\|S\|^{+})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}

there exists an equivalence
{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}\simeq\varphi

relative to
{\llbracket\xi^{\prime}\rrbracket}
.
∎

Proposition 3.2.1.18
.

Let
{B}
be a triangulable stratified space and

I:{A}\hookrightarrow{B}

a closed triangulable stratified subspace.
Suppose that
\xi:{X}\to{B}
is a closed
1
-mesh bundle
such that
I^{*}\xi
is piecewise linear.
Then there exists a piecewise linear closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi^{\prime}
over
{B}
, together with an equivalence
{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}\simeq{\llbracket\xi^{\prime}\rrbracket}
that restricts to the identity on
{\llbracket I^{*}\xi\rrbracket}
.

Proof.

We again restrict to the case that
I=\|i\|^{+}
for an inclusion

i:R\hookrightarrow S
of marked posets.
We then have a diagram of marked simplicial sets

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{R}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}^{+}(\|R\|^{+})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})^{\natural}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{S}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}^{+}(\|S\|^{+})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})^{\natural}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\eta_{R}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Exit}^{+}(I)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket I^{*}\xi\rrbracket}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\eta_{S}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}}

By the assumption that the restriction
I^{*}\xi
is piecewise linear,
the composite
{\llbracket I^{*}\xi\rrbracket}\circ\eta_{R}:R\to(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})^{\natural}

lands within the simplicial subset of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
containing only piecewise linear
closed
1
-mesh bundles.
The map
{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}\circ\eta_{S}
is a solution to the lifting problem

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{R}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})^{\natural}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{S}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{(\Delta^{\textup{op}})^{\natural}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket I^{*}\xi\rrbracket}\circ\eta_{R}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{sing}^{\natural}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{sing}\circ{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}\circ\eta_{S}}

We can construct another solution
\varphi:S\to(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})^{\natural}

to this lifting problem:
Using the technique used in the proof of Proposition
3.2.1.13
,
the map
R\to(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})^{\natural}
can be extended simplex by simplex
to a map
S\to(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})^{\natural}
using linear interpolation of the
heights of the singular strata.
Since the space of lifts is contractible, we have an equivalence of lifts

{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}\circ\eta_{S}\simeq\varphi
.
Now using Lemma
3.2.1.16

we obtain a closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi^{\prime}
and an equivalence
{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}\simeq{\llbracket\xi^{\prime}\rrbracket}

that restricts to the identity on
{\llbracket I^{*}\xi\rrbracket}
.
The closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi^{\prime}
is piecewise linear through the way we constructed

\varphi
via linear interpolation.
∎

Corollary 3.2.1.19
.

Let
\xi:{X}\to{B}
be a closed
1
-mesh bundle so that

{B}
is triangulable. Then
{X}
is triangulable as well.

Lemma 3.2.1.20
.

Let
\xi:{X}\to{B}
be a closed
1
-mesh bundle.
Then the induced map

\textup{Exit}(\xi):\textup{Exit}({X})\longrightarrow\textup{Exit}({B})

is a categorical fibration.
In particular when
{B}
is a fibrant stratified space then so is
{X}
.

Proof.

To show that the map
\textup{Exit}(\xi)
is an inner fibration,
we need to construct lifts for inner horns

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Lambda^{i}[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Exit}(\xi)}

with
0<i<k
.
By adjunction this is equivalent to solving lifting problems of the form:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Lambda^{i}[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}

Then by taking pullbacks we can reduce to the case that
{B}=\|\Delta[k]\|
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Lambda^{i}[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\tau}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
id

(3.2)

When
\tau(k)
is singular, then
\tau
factors through
\textup{sing}({X})
,
and we get a unique lift by Lemma
3.2.1.9
.
Now suppose instead that
\tau(k)
is regular.
There must exist singular points
s_{0},s_{1}\in{X}
with
\xi(s_{0})=\xi(s_{1})=k

which are adjacent to the stratum of
\tau(k)
from above and below.
By Lemma
3.2.1.9
we then get unique lifts

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\{k\}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces s_{0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
id
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma_{0}}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\{k\}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces s_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
id
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma_{1}}

We have
\sigma_{0}(x)\leq\tau(x)\leq\sigma_{1}(x)
for all
x\in\|\Lambda^{i}[k]\|

in the fibrewise ordering.
By cutting off the strata below
\sigma_{0}
and above
\sigma_{1}

followed by rescaling,
we can reduce to the case that
\operatorname{U}({X})={[0,1]}\times{|\Delta[k]|}

and that
{X}
has a single regular stratum over
k\in\|\Delta[k]\|
.
But then the closure of that stratum must be the entirety of
{X}
.
We can therefore safely provide the filler for (
3.2
) by linear interpolation.

To see that
\textup{Exit}(\xi)
is a categorical fibration it now remains to show that
it is an isofibration.
This followed from
\xi
being a stratified fibration by using local trivialisations over any stratum of
{B}
.
∎

Lemma 3.2.1.21
.

Let
\xi:{X}\to{B}
be a
1
-framed stratified bundle
that satisfies:

(1)

\xi
is a stratified fibre bundle.

(2)

For every
b\in{B}
the fibre
\xi^{-1}(b)
is a closed
1
-mesh.

(3)

\textup{Exit}(\xi)
is an inner fibration.

Then
\xi
is a closed
1
-mesh bundle.

Proof.

Suppose for the purpose of contradiction that
\textup{sing}({X})
is not closed.
Then there must exist an exit path
\gamma_{12}:\|\Delta[1]\|\to{X}

such that
x_{1}:=\gamma_{12}(0)
is regular and
x_{2}:=\gamma_{12}(1)
is singular.
Since
x_{1}
is regular there must be another point
x_{0}\in{X}

in the same stratum as
x_{1}
so that
\xi(x_{1})=\xi(x_{0})
but
x_{1}\neq x_{0}
.
We pick a path
\gamma_{01}:\|\Delta[1]\|\to{X}
from
x_{0}
and
x_{1}

within the fibre
\xi^{-1}(\xi(x_{1}))
.
Then
\gamma_{01}
and
\gamma_{12}
together define a stratified horn

\gamma:\|\Lambda^{1}[2]\|\to{X}
.
Since
\xi\circ\gamma_{01}
is constant, the horn
\xi\circ\gamma
extends
to a stratified
2
-simplex
\sigma:\|\Delta[2]\|\to{B}
such that

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[2]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[1]\|}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\langle 0,1\rangle}_{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi\circ\gamma_{01}}

By assumption (3), we then have a lift

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Lambda^{1}[2]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[2]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\gamma}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\hat{\gamma}}

Since
\hat{\gamma}(2)=\gamma(2)
is singular,
we have that the paths

\hat{\gamma}\circ\langle 0,2\rangle_{*}

and

\hat{\gamma}\circ\langle 1,2\rangle_{*}

agree on
\|\Delta[1]\|\setminus\{0\}
.
But then by continuity we must have

x_{0}=\hat{\gamma}(0)=(\hat{\gamma}\circ\langle 0,2\rangle_{*})(0)=(\hat{\gamma}\circ\langle 1,2\rangle_{*})(0)=\hat{\gamma}(1)=x_{1}

This contradicts our choice of
x_{0}\neq x_{1}
.
∎

Lemma 3.2.1.22
.

Let
\xi:{X}\to{B}
be a closed
1
-mesh bundle.
Then the induced map

\textup{Exit}(\xi):\textup{Exit}({X})\longrightarrow\textup{Exit}({B})

is a flat categorical fibration.

Proof.

The map is a categorical fibration by Lemma
3.2.1.20
.
To show that
\textup{Exit}(\xi)
is also flat,
we demonstrate that for every
2
-simplex

\sigma:\Delta[2]\to\textup{Exit}({B})

the map

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Fun}_{/\textup{Exit}({B})}(\Delta[2],\textup{Exit}({E}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Fun}_{/\textup{Exit}({B})}(\Delta[1],\textup{Exit}({E}))}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\langle 0,2\rangle}^{*}}

(3.3)

has weakly contractible fibres
over any
\tau:\Delta[1]\to\textup{Exit}({E})
such that

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[1]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({E})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[2]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\tau}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\langle 0,2\rangle}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma}

Without loss of generality we can simplify to the situation where

{B}
is the stratified
2
-simplex
\|\Delta[2]\|
.
Then
\tau
corresponds to a partial section
s:\|\Delta[1]\|\to{X}

which fits into the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[1]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[2]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[2]\|}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\langle 0,2\rangle}_{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces s}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
id

When
F
denotes the fibre of (
3.3
) over
\tau
,
a
k
-simplex of
F

is a stratified map
h:\|\Delta[k]\|\times\|\Delta[2]\|\to{X}
such that
the following diagram commutes:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|\times\|\Delta[1]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|\times\|\Delta[2]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[2]\|}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{id}\times\langle 0,2\rangle}_{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces s\circ\pi_{2}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{2}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces h}

Here
\pi_{2}
is the projection onto the second factor.

Suppose first that
s(2)\in{X}
is a singular point.
Then
s:\|\Delta[1]\|\to{X}
must factor through
\textup{sing}({X})

and so by Lemma
3.2.1.9

the simplicial set
F
must have a unique
k
-simplex for every
k\geq 0
.
It is therefore contractible.

Suppose now that
s(2)\in{X}
is a regular point.
Let
x_{0}\in\xi^{-1}(0)
be the highest singular point such that
x_{0}\leq s(2)

in the fibrewise ordering. Similarly, let
x_{1}\in\xi^{-1}(2)
be the lowest
singular point with
s(2)\leq x_{1}
.
By Lemma
3.2.1.9
there are unique lifts

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[0]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{sing}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[2]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[2]\|}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces x_{0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\langle 2\rangle}
id
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\tau_{0}}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[0]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{sing}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[2]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[2]\|}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces x_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\langle 2\rangle}
id
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\tau_{1}}

By restricting
{X}
to the points between
\tau_{0}
and
\tau_{1}

and rescaling, we can simplify to the case that
\operatorname{U}({X})={[0,1]}\times{|\Delta[2]|}
and
{X}
has exactly one regular stratum over
2\in\|\Delta[2]\|
.
Let
{E}
be the subspace of
{X}
consisting of those points

x\in{X}
such that there exists a map
\gamma:\|\Delta[1]\|\to{X}

which fits into the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[0]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[1]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[2]\|}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces x}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\langle 2\rangle}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\langle 1,2\rangle}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\gamma}

Then there is a map
F\to\textup{Exit}({E})
which sends a
k
-simplex

h:\|\Delta[k]\|\times\|\Delta[2]\|\to{X}
to the restriction

h(-,1):\|\Delta[k]\|\to{E}
.
We see that this map is an equivalence and
{E}
is a stratified interval.
It follows that
F
is weakly contractible.
∎

3.2.2
Closed
n
-Meshes

Definition 3.2.2.1
.

A
closed
n
-mesh bundle
is an
n
-framed stratified bundle

\xi:{X}_{n}\to{X}_{0}
such that
\xi
is the composite
of a sequence of closed
1
-mesh bundles

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{n-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cdots}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{0}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi_{n}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi_{1}}

(3.4)

and
\xi
is equipped with the composite
n
-framing.

Observation 3.2.2.2
.

When we have a closed
n
-mesh bundle
\xi:{X}_{n}\to{X}_{0}

arising as the composite of a sequence of closed
1
-mesh bundles (
3.4
),
we can uniquely recover that sequence from
\xi
.
For any
0\leq i\leq n
the stratified space

{X}_{i}
is the quotient of
{X}_{n}
which identifies two points
when their last
i
coordinates in the framing agree.

Construction 3.2.2.3
.

Let
\xi:{X}_{n}\to{X}_{0}
be a closed
n
-mesh bundle
that decomposes into a sequence of closed
1
-mesh bundles

\xi=\xi_{n}\circ\cdots\circ\xi_{1}
.
Whenever
0\leq m\leq n
, we define the
m
-truncation
of
\xi
to
be the closed
m
-mesh bundle
\xi_{m}\circ\cdots\circ\xi_{1}
.

Lemma 3.2.2.4
.

Let
\xi:{X}\to{B}
be a closed
n
-mesh bundle. Then the induced map

\textup{Exit}(\xi):\textup{Exit}({X})\longrightarrow\textup{Exit}({B})

is a flat categorical fibration.
In particular when
{B}
is a fibrant stratified space,
then so is
{X}
.

Proof.

We write
\xi
as the composite of closed
1
-mesh bundles

\xi=\xi_{n}\circ\cdots\circ\xi_{1}
.
Then
\textup{Exit}(\xi)
is the composite of the induced maps

\textup{Exit}(\xi_{n})\circ\cdots\circ\textup{Exit}(\xi_{1})

which are flat categorical fibrations by Lemma
3.2.1.22
.
Therefore
\textup{Exit}(\xi)
is again a flat categorical fibration.
∎

Lemma 3.2.2.5
.

Closed
n
-mesh bundles are closed under pullback.

Proof.

Let
\xi:{X}\to{B}
be a closed
n
-mesh bundle and let

f:{A}\to{B}
be a map of stratified spaces.
We can write
\xi
as the composite of closed
1
-mesh bundles

\xi_{i}:{X}_{i}\to{X}_{i-1}
for
1\leq i\leq n
.
In particular
{X}_{n}={X}
and
{X}_{0}={B}
.
Then the pullback of
\xi
along
f
decomposes into a sequence of
pullbacks of closed
1
-mesh bundles

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}={Y}_{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}_{n-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cdots}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}_{0}={A}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}={X}_{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{n-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cdots}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{0}={B}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta_{n}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta_{1}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi_{n}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi_{1}}

By Lemma
3.2.1.8
closed
1
-mesh bundles are
closed under pullback.
Therefore, the pullback of
\xi
along
f
is the closed
n
-mesh bundle

\zeta_{1}\circ\cdots\circ\zeta_{n}
.
∎

Definition 3.2.2.6
.

We let
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
be the simplicial set whose
k
-simplices consist of a
closed
n
-mesh bundle
\xi:{X}\to\|\Delta[k]\|
.
An order-preserving map
[k^{\prime}]\to[k]
acts by pullback along the
induced map
\|\Delta[k^{\prime}]\|\to\|\Delta[k]\|
.
Truncation of closed
(n+1)
-mesh bundles defines a map of simplicial sets

\operatorname{tr}_{n}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n+1}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.

Observation 3.2.2.7
.

In the case that
n=0
,
a
k
-simplex of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{0}
is a closed
0
-mesh bundle

\xi:{X}\to\|\Delta[k]\|
.
This means that
\xi
is the composite of a length zero sequence of
1
-mesh bundles,
and so
\xi
is the identity on
\|\Delta[k]\|
.
It therefore follows that
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{0}\cong*
is the terminal object
in
sSet
.

Lemma 3.2.2.8
.

The truncation map
\operatorname{tr}_{n}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n+1}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is an inner fibration.
In particular
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is a quasicategory for each
n\geq 0
.

Proof.

Suppose we have a lifting problem

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Lambda^{i}[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n+1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{tr}_{n}}

for some
0<i<k
.
Unpacking the definitions, we then have a diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Lambda^{i}[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta^{\prime}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta}

where
\xi
is a closed
1
-mesh bundle and
\zeta
,
\zeta^{\prime}
are closed
n
-mesh bundles.
By Corollary
3.2.1.19
we have that
{Y}
is triangulable.
The pullback square of stratified spaces induces a pullback square of simplicial sets

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({Y}^{\prime})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({Y})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}(\|\Lambda^{i}[k]\|)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}(\|\Delta[k]\|)}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Exit}(\zeta^{\prime})}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Exit}(\zeta)}

By Lemma
3.2.2.4
the map
\textup{Exit}(\zeta)
is a flat categorical fibration.
Since
\|\Delta[k]\|
is fibrant and the stratified inner horn inclusion
is a stratified weak equivalence, it follows by Lemma
2.2.3.2
that
the inclusion
{Y}^{\prime}\hookrightarrow{Y}
is a stratified weak equivalence.
Since
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
is a quasicategory, we can therefore find an extension

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({Y}^{\prime})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({Y})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi^{\prime}\rrbracket}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi}

Then by Proposition
3.2.1.17

there exists a closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi:{X}\to{Y}

so that
\xi
restricts to
\xi^{\prime}
along the inclusion
{Y}^{\prime}\to{Y}
.
The composite
\zeta\circ\xi
is a closed
(n+1)
-mesh bundle over

\|\Delta[k]\|
that represents a solution to the lifting problem.
∎

Construction 3.2.2.9
.

Suppose that
\xi:{X}_{n}\to{X}_{0}
is a closed
n
-mesh bundle.
Then for every stratified
k
-simplex
\sigma:\|\Delta[k]\|\to{X}_{0}

we have a closed
n
-mesh bundle
\sigma^{*}\xi
over
\|\Delta[k]\|
by pullback of
\xi
along
\sigma
.
This defines the
classifying map

{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}:\textup{Exit}({X}_{0})\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.

Lemma 3.2.2.10
.

Let
S
be a marked poset and
\varphi:S\to(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n})^{\natural}

a map of marked simplicial sets.
Then there exists a unique closed
n
-mesh bundle

\xi
over
\|S\|^{+}

such that the following diagram commutes:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{S}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n})^{\natural}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}^{+}(\|S\|^{+})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}}

Proof.

By induction assume that the claim holds for some
n\geq 0
.
Let
S
be a marked poset and
\varphi:S\to(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n+1})^{\natural}

a map of marked simplicial sets.
By truncation the map
\varphi
induces a map
\psi:S\to(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n})^{\natural}
.
Then by induction there exists a unique closed
n
-mesh bundle

\zeta:{Y}\to\|S\|^{+}
such that
{\llbracket\zeta\rrbracket}

fits into the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{S}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n})^{\natural}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}^{+}(\|S\|^{+})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\zeta\rrbracket}}

For every marked flag
\sigma
in
S
the map
\varphi
holds a closed
n
-mesh
bundle
\zeta_{\sigma}
and a closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi_{\sigma}

which together with
\zeta
fit into the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{\sigma}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}_{\sigma}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|({|\Delta[k]|},T)\|^{+}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|S\|^{+}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi_{\sigma}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta_{\sigma}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma}

The stratified space
{Y}_{\sigma}
is a closed triangulable subspace
of
{Y}
and the family of these subspaces for all marked flags
\sigma
of
S

covers
{Y}
.
Using Lemma
3.2.1.16
we may therefore glue together the closed
1
-mesh bundles
to obtain a closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi:{X}\to{Y}
.
Then for each
\sigma
the composite
\zeta\circ\xi
restricts to the
closed
(n+1)
-mesh bundle
\zeta_{\sigma}\circ\xi_{\sigma}
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{\sigma}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}_{\sigma}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|({|\Delta[k]|},T)\|^{+}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|S\|^{+}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi_{\sigma}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta_{\sigma}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma}

It follows that
\zeta\circ\xi
is the unique closed
(n+1)
-mesh bundle
induced by
\varphi
.
∎

Proposition 3.2.2.11
.

Let
{B}
be a triangulable stratified space and

I:{A}\hookrightarrow{B}

a closed triangulable stratified subspace.
Suppose that
\varphi:\textup{Exit}({B})\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is a map
and
\xi^{\prime}
a closed
n
-mesh bundle over
{A}
such that

{\llbracket\xi^{\prime}\rrbracket}=\varphi\circ I
.
Then there is a closed
n
-mesh bundle
\xi
over
{B}
together
with an equivalence

\varphi\simeq{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}

relative to
{\llbracket\xi^{\prime}\rrbracket}
.

Proof.

Analogous to the proof of Proposition
3.2.1.17

by using Lemma
3.2.1.16
.
∎

3.2.3
Closed
n
-Meshes with Labels

Suppose that
\xi:{X}\to{B}
is a closed
n
-mesh bundle and
C
a simplicial set.
We say that
\xi
is labelled in
C
when it is equipped with a map of simplicial sets

L:\textup{Exit}({X})\to C
which we will call a
labelling map
.
This notion will be particularly well-behaved when
C=\mathcal{C}
is a quasicategory.

Observation 3.2.3.1
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a
1
-category and
f:E\to B
a map in
\mathcal{C}

together with a section, i.e. a map
s:B\to E
such that
\textup{id}=f\circ s
.
When the pullback of
f
along a map
g:A\to B
exists in
\mathcal{C}
,
then the universal property induces a unique section of the pulled back map

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{E\times_{B}A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{E}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{B}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces s\circ g}
id
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces g}

Definition 3.2.3.2
.

We denote by
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}
the simplicial set
whose
k
-simplices consist of a closed
n
-mesh bundle
\xi:{X}\to\|\Delta[k]\|

together with a section
s:\|\Delta[k]\|\to{X}
with
\textup{id}=f\circ s
.
An order-preserving map
[k^{\prime}]\to[k]
acts by pullback
along the induced map
\|\Delta[k^{\prime}]\|\to\|\Delta[k]\|

which induces a new section as in Observation
3.2.3.1
.
We write
\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{M}}}^{n}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
for the map of simplicial sets
which forgets the section.
The map
\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{M}}}^{n}
induces a polynomial functor

\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(-):\textup{sSet}\to\textup{sSet}
.

Observation 3.2.3.3
.

In Observation
3.2.3.3
we have seen
that
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{0}\cong*
.
A
k
-simplex of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{0}_{*}
is a closed
0
-mesh bundle

\xi:{X}\to\|\Delta[k]\|
together with a section

s:\|\Delta[k]\|\to{X}
.
Because
\xi
is the identity on
\|\Delta[k]\|
,
the section must also be the identity.
Therefore,
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{0}_{*}\cong*
is the terminal object
of
sSet
and
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{0}_{*}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{0}
is the identity on

*
.
It follows that for any simplicial set
C
there is a natural isomorphism
of simplicial sets
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{0}(C)\cong C
.

Lemma 3.2.3.4
.

The map

\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{M}}}^{n}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}

is a categorical fibration.
In particular the simplicial set
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}
is a quasicategory.

Proof.

We first show that the map is an inner fibration.
Suppose we have a lifting problem

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Lambda^{i}[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{M}}}^{n}}

for some
0<i<k
.
The given data corresponds to a closed
n
-mesh bundle
\xi
together with a partial section

s
which fit into the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Lambda^{i}[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces s^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}

Using the
\|-\|\dashv\textup{Exit}
adjunction this corresponds to a diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Lambda^{i}[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}(\|\Delta[k]\|)}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Exit}(\xi)}

By Lemma
3.2.2.4
the map
\textup{Exit}(\xi)
is in particular
an inner fibration, so there is a lift

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Lambda^{i}[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}(\|\Delta[k]\|)}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Exit}(\xi)}

which classifies an extension of the partial section
s^{\prime}
to a full section
of
\xi
.
Then
\xi
together with the full section is a solution to the lifting problem.
We have therefore shown that
\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{M}}}^{n}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is an inner fibration. It follows similarly that
\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{M}}}^{n}
is an isofibration.
∎

Lemma 3.2.3.5
.

Let
\xi:{X}\to{B}
be a closed
n
-mesh bundle.
Then there is a pullback square

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Exit}(\xi)}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{M}}}^{n}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}}

(3.5)

of simplicial sets.
In particular, when
{B}
is a fibrant stratified space,
the pullback square is a homotopy pullback of quasicategories.

Proof.

We begin by describing the map
\textup{Exit}({X})\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}
explicitly.
A
k
-simplex of
\textup{Exit}({X})
is a stratified
k
-simplex
\sigma:\|\Delta[k]\|\to{X}
.
We need to send
\sigma
to a
k
-simplex of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}
, representing a closed
n
-mesh bundle over
\|\Delta[k]\|
together with a section.
To make the square (
3.5
) commute,
this closed
n
-mesh bundle needs to be the pullback

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}\times_{\|\Delta[k]\|}{B}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}\times_{{B}}{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces(\xi\circ\sigma)^{*}\xi}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi^{*}\xi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}

Via the universal property of the pullback the map
\sigma:\|\Delta[k]\|\to{X}
induces a section of
(\xi\circ\sigma)^{*}\xi
and therefore a
k
-simplex of

\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}
as needed.

It remains to show that the square (
3.5
) is a
pullback square of simplicial sets.
A
k
-simplex of
\textup{Exit}({B})\times_{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}

consists of a diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|\times_{{B}}{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi^{*}\sigma}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces s}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma}

(3.6)

The induced map

\textup{Exit}({B})\times_{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}\to\textup{Exit}({X})

sends the diagram (
3.6
) to the stratified
k
-simplex

\xi^{*}\sigma\circ s:\|\Delta[k]\|\to{X}
.
Conversely, by the universal property of the pullback of stratified spaces in (
3.6
),
the stratified
k
-simplex of
{X}
uniquely determines the section
s
.
Therefore, the square (
3.5
) is a pullback square of simplicial sets.
∎

Construction 3.2.3.6
.

Let
\xi:{X}\to{B}
be a closed
n
-mesh bundle together
with a labelling map
\ell:\textup{Exit}({X})\to C
for some simplicial set
C
.
For any stratified
k
-simplex
\sigma:\|\Delta[k]\|\to{B}

we have an induced diagram of simplicial sets

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{E}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X}_{\sigma})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}(\|\Delta[k]\|)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Exit}(\sigma^{*}\xi)}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Exit}(\xi)}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}}

Then
{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}
together with the composite

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{E}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X}_{\sigma})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{C}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\ell}

determine a
k
-simplex of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(C)
.
This defines the
classifying map

{\llbracket\xi;\ell\rrbracket}:\textup{Exit}({B})\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(C)
and is compatible with
the unlabelled case by making the following diagram commute:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(C)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi;\ell\rrbracket}}

Lemma 3.2.3.7
.

The forgetful map

\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{M}}}^{n}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}

is a flat categorical fibration.

Proof.

The map
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is already a categorical fibration by
Lemma
3.2.3.4
.
The map is flat if for every
2
-simplex

\sigma:\Delta[2]\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
the pulled back map

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[2]\times_{\textup{M}^{n}}\textup{M}^{n}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{M}^{n}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[2]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{M}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathfrak{M}^{n}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma}

(3.7)

is flat.
The
2
-simplex
\sigma
determines a closed
n
-mesh bundle

\xi:{X}\to\|\Delta[2]\|
by the definition of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.
Using Lemma
3.2.3.5
the square
(
3.7
) factors as the composite
of the pullback squares

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[2]\times_{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[2]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}(\|\Delta[2]\|)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Exit}(\xi)}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathfrak{M}^{n}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}}

By Lemma
3.2.1.22
the map
\textup{Exit}(\xi)
is a flat categorical fibration.
Because
\varphi
is the pullback of
\textup{Exit}(\xi)
, it follows that it is a flat categorical fibration as well.
∎

Proposition 3.2.3.8
.

The functor
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(-):\textup{sSet}\to\textup{sSet}
satisfies the following properties:

1.

\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})\to\textup{M}^{n}
is a categorical fibration when
\mathcal{C}
is a quasicategory.

2.

\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(-)
preserves quasicategories.

3.

\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(-)
preserves categorical equivalences between quasicategories.

Proof.

By Lemma
3.2.3.7
the map

\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is a flat categorical fibration.
Therefore, the claims follow by Proposition
2.2.3.4
.
∎

Proposition 3.2.3.9
.

Let
{B}
be a triangulable stratified space and

I:{A}\hookrightarrow{B}

a closed triangulable stratified subspace.
Let
\mathcal{C}
be a quasicategory.
Suppose that
\varphi:\textup{Exit}({B})\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})

is a map and
\xi^{\prime}:{X}^{\prime}\to{A}
a closed
n
-mesh bundle
with a labelling map
\ell^{\prime}:\textup{Exit}({X}^{\prime})\to\mathcal{C}

such that
{\llbracket\xi^{\prime};\ell^{\prime}\rrbracket}=\varphi\circ\textup{Exit}(I)
.
Then there is a closed
n
-mesh bundle
\xi:{X}\to{B}

with a labelling map
\ell:\textup{Exit}({X})\to\mathcal{C}

together with an equivalence

\varphi\simeq{\llbracket\xi;\ell\rrbracket}

relative to
{\llbracket\xi^{\prime};\ell^{\prime}\rrbracket}
.

Proof.

By restriction along the map that forgets the labelling,
we obtain a map
\psi
which together with the other given data fits into the diagram:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({A})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({A})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi^{\prime};\ell^{\prime}\rrbracket}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi^{\prime}\rrbracket}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi}

The closed
n
-mesh bundle
\xi^{\prime}
together with the map
\psi

satisfy the conditions of Proposition
3.2.2.11
,
and so we obtain a closed
n
-mesh bundle
\xi:{X}\to{B}

together with an equivalence
h:\psi\simeq{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}
relative to

{\llbracket\xi^{\prime}\rrbracket}
.
Because
\mathcal{C}
is a quasicategory,
by Proposition
3.2.3.8
the forgetful map

\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})
is a categorical
fibration.
Therefore we can lift the equivalence
h
to an equivalence

\varphi\simeq{\llbracket\xi;\ell\rrbracket}
relative to
{\llbracket\xi^{\prime};\ell^{\prime}\rrbracket}

where
\ell:\textup{Exit}({X})\to\mathcal{C}
is a labelling functor for

\xi
.
∎

3.2.4

n
-Meshes

Construction 3.2.4.1
.

We construct a

Then the classifying maps

and

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}}}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{E}}}

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
