\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Exit}(\zeta)}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{M}}}^{n}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\zeta\rrbracket}}

This diagram then determines a
k
-simplex of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})
.

Observation 3.2.4.2
.

Let
\xi:{X}\to{Y}
be a closed
1
-mesh bundle and

\zeta:{Y}\to{B}
a closed
n
-mesh bundle. Then the packing map
sends the classifying map of the composite closed
(n+1)
-mesh bundle
{\llbracket\zeta\circ\xi\rrbracket}:\textup{Exit}({B})\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n+1}

to the classifying map
{\llbracket\zeta;{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}\rrbracket}
.

Lemma 3.2.4.3
.

The packing map

\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n+1}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})

is a categorical equivalence.

Proof.

Suppose we have a lifting problem of the form

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n+1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})}}

(3.8)

Unpacking the definitions, we are given closed
n
-mesh bundles
\zeta
,
\zeta^{\prime}
and a closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi^{\prime}
which together fit into the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{X_{n+1}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{X_{n}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{X_{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial\|\Delta[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta^{\prime}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta}

We have pullback squares

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{E}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X}_{n}^{\prime})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}(\partial\|\Delta[k]\|)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\zeta^{\prime}\rrbracket}}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{E}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X}_{n})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}(\|\Delta[k]\|)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\zeta\rrbracket}}

By Lemma
3.2.3.7
the map
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}

is a flat categorical fibration.
Since the inclusions
\partial\Delta[k]\hookrightarrow\textup{Exit}(\partial\|\Delta[k]\|)

and
\Delta[k]\to\textup{Exit}(\|\Delta[k]\|)
are categorical equivalences,
it then follows by Lemma
2.2.3.2
that the
inclusions

\mathcal{E}^{\prime}\hookrightarrow\textup{Exit}({X}_{n}^{\prime})
and

\mathcal{E}\hookrightarrow\textup{Exit}({X}_{n})
are categorical equivalences as well.
We have a labelling functor
\ell:\mathcal{E}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
which fits
into the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{E}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{E}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X}^{\prime})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\ell}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi^{\prime}\rrbracket}}

Since
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
is a quasicategory, we can then find a lift

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X}^{\prime})\sqcup_{\mathcal{E}^{\prime}}\mathcal{E}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi}

By Corollary
3.2.1.19
we have that
{X}_{n}
is triangulable and

{X}_{n}^{\prime}\subseteq{X}_{n}
a closed subspace.
Then by Proposition
3.2.1.17

we can find a closed
1
-mesh bundle

\xi:{X}_{n+1}\to{X}_{n}
extending
\xi^{\prime}
such that

{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}\simeq\varphi
while preserving the restriction

{\llbracket\xi^{\prime}\rrbracket}
.
Then the closed
(n+1)
-mesh bundle
\zeta\circ\xi
determines a lift

\Delta[k]\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n+1}
which makes the upper left
triangle of the lifting problem
3.8
commute.
The lower right triangle commutes up to homotopy given by the path
{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}\simeq\varphi
.
∎

Corollary 3.2.4.4
.

The packing map
\operatorname{pack}_{n}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n+1}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})

is a split monomorphism.

Proof.

The map
\operatorname{pack}_{n}
is a categorical equivalence and a cofibration,
and
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n+1}
is a quasicategory. Therefore there exists a lift in the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n+1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n+1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})}}
id
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{pack}_{n}}

and therefore a retraction for
\operatorname{pack}_{n}
.
∎

Proposition 3.2.4.5
.

For every quasicategory
\mathcal{C}
there is a categorical equivalence

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n+1}(\mathcal{C})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}(\mathcal{C}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n+1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{pack}_{n}}

Proof.

Let us write
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})
for the simplicial set obtained by the pullback

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}

The packing map fits into a pullback square

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n+1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})\times_{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}}\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n+1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}

(3.9)

which can be verified by unrolling the definitions.
Then via Construction
2.2.1.2

the pullback square (
3.9
)
induces a map between the induced polynomial functors.
By Lemma
2.2.2.4
the polynomial functor
induced by the map on the right of (
3.9
) is
the composite
\textup{M}^{n}(\textup{M}^{1}(-))
.
Then by Lemma
2.2.3.5
the map is a categorical equivalence.
∎

Corollary 3.2.4.6
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a quasicategory. Then there is an equivalence

\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})\simeq\underbrace{(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}\circ\cdots\circ\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})}_{\textup{$n$ times}}(\mathcal{C})

3.2.5
Open Meshes

Open meshes are the dual of closed meshes, both geometrically and algebraically.
Where closed meshes model stratifications that are generalised pasting diagrams,
open meshes represent generalised string diagrams.

Definition 3.2.5.1
.

An
open
1
-mesh

{M}
is a finite stratification of
\mathbb{R}
whose strata are
either
singular
, consisting of just a point,
or
regular
, consisting of an open interval.
A point in
{M}
is singular or regular if it is contained in a stratum that is
singular or regular, respectively.

Definition 3.2.5.2
.

An
open
1
-mesh bundle
is a
1
-framed
stratified bundle
f:{M}\to{B}

that satisfies the following conditions:

1.

f
is a stratified fibre bundle.

2.

For every
b\in{B}
the fibre
f^{-1}(b)
is an open
1
-mesh.

3.

The regular points in all fibres form an open subset of
{M}
.

Construction 3.2.5.3
.

We pick any continuous and order-preserving isomorphism between the open interval

{(-1,-1)}
and
\mathbb{R}
,
for instance
x\mapsto\tan(\tfrac{\pi}{2}x)
or any piecewise linear approximation of that map.
From this isomorphism we can derive an induced embedding
\mathbb{R}\hookrightarrow{[-1,1]}
whose
image consists of the open interval
{(-1,1)}\subseteq{[-1,1]}
.
Suppose that
f:{M}\to{B}
is an open
1
-mesh bundle.
Then there exists a closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi:{X}\to{B}
such that

\operatorname{U}(\xi)
is the projection
{[-1,1]}\times\operatorname{U}({B})\to\operatorname{U}({B})
,
and we have a pullback square of stratified spaces

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathbb{R}\times\operatorname{U}({B})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{[-1,1]}\times\operatorname{U}({B})}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}

We call
\xi
the
compactification
of
f
.
Any different choice of continuous order-preserving isomorphism
{(-1,1)}\cong\mathbb{R}

yields a compactification that is framed isomorphic.

We use the compactification of open
1
-mesh bundles to transfer most of
the theory of closed meshes to open meshes.

Lemma 3.2.5.4
.

Let
f:{M}\to{B}
be an open
1
-mesh bundle.
Then the induced map
\textup{Exit}(f)
is a flat categorical fibration.

Proof.

When
\xi:{X}\to{B}
is the compactification of
f

we have constructible embedding
i:{M}\hookrightarrow{X}
,
and so
\textup{Exit}(i)
must be a categorical fibration.
To see that
\textup{Exit}(i)
is also flat, we consider a diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[1]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({M})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[2]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\langle 0,2\rangle}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Exit}(i)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma}

There are no exit paths in
{X}
which start in
{M}
but end in the
boundary
{X}\setminus{M}
.
Therefore
\sigma(0)\in{X}
being in
{M}
implies that also

\sigma(1)
is in
{M}
.
Since
{M}
is a constructible subspace of
{X}
,
the stratified
2
-simplex
\sigma
must then factor uniquely through
{M}
.
Hence,
\textup{Exit}(i)
is flat.
The induced map
\textup{Exit}(\xi)
is a flat categorical fibration by Lemma
3.2.1.22
, and so
the composite
\textup{Exit}(f)=\textup{Exit}(\xi)\circ\textup{Exit}(i)
is a flat categorical fibration as well.
∎

Definition 3.2.5.5
.

We denote by
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}
the simplicial set whose
k
-simplices are
the open
1
-mesh bundles
f:{M}\to\|\Delta[k]\|
.
An order-preserving map
[k^{\prime}]\to[k]
acts by pullback along the induced
map
\|\Delta[k^{\prime}]\|\to\|\Delta[k]\|
.
Compactification of open
1
-mesh bundles defines a map of simplicial sets

\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
.

Definition 3.2.5.6
.

The category
\nabla
of
strict intervals
is the subcategory of

\Delta
whose objects are finite ordinals
[n]
with
n>0
and whose maps
are order-preserving maps
\alpha:[n]\to[m]
that are endpoint preserving,
i.e. satisfy
\alpha(0)=0
and
\alpha(n)=m
.

Construction 3.2.5.7
.

We let
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{\textup{cb}}
be the simplicial subset of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}

of
continuously bounded
closed
1
-meshes, defined by the pullback
of simplicial sets

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{\textup{cb}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\nabla^{\textup{op}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{\textup{op}}}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
sing

The induced map
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{\textup{cb}}\to\nabla^{\textup{op}}
is again a trivial fibration and
so
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{\textup{cb}}
is a quasicategory.
The compactification map
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
factors through
the inclusion
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{\textup{cb}}\hookrightarrow\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
.

Lemma 3.2.5.8
.

The compactification map
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{\textup{cb}}
is a split monomorphism.
In particular
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}
is a retract of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{\textup{cb}}
and therefore quasicategory.

Proof.

We define the retraction
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{\textup{cb}}\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}
as follows:
Given a continuously bounded closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi:{X}\to\|\Delta[k]\|
,
we perform the following three steps:

1.

Linearly rescale the framing to be fibrewise supported on the closed interval
{[-1,1]}
.

2.

Remove the first and last singular stratum in each fibre.

3.

Rescale using the chosen continuous order-preserving isomorphism
{(-1,1)}\cong\mathbb{R}
.

The result is an open
1
-mesh bundle over
\|\Delta[k]\|
and therefore a
k
-simplex of
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}
.

When we start with an open
1
-mesh bundle and compactify, the resulting closed
1
-mesh bundle is already supported on
{[-1,1]}
in each fibre and so the rescaling does not affect it.
We then remove the strata that compactification has added, and undo the rescaling from
\mathbb{R}
to
{(-1,1)}
performed by compactification. Therefore, we end up with the open
1
-mesh bundle that we started with.
∎

Lemma 3.2.5.9
.

Let
f:{M}\to{B}
be an open
1
-mesh bundle.
Then the restriction

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}(\textup{reg}({M}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({M})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Exit}(f)}

is a left fibration.

Proof.

By Lemma
3.2.5.4

we have that
\textup{Exit}(f)
is a categorical fibration.
Because
\textup{reg}({M})
is a constructible subspace of
{M}
,
the inclusion map induces a categorical fibration
\textup{Exit}(\textup{reg}({M}))\to\textup{Exit}({M})
.
Therefore, the composite

\textup{Exit}(\textup{reg}({M}))\to\textup{Exit}({B})

is a categorical fibration as well.

Via the framing we interpret
\operatorname{U}({M})
as an open subspace of
\mathbb{R}\times\operatorname{U}({B})
and
\operatorname{U}(f)
as the projection.
Let
\gamma:\|\Delta[1]\|\to{B}
be an exit path and
(h,b)\in{M}
a regular point with
f(h,b)=b=\gamma(0)
.
The subspace
\textup{reg}({M})
of regular points is open in
{M}
,
and so it follows that there exists an
\varepsilon>0
so that the map
\hat{\gamma}:\|\Delta[1]^{\textup{op}}\|\cap{[0,\varepsilon)}\to{M}
defined by
\hat{\gamma}(t)=(h,\gamma(t))
is a well-defined stratified map.
Then via the trivialisation of
f
over the stratum of
{B}
containing
\gamma(1)
, we can extend
\hat{\gamma}
to a lift
\hat{\gamma}:\|\Delta[1]\|\to{M}
of
\gamma
starting at
(b,h)
.
The space of such lifts is contractible since they necessarily all land within the same regular stratum.
Therefore, it follows that
\textup{Exit}(\textup{reg}({M}))\to\textup{Exit}({B})
is a left fibration.
∎

Construction 3.2.5.10
.

Suppose that
f:{M}\to{B}
is an open
1
-mesh bundle,
then by Lemma
3.2.5.9
there is a diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}(\textup{reg}({M}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{S}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
S

where
\textup{S}_{*}
is the
\infty
-category of pointed spaces.
The map
\textup{Exit}({B})\to\textup{S}
sends a point
b\in{B}
to the
subspace of regular points in the fibre
f^{-1}(b)
.
Using the functor
\pi_{0}:\textup{S}\to\textup{Set}
which sends a space to the set of its connected components, we then get a diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}(\textup{reg}({M}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Set}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
Set

The number of regular strata over any point
b\in{B}
is finite but never zero,
and the regular strata in
f^{-1}(b)
inherit an ordering from the
1
-framing of
f
.
Therefore, we obtain an induced diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}(\textup{reg}({M}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{reg}(f)}

Observation 3.2.5.11
.

For any finite non-empty ordinal
[n]
we can equip the set of order-preserving
maps
[n]\to[1]
with the pointwise order; the result is a finite total
order with at least two elements.
An order-preserving map
[n]\to[m]
acts upon a map
[m]\to[1]

by precomposition, preserving the pointwise order as well as the maximum and minimum element.
This defines a functor
\Delta\to\nabla^{\textup{op}}
which moreover is an isomorphism.

Example 3.2.5.12
.

We can interpret the functor
\Delta\to\nabla^{\textup{op}}
as sending an ordinal
[n]

to the totally ordered set of gaps in between the elements of
[n]
, including a gap at the beginning and end.
For example, the functor sends
[3]
to the ordinal
[4]
:

0
1
2
3
0
1
2
3
4

Lemma 3.2.5.13
.

The map
\textup{reg}:\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}\to\Delta
fits into the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{\textup{cb}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\nabla^{\textup{op}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{\textup{op}}}}
reg
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{sing}^{\textup{op}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}

In particular the map
\textup{reg}:\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}\to\Delta
is a retract of the map

\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{\textup{cb}}\to\nabla^{\textup{op}}
and therefore a trivial fibration.

Proof.

Suppose that
f:{M}\to\|\Delta[k]\|
is an open
1
-mesh bundle
and
\xi:{X}\to\|\Delta[k]\|
the compactification of
f
.
Let
i\in[k]
then
\textup{sing}(\xi)(i)
is the set of singular strata of

\xi
over
i\in\|\Delta[k]\|
, ordered via the framing.
Since the regular strata of
\xi
correspond exactly to the regular strata of

f
, we have that
\textup{reg}(f)(i)
classifies the set of regular strata of
\xi

over
i\in\|\Delta[k]\|
ordered via the framing.

For every singular stratum
s\in\textup{sing}(\xi)(i)
we have an order-preserving
map
\alpha^{i}_{s}:\textup{reg}(f)(i)\to[1]
which sends a regular stratum to

0
exactly when it is below the singular stratum
s
in the fibrewise ordering.
The assignment
s\mapsto\alpha^{i}_{s}
is an order-preserving isomorphism between

\textup{sing}(\xi)(i)
and the poset of order-preserving maps
\textup{reg}(f)(i)\to[1]
.

Any section of
\xi
which only intersects singular strata cuts
{X}

into two parts, above and below the section.
Together with the previous observation, it follows that the duality isomorphism

\Delta\cong\nabla^{\textup{op}}
sends
\textup{reg}(f)
to
\textup{sing}(\xi)
.
∎

Observation 3.2.5.14
.

We have a span of equivalences

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})^{\textup{op}}}}
reg
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{sing}^{\textup{op}}}

which induces an equivalence between
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}

and the opposite
(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})^{\textup{op}}
.
This equivalence implements a form of Poincaré duality between open and closed
1
-meshes.
We will see that this equivalence extends to higher-dimensional meshes as well.

At this point the rest of the theory of closed meshes transfers entirely analogously.
Instead of individually reproving each step, we summarise the results as follows.

Definition 3.2.5.15
.

An open
n
-mesh bundle is a sequence of open
1
-mesh bundles

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}_{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}_{n-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cdots}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}_{0}}}

(3.10)

We denote by
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
the simplicial set whose
k
-simplices are open

n
-mesh bundles over
\|\Delta[k]\|
.
The
k
-simplices of the simplicial set
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}
are open
n
-mesh bundles
together with a section.
There is a projection map
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
which forgets the section
and a truncation map
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n+1}\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
which cuts off the last
1
-mesh bundle.
We write
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(-)
for the polynomial functor on simplicial sets induced by
the map
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.

Observation 3.2.5.16
.

The truncation map
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n+1}\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is a categorical fibration,
and therefore for all
n\geq 0
the simplicial set
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is a quasicategory.
The forgetful map
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is a flat categorical fibration,
and so the simplicial set
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}
is a quasicategory as well.
For each open
n
-mesh bundle
f:{M}\to{B}
there is a
classifying map
{\llbracket f\rrbracket}:\textup{Exit}({B})\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}

which fits into the pullback square

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({M})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Exit}(f)}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket f\rrbracket}}

Then for every quasicategory
\mathcal{C}
the map

\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is a categorical fibration,
and
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(-)
preserves categorical equivalences between quasicategories.
For any simplicial set
C
there is a packing map

\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n+1}(C)\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}(C))

which is a categorical equivalence when
C=\mathcal{C}
is a quasicategory.

3.2.6
Meshed Grids

The functor
\textup{sing}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
is a trivial fibration
and therefore has a section
\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}:\Delta^{\textup{op}}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}

which sends an ordinal
[i]
to the closed
1
-mesh with
i+1
singular
strata. Similarly, for open meshes, the functor
\textup{reg}:\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}\to\Delta

has an essentially unique section
\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}:\Delta\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}
.
Using the stacked product of framed stratified bundles, defined below, we can
use these sections to obtain the grid mesh functors
\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}:\Delta^{n,\textup{op}}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
and
\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}:\Delta^{n}\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.

Construction 3.2.6.1
.

Suppose that
p_{0}:{E}_{0}\to{B}
is an
n
-framed stratified bundle
and
p_{1}:{E}_{1}\to{B}
is an
m
-framed stratified bundle.
Let
p_{1}^{*}p_{0}:{E}_{0}\times_{{B}}{E}_{1}\to{E}_{1}
be the
n
-framed
stratified bundle defined by the pullback

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}_{0}\times_{{B}}{E}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}_{0}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p_{1}^{*}p_{0}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p_{0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p_{1}}

Then the
stacked product

p_{0}\triangleleft p_{1}
of
p_{0}
and
p_{1}
is the composite

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}_{0}\times_{{B}}{E}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p_{1}^{*}p_{0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p_{1}}

with the composite
(n+m)
-framing.

Lemma 3.2.6.2
.

Let
p_{0}:{E}_{0}\to{B}
be a closed
n
-mesh bundle
and
p_{1}:{E}_{1}\to{B}
a closed
m
-mesh bundle.
Then the stacked product
p_{0}\triangleleft p_{1}
is a closed
(n+m)
-mesh bundle.
Moreover the analogous claim holds for open mesh bundles.

Proof.

By Lemma
3.2.2.5
the pullback

p_{1}^{*}p_{0}
with the induced
n
-framing is again a closed
n
-mesh bundle.
Then the result follows since the framed composite of a closed
n
-mesh bundle
followed by a closed
m
-mesh bundle is a closed
(n+m)
-mesh bundle.
∎

Construction 3.2.6.3
.

Suppose that
\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}:\Delta^{\textup{op}}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
is a section
of the equivalence
\textup{sing}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
.
Then via the stacked product of closed
n
-meshes, we can define
the
closed grid mesh
functor

\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}:\Delta^{n,\textup{op}}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.
A
k
-simplex
\sigma:\Delta[k]\to\Delta^{n,\textup{op}}
of the
n
-fold
product of
\Delta^{\textup{op}}
with itself
consists of a
family of
k
-simplices
\sigma_{i}:\Delta[k]\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
for
all
1\leq i\leq k
.
Then
\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
sends
\sigma
to the closed
n
-mesh bundle
over
\|\Delta[k]\|

obtained as the stacked product

\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{n}):=\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\sigma_{1})\triangleleft\cdots\triangleleft\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\sigma_{n})

Construction 3.2.6.5
.

Suppose that
\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}:\Delta^{\textup{op}}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
is a section
of the equivalence
\textup{reg}:\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}\to\Delta
.
Then via the stacked product of open
n
-meshes, we can define
the
open grid mesh
functor

\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}:\Delta^{n}\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.
A
k
-simplex
\sigma:\Delta[k]\to\Delta^{n}
of the
n
-fold
product of
\Delta
with itself
consists of a
family of
k
-simplices
\sigma_{i}:\Delta[k]\to\Delta
for
all
1\leq i\leq k
.
Then
\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
sends
\sigma
to the open
n
-mesh bundle
over
\|\Delta[k]\|

obtained as the stacked product

\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{n}):=\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\sigma_{1})\triangleleft\cdots\triangleleft\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\sigma_{n})

Example 3.2.6.6
.

The open grid meshes look like this:

\displaystyle\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\dot{\textup{M}}}^{2}[0,0]

Observation 3.2.6.7
.

For
n\leq 1
the grid mesh functors
\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
and
\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}

are equivalences. For
n>1
the functors are fully faithful, exhibiting

\Delta^{n,\textup{op}}
and
\Delta^{n}
as full subcategories of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}

and
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.

3.3
Trusses

In §
3.2.1
we have seen that
the
\infty
-category
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
that classifies
closed
1
-mesh bundles is equivalent to the
1
-category
\Delta^{\textup{op}}
.
The geometric theory of closed
1
-mesh bundles is therefore captured,
up to equivalence,
by the combinatorics of finite non-empty ordinals and order-preserving maps.
Closed
n
-trusses are the combinatorial objects that extend this correspondence to closed
n
-meshes.
Dually, open
n
-trusses are the combinatorial objects associated with open
n
-meshes.

Open trusses are a generalisation of the zigzag construction of
[
RV19
,
HRV22
]
,
which admits a computable representation and serves as the core of a graphical proof assistant for higher categories.
The data structures and algorithms for the zigzag construction straightforwardly
extend to trusses.
To keep the scope of this thesis manageable, we will however not explore the computational aspects further.

3.3.1
Closed Trusses

We begin with closed trusses.
With the intention in mind that the
1
-category
\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}
that classifies closed
1
-trusses should be equivalent to
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}

while being purely combinatorial in nature,
the equivalence
\textup{sing}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}

allows us to simply define
\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}:=\Delta^{\textup{op}}
.
We can then define the counterpart
\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}
of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{*}
as follows.

Definition 3.3.1.1
.

The objects of the
1
-category
\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}
are
singular objects
of
the form
\bar{\textup{s}}_{i}[n]
for natural numbers
0\leq i\leq n
and
regular objects

\bar{\textup{r}}_{i}[n]
for
0\leq i<n
.
The morphisms of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}
are defined as

\displaystyle\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}(\bar{\textup{s}}_{j}[m],\bar{\textup{s}}_{i}[n])

\displaystyle=\{\alpha:[n]\to[m]\mid\alpha(i)=j\}

\displaystyle\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}(\bar{\textup{r}}_{j}[m],\bar{\textup{r}}_{i}[n])

\displaystyle=\{\alpha:[n]\to[m]\mid\alpha(i)\leq j<\alpha(i+1)\}

\displaystyle\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}(\bar{\textup{s}}_{j}[m],\bar{\textup{r}}_{i}[n])

\displaystyle=\{\alpha:[n]\to[m]\mid\alpha(i)\leq j\leq\alpha(i+1)\}

\displaystyle\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}(\bar{\textup{r}}_{j}[m],\bar{\textup{s}}_{i}[n])

\displaystyle=\varnothing

and compose as the opposite of the underlying order-preserving maps. There is a
canonical forgetful functor
\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
called the

universal closed
1
-truss bundle
which sends both

\bar{\textup{s}}_{i}[n]
and
\bar{\textup{r}}_{i}[n]
to
[n]
.
A
closed
1
-truss bundle
is a map
f:E\to B
of simplicial sets
together with a pullback square

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Delta^{\textup{op}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1}}

The map
\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1}
induces a polynomial functor
\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}(-):\textup{sSet}\to\textup{sSet}
.

Example 3.3.1.2
.

The fibre of
\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
over a finite ordinal
[n]

is a sequence of
n
consecutive cospans between
n
regular and
n+1
singular elements

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{s}}_{0}[n]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{r}}_{0}[n]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{s}}_{1}[n]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cdots}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{s}}_{n-1}[n]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{r}}_{n-1}[n]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{s}}_{n}[n]}

In particular the fibre over
[0]
consists of a single singular element
\bar{\textup{s}}_{0}[0]
.
We observe that these fibres are equivalent to the exit path
\infty
-categories of closed
1
-meshes with the requisite number of singular strata.

Example 3.3.1.3
.

The fibre of
\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
over the opposite of an order
preserving map
\alpha:[n]\to[m]
consists of two sequences of cospans
with
m+1
and
n+1
singular elements, respectively, connected together
to form a planar diagram.
The maps between the singular elements are determined directly by
\alpha
,
while the remaining maps follow.

1.

The opposite of the map
[1]\to[2]
defined by
0\mapsto 1
and
1\mapsto 2

restricts a sequence of two consecutive cospans to the second cospan.
We interpret this as the restriction to a subdiagram.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{s}}_{0}[2]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{r}}_{0}[2]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{s}}_{1}[2]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{r}}_{1}[2]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{s}}_{2}[2]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{s}}_{0}[1]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{r}}_{0}[1]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{s}}_{1}[1]}

2.

The opposite of the unique map
[1]\to[0]
splits a singular element by inserting a regular element between them.
We interpret this as inserting an identity level into a diagram.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{s}}_{0}[0]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{s}}_{0}[1]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{r}}_{0}[1]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{s}}_{1}[1]}

3.

The opposite of the map
[1]\to[2]
defined by
0\mapsto 0
and
1\mapsto 2

merges two regular levels.
We interpret this as a composition operation.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{s}}_{0}[2]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{r}}_{0}[2]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{s}}_{1}[2]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{r}}_{1}[2]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{s}}_{2}[2]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{s}}_{0}[1]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{r}}_{0}[1]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\textup{s}}_{1}[1]}

Lemma 3.3.1.4
.

The map
\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
is a categorical fibration.

Proof.

Being a functor between
1
-categories, the map is automatically an inner fibration
by Lemma
2.1.2.7
.
Because
\Delta^{\textup{op}}
is skeletal, i.e. the isomorphisms in
\Delta^{\textup{op}}
are exactly the
identity maps, the map
\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
is trivially an isofibration.
∎

Lemma 3.3.1.5
.

Let
P
be a poset,
\varphi:P\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
a functor and

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\times_{\Delta^{\textup{op}}}P}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{P}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{\textup{op}}}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi}

the pullback of simplicial sets.
Then
\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\times_{\Delta^{\textup{op}}}P
is a poset.

The stratified geometric realisation functor
\|-\|:\textup{sSet}\to\textup{Strat}

gives us a method to geometrically realise a closed
1
-truss bundle
as a map of stratified spaces.
Equipped with the appropriate
1
-framing, the result is a closed
1
-mesh bundle.
Remember that when
P
is a poset, the stratified geometric realisation
\|P\|
is glued together from a stratified
k
-simplex
\|\Delta[k]\|
for every flag
[k]\hookrightarrow P
.

Construction 3.3.1.6
.

We construct a geometric realisation functor
\Delta^{\textup{op}}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}

that sends a
k
-simplex
\alpha:[k]\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
to a closed
1
-mesh
bundle
\xi:{X}\to\|\Delta[k]\|
with
\textup{sing}(\xi)=\alpha
.
We first obtain a closed
1
-truss bundle

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{E}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{\textup{op}}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha}

by pullback, where
\mathcal{E}
is a poset by Lemma
3.3.1.5
.
To every element
e\in\mathcal{E}
we assign a coordinate

R(e)\in{|\Delta[k]|}\times\mathbb{R}
with
R(e)=(F(e),2i)
when

\alpha^{\prime}(e)=\bar{\textup{s}}_{i}[n]
and
R(e)=(F(e),2i+1)
when

\alpha^{\prime}(e)=\bar{\textup{r}}_{i}[n]
.
This assignment extends to an embedding
|\mathcal{E}|\to{|\Delta[k]|}\times\mathbb{R}
by linear interpolation, defining a framing for the stratified bundle

\|F\|:\|\mathcal{E}\|\to\|\Delta[k]\|
.
Then
\xi:=\|F\|
is a closed
1
-mesh bundle with
\textup{sing}(\xi)=\alpha
.

Remark 3.3.1.7
.

There are other possible coordinate assignments
for Construction
3.3.1.6

that result in the geometric realisation being a closed
1
-mesh bundle.
In particular any coordinate assignment which respects the frame order
(see
[
DD21
]
) will lead to an equivalent result.

Lemma 3.3.1.8
.

The geometric realisation functor
\Delta^{\textup{op}}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}

from Construction
3.3.1.6

is a homotopy inverse to the equivalence

\textup{sing}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
.

Proof.

By Proposition
3.2.1.13
the functor

sing
is a trivial fibration and therefore
and equivalence of quasicategories.
The functor
\Delta^{\textup{op}}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
is a section of the equivalence

sing
and therefore a homotopy inverse.
∎

Construction 3.3.1.9
.

We construct a map
\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{*}
which fits into the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{\textup{op}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{M}}}^{1}}

where
\Delta^{\textup{op}}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
is the geometric realisation functor
from Construction
3.3.1.6
.
Let
\alpha^{\prime}:[k]\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}
be a
k
-simplex.
Then by composition with
\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
, we get a
k
-simplex

\alpha:[k]\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
.
By taking the pullback and by the universal property of that pullback,
we then have a diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{E}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{\textup{op}}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
id
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces S}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha}

The
k
-simplex
\alpha^{\prime}:[k]\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}
therefore determines
a
1
-truss bundle together with a section.
We can then take the stratified geometric realisation

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\mathcal{E}\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[k]\|}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\|F\|}
id
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\|S\|}

and equip the stratified bundle
\|F\|
with a
1
-framing as in
Construction
3.3.1.6
.
The closed
1
-mesh bundle
\|F\|
and its section
\|S\|

together determine a
k
-simplex of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{*}
.

Lemma 3.3.1.10
.

The geometric realisation map

\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{*}

from Construction
3.3.1.9

is a categorical equivalence.

Proof.

We construct a map
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{*}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}
and demonstrate that it
is a deformation retraction of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{*}
.
A
k
-simplex of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{*}
is represented by
a closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi:{X}\to\|\Delta[k]\|

together with a section
s:\|\Delta[k]\|\to{X}
.
The map
\textup{sing}(\xi):[k]\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
induces a closed
1
-truss bundle

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{E}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{\textup{op}}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{sing}(\xi)}

and by Construction
3.3.1.6
a closed
1
-mesh bundle
\|F\|:\|\mathcal{E}\|\to\|\Delta[k]\|
with
\textup{sing}(\|F\|)=\textup{sing}(\xi)
.
We have by Proposition
3.2.1.13
that

\textup{sing}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
is a trivial fibration;
therefore there exists a closed
1
-mesh bundle

h:{H}\to{|\Delta[1]|}\times\|\Delta[k]\|

which restricts to
\xi
and
\|F\|

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{H}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\mathcal{E}\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\{0\}\times\|\Delta[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{|\Delta[1]|}\times\|\Delta[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\{1\}\times\|\Delta[k]\|}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces h}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\|F\|}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\llcorner}

As a closed
1
-mesh bundle
h
is a stratified fibre bundle,
and therefore we must have isomorphisms of posets

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})\cong\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({H})\cong\mathcal{E}
.
Consequently, we have a diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{E}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{\textup{op}}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({\xi})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1}}
id
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({s})}
id
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{sing}(\xi)}

The composite
[k]\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}
then defines a
k
-simplex of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}

as desired.
This defines the deformation retraction
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{*}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}
.
∎

Lemma 3.3.1.11
.

The map
\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
is a flat categorical fibration.

Proof.

The map already is a categorical fibration by Lemma
3.3.1.4
.
By Lemma
3.2.3.7
the map

\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{M}}}^{1}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{*}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}
is a flat categorical fibration.
The geometric realisation functors fit into the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{\textup{op}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{M}}}^{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}

in which by the horizontal maps are equivalences
by Lemma
3.3.1.8
and Lemma
3.3.1.10
.
Therefore the map
\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}

must be flat as well.
∎

Proposition 3.3.1.12
.

The polynomial functor

\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}(-):\textup{sSet}\to\textup{sSet}

induced by the universal closed
1
-truss bundle

\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}

satisfies the following properties:

1.

\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}(\mathcal{C})\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}
is a categorical fibration when
\mathcal{C}
is a quasicategory.

2.

\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}(-)
preserves quasicategories.

3.

\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}(-)
preserves
1
-categories.

4.

\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}(-)
preserves categorical equivalences between quasicategories.

Construction 3.3.1.13
.

The geometric realisation maps from
Construction
3.3.1.6
and
Construction
3.3.1.9

arrange into a diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{M}}}^{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}

and are equivalences by
Lemma
3.3.1.8
and

3.3.1.10
.
Since the maps are also monomorphisms
they are deformation retractions.
Then for any simplicial set

we obtain by Construction

a geometric realisation functor for closed labelled
1
-truss bundles

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}(C)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}(C)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}}}

When
\mathcal{C}
is a quasicategory,
the geometric realisation map

2.2.3.6
.

We recall from §
3.2.4
that for any quasicategory

\mathcal{C}
there is an equivalence between the quasicategory

,
which classifies closed
n
-meshes with labels in
\mathcal{C}
, and the

\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}(-):\textup{sSet}\to\textup{sSet}
to
\mathcal{C}
.
In the case of closed trusses, we define
\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n}(-)
from

Construction 3.3.1.14
.

We write
\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{n}(-):\textup{sSet}\to\textup{sSet}
for the

We abbreviate

.
Similarly,

\mathcal{C}
is.

Observation 3.3.1.15
.

Suppose that
A
,

,

Construction 3.3.1.16
.

Let

3.3.2
Open Trusses

We have a duality equivalence between closed and open
1
-meshes

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})^{\textup{op}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
reg
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{sing}^{\textup{op}}}

using that
reg
and
sing
are equivalences.
In the case of trusses we want the duality equivalence to be an isomorphism of
1
-categories,
leading us to define open
1
-trusses as follows.

Definition 3.3.2.1
.

The objects of the
1
-category
\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}
are
singular objects
of
the form
\dot{\textup{s}}_{i}[n]
for natural numbers
0\leq i<n
and
regular objects

\dot{\textup{r}}_{i}[n]
for
0\leq i\leq n
.
The morphisms of
\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}
are defined as

\displaystyle\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}(\dot{\textup{r}}_{i}[n],\dot{\textup{r}}_{j}[m])

\displaystyle=\{\alpha:[n]\to[m]\mid\alpha(i)=j\}

\displaystyle\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}(\dot{\textup{s}}_{i}[n],\dot{\textup{s}}_{j}[m])

\displaystyle=\{\alpha:[n]\to[m]\mid\alpha(i)\leq j<\alpha(i+1)\}

\displaystyle\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}(\dot{\textup{s}}_{i}[n],\dot{\textup{r}}_{j}[m])

\displaystyle=\{\alpha:[n]\to[m]\mid\alpha(i)\leq j\leq\alpha(i+1)\}

\displaystyle\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}(\dot{\textup{r}}_{i}[n],\dot{\textup{s}}_{j}[m])

\displaystyle=\varnothing

and compose as the underlying order-preserving maps. There is a
canonical forgetful functor
\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\Delta
called the

universal open
1
-truss bundle
which sends both

\dot{\textup{s}}_{i}[n]
and
\dot{\textup{r}}_{i}[n]
to
[n]
.
An
open
1
-truss bundle
is a map of simplicial sets

f:E\to B

together with a pullback square

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Delta}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}

Observation 3.3.2.2
.

There is a unique isomorphism
(-)^{\dagger}:\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to(\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*})^{\textup{op}}

over
\Delta
which sends a regular object
\dot{\textup{r}}_{i}[n]
to
the singular object
\bar{\textup{s}}_{i}[n]
and a singular object

\dot{\textup{s}}_{i}[n]
to the regular object
\bar{\textup{r}}_{i}[n]
.
This is the
duality isomorphism
between open and closed
1
-trusses.

Construction 3.3.2.3
.

The
compactification functor
for
1
-trusses
is the inclusion
\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\hookrightarrow\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}

that is defined on objects by

\dot{\textup{r}}_{i}[n]\mapsto\bar{\textup{r}}_{i}[n+1]
and
\dot{\textup{s}}_{i}[n]\mapsto\bar{\textup{s}}_{i+1}[n+1]

and fits into the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{\textup{op}}}}

A fibre of
\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\Delta
over some ordinal is a zigzag of maps
between regular and singular elements, ending with regular elements on both sides.
The functor
\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}
includes these zigzags into the
middle of the zigzag that is padded with singular elements on the ends.

Example 3.3.2.4
.

The compactification functor

\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\hookrightarrow\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}
embeds
the fibre of
\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\Delta
over
[1]

into the fibre of
\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\Delta^{\textup{op}}
over
[2]
as follows:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\dot{\textup{r}}_{0}[1]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\dot{\textup{s}}_{0}[1]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\dot{\textup{r}}_{1}[1]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\bar{\textup{s}}_{0}[2]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\bar{\textup{r}}_{0}[2]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\bar{\textup{s}}_{1}[2]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\bar{\textup{r}}_{1}[2]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\bar{\textup{s}}_{2}[2]}}

We know that the map
\textup{reg}:\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}\to\Delta

is a trivial fibration and therefore admits a homotopy inverse
which geometrically realises a finite non-empty ordinal
[i]
as an
open
n
-truss with
i+1
regular strata.
Just as with closed
1
-trusses, we can find an explicit construction
for such a geometric realisation functor that extends also to a functor

\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{*}
of pointed trusses and meshes.

However, in contrast to closed
1
-trusses, the geometric realisation
of an open
1
-truss bundle
f:E\to B
is
not

\|f\|:\|E\|\to\|B\|
regardless of
the framing we might put on
\|f\|
.
For any
b\in B
the fibre
f^{-1}(b)
is necessarily finite,
and therefore its geometric realisation as a topological space
|f^{-1}(b)|

is compact. The underlying space of an open
1
-mesh is
\mathbb{R}
,
which is not compact, and so
\|f\|
can not be an open
1
-mesh bundle.
Non-compact stratified spaces in general do not have finite triangulations, but they can have finite
relative triangulations, i.e. be presented as the complement

\|B\|\setminus\|B^{\prime}\|
where
B^{\prime}\subseteq B
is a downwards closed subposet.
For the geometric realisation of open
1
-trusses, we make us of this idea as follows: We first compactify the open
1
-truss to obtain a closed
1
-truss,
which we can then geometrically realise to a closed
1
-mesh. We can then
remove the first and last singular strata in each fibre, resulting in
the open
1
-mesh we need.

Construction 3.3.2.5
.

We can construct geometric realisation functors for open
1
-trusses via
compactification and the geometric realisation functors of closed
1
-trusses
from Construction
3.3.1.6
and
Construction
3.3.1.9
.
In particular we have a diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{\textup{op}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{\textup{op}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta}}

in which all rows consist of equivalences and compose to the identity.
Concretely, the functor
\Delta\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}
is the section
of
\textup{reg}:\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}\to\Delta
which sends
[i]\in\Delta

to the geometric realisation of
[i+1]\in\Delta^{\textup{op}}

as a closed
1
-truss. It then removes the first and last singular
strata of the resulting closed
1
-mesh and rescales to
\mathbb{R}
.
The functor
\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{*}
proceeds similarly,
keeping track of the section.

Observation 3.3.2.6
.

At this point we can again proceed analogously to our discussion
of closed
n
-trusses from §
3.3.1
.
We quickly state the corresponding results.
The universal open
1
-truss bundle

\cramped{\dot{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1}:\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}\to\Delta

is a flat categorical fibration since
it is equivalent to the flat categorical fibration
\cramped{\dot{\mathfrak{M}}}^{1}:\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}_{*}\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}
.
Therefore, the induced polynomial functor
\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}(-):\textup{sSet}\to\textup{sSet}
preserves quasicategories,
1
-categories, and categorical equivalences between quasicategories.
Moreover, via geometric realisation we obtain a natural equivalence

\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}(\mathcal{C})\simeq\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{1}(\mathcal{C})

for any quasicategory
\mathcal{C}
.
We can then define
\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n}(C)
for any
n\geq 0
and simplicial set

C
by iterating the functor
\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}(-)
:

\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n}(C):=\underbrace{(\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}\circ\cdots\circ\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1})}_{\textup{$n$ times}}(C)

In particular we then have a
1
-category
\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n}:=\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n}(*)
which classifies unlabelled open
n
-truss bundles.
Using the packing construction for open
n
-meshes,
we have a natural equivalence
\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})\simeq\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})
for every quasicategory
\mathcal{C}
.

Construction 3.3.2.7
.

The universal closed
1
-truss bundle
\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1}
is (isomorphic to) the categorical opposite of the universal open
1
-truss bundle
\cramped{\dot{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1}
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1,\textup{op}}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\dot{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{T}}}^{1,\textup{op}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}

We therefore have a natural isomorphism between the induced polynomial functors

\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}(C^{\textup{op}})\cong\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}(C)^{\textup{op}}

for all simplicial sets of labels
C
. This induces a natural isomorphism

\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n}(C)=\underbrace{(\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1}\circ\cdots\circ\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{1})}_{\textup{$n$ times}}(C^{\textup{op}})\cong\underbrace{(\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1}\circ\cdots\circ\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{1})}_{\textup{$n$ times}}(C)^{\textup{op}}=\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{n}(C)^{\textup{op}}

for all
n\geq 0
and simplicial sets
C
.
Together with the geometric realisation equivalences for open and closed
trusses, we obtain a duality equivalence between open and closed
n
-meshes
with labels in any quasicategory
\mathcal{C}
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C}^{\textup{op}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})^{\textup{op}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C}^{\textup{op}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})^{\textup{op}}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}

Construction 3.3.2.8
.

Via the geometric realisation equivalence for open trusses and meshes,
the open grid mesh functor from Construction
3.2.6.5

induces an analogous functor for open trusses:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n}}}

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}

Moreover the grid functors are compatible with duality:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{n}}}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta^{n}}}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n}}}

3.4
Refinements

Open and closed n-meshes are both n-framed stratified spaces and therefore objects of
\textup{FrStrat}^{n}
.
Here we study the interaction of meshes with refinement maps between n-framed stratified spaces.
In §
3.4.1
we take a framed refinement map
\varphi:{X}\to{Y}

of closed
n
-meshes and view it as a map
{X}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{Y}
in
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
, called a degeneracy bordism. By taking compactifications, we get an analogous theory of
degeneracy bordisms of open
n
-meshes in §
3.4.2
.
In §
3.4.3
we explore how to find the coarsest mesh that refines a tame stratified space,
which we then use in §
3.4.4
to define normal forms of meshes.

3.4.1
Degeneracy Bordisms of Closed Meshes

Example 3.4.1.1
.

Suppose we have a
1
-framed refinement map between closed
1
-meshes

{X}_{0}
{X}_{1}
\varphi

Then the projection map
\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}(\varphi)\to\|\Delta[1]\|
from the open
mapping cylinder of
\varphi
(see §
2.3.4
) can be equipped with a
1
-framing so
that it becomes the closed
1
-mesh bundle

This closed
1
-mesh bundle in turn defines a bordism of closed
1
-meshes

\cramped{\textup{deg}}_{\bar{\textup{M}}}(\varphi):{X}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{Y}
which we call the
degeneracy bordism induced by
\varphi
.

Via the degeneracy bordisms arising from open mapping cylinders,
we can represent
n
-framed refinement maps between closed
n
-meshes as maps
within the
\infty
-category
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.
To make this work in general, we first need to equip open mapping cylinders of
n
-framed stratified
bundles with an induced
n
-framing.

Construction 3.4.1.2
.

Suppose that we have a sequence of
n
-framed refinement maps

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{0}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cdots}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{k-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{k}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{0}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cdots}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{k-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{k}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi_{k}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{k-1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{k}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{k}}

between
n
-framed stratified bundles and let

F:\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}^{k}({X}_{\bullet})\to\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}^{k}({B}_{\bullet})

be the induced map between the open mapping cylinders.
Then we can equip
F
with an
n
-framing, defined for
x\in{X}_{0}

and
b\in\|\Delta[k]\|
by linear interpolation

\operatorname{fr}(F)(x,b):=\sum_{i\in[k]}b_{i}(\operatorname{fr}(f_{i})\circ\varphi_{i}\circ\cdots\circ\varphi_{1})(x)

This is well-defined because each
\varphi_{i}
is a refinement map and therefore
the underlying map of topological spaces
\operatorname{U}(\varphi_{i})
is an isomorphism.

Proposition 3.4.1.3
.

Suppose that we have a sequence of
n
-framed refinement maps

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{0}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cdots}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{k-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{k}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{0}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cdots}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{k-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{k}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi_{0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi_{k}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi_{k-1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi_{k}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{k}}

between closed
n
-mesh bundles.
Then the map
\Xi:\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}^{k}({X}_{\bullet})\to\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}^{k}({B}_{\bullet})

between the
k
-fold open mapping cylinders, equipped with the
n
-framing
from Construction
3.4.1.2
, is a closed
n
-mesh bundle.

Proof.

When
n=0
the claim is trivial, so suppose that
n>0
.
By writing the closed
n
-mesh bundles as composites
of closed
1
-mesh bundles followed by closed
(n-1)
-mesh bundles,
we obtain a diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{0}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cdots}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{k-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{k}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}_{0}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cdots}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}_{k-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}_{k}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{0}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cdots}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{k-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{k}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi_{0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi_{k}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi_{k-1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi_{k}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\rho_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta_{0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\rho_{k}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta_{k-1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta_{k}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{k}}

By induction, the map between open
k
-fold mapping cylinders

G:\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}^{k}({Y}_{\bullet})\to\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}^{k}({B}_{\bullet})

induced by the lower half of this diagram
is a closed
(n-1)
-mesh bundle when equipped with the framing
from Construction
3.4.1.2
.
Let
F:\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}^{k}({X}_{\bullet})\to\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}^{k}({Y}_{\bullet})

be the map between open
k
-fold mapping cylinders induced by the
upper half of the diagram and equip
F
with the
1
-framing
from Construction
3.4.1.2
.
Then the
1
-framing map
\operatorname{fr}(F)
is closed, and by Lemma
2.3.4.4

the induced map
\textup{Exit}(F)
is an isofibration.
Therefore, by Lemma
3.2.1.21

the
1
-framed stratified bundle
F
is a closed
1
-mesh bundle.
Therefore, the composite
G\circ F:\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}^{k}({X}_{\bullet})\to\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}^{k}({B}_{\bullet})

is a closed
n
-mesh bundle.
∎

Definition 3.4.1.4
.

Let
\varphi:{X}\to{Y}
be an
n
-framed refinement map
between closed
n
-meshes. Then the
degeneracy bordism induced by

\varphi
is the bordism of closed
n
-meshes

\cramped{\textup{deg}}_{\bar{\textup{M}}}(\varphi):{X}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{Y}

represented by the closed
n
-mesh bundle
\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}(\varphi)\to\|\Delta[1]\|
.

Definition 3.4.1.5
.

Let
f:{M}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{N}
be a bordism of closed
n
-meshes
represented by a closed
n
-mesh bundle
\Xi:{E}\to\|\Delta[1]\|
.
Then
f
is a
degeneracy bordism
if
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({\Xi}):\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}})\to[1]

is the cocartesian fibration associated to a surjective map of posets

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})\to\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{Y}})
.

Proposition 3.4.1.6
.

Let
f:{X}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{Y}
be a bordism of closed
n
-meshes.
Then
f
is a degeneracy bordism if and only if it is equivalent to

\cramped{\textup{deg}}_{\bar{\textup{M}}}(\varphi)
for some

n
-framed refinement map

\varphi:{X}\to{Y}
.
In that case we have that
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({\varphi}):\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})\to\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{N}})
is the surjective map of posets associated to the degeneracy bordism
f
.

Proof.

Let
\Xi:{E}\to\|\Delta[1]\|
be the closed
1
-mesh bundle that
represents
f
. Suppose first that
f
is a degeneracy bordism and let

s:\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})\to\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{Y}})
be the surjective map
of posets which unstraightens to the cocartesian fibration

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({\Xi}):\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}})\to[1]
.
Via the equivalence
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}\simeq\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{n}

between closed
n
-meshes and
n
-trusses, we may assume that
{X}
,
{Y}
and
\Xi
arise
as the geometric realisation of closed
n
-truss bundles

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{Y}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{[0]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{[1]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{[0]}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\llcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\langle 0\rangle}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\langle 1\rangle}

as described in Construction
3.3.1.6
.
The surjective map of posets

s:\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})\to\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{Y}})

induces a refinement map

\varphi:\|\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})\|\to\|\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({Y})\|
.
Unpacking the details of Construction
3.3.1.6
, we can see that

\varphi
preserves the
n
-framing and that
\Xi
is the open mapping cylinder
of
\varphi
.

For the implication in the other direction,
let
\varphi:{X}\to{Y}
be an
n
-framed refinement map
such that
\Xi:\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}(\varphi)\to\|\Delta[1]\|
represents the bordism

f:{X}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{Y}
.
Then Lemma
2.3.4.6
implies that
f
is a degeneracy bordism as required.
∎

Lemma 3.4.1.7
.

Degeneracy bordisms of closed
n
-meshes are closed under composition in the

\infty
-category
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.

Proof.

We use that by Proposition
3.4.1.6
each degeneracy bordism of closed
n
-meshes
is induced by
n
-framed refinement maps.
Let
\varphi_{01}:{X}_{0}\to{X}_{1}
and
\varphi_{12}:{X}_{1}\to{X}_{2}

be
n
-framed refinement maps between closed
n
-mesh bundles.
Then projection map
\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}({X}_{\bullet})\to\|\Delta[2]\|
of the
2
-fold open mapping cylinder
is a closed
n
-mesh bundle by Proposition
3.4.1.3
that represents the composition
of the induced degeneracy bordisms
\cramped{\textup{deg}}_{\bar{\textup{M}}}(\varphi_{01})
followed by

\cramped{\textup{deg}}_{\bar{\textup{M}}}(\varphi_{12})
. In particular the composite is

\cramped{\textup{deg}}_{\bar{\textup{M}}}(\varphi_{12}\circ\varphi_{01})
and therefore itself a degeneracy bordism
by Proposition
3.4.1.6
.
∎

We can broaden the concept of a degeneracy map of closed
n
-meshes to incorporate
labels within any quasicategory
\mathcal{C}
. The labelling of a degeneracy bordism
of labelled closed
n
-meshes is determined completely (up to contractible choice) by the labelling of
the codomain.

Definition 3.4.1.8
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C}
is a quasicategory and
\pi:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
the functor which forgets the labels.
Then a bordism
f
of closed
n
-meshes with labels in
\mathcal{C}
is a
degeneracy bordism

if
\pi(f)
is a degeneracy bordism and
f
is
\pi
-cartesian.

Lemma 3.4.1.9
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a quasicategory and
\pi:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}

the functor which forgets the labels.
Then
\pi
admits cartesian lifts of degeneracy maps.

Proof.

Let
\varphi:{X}\to{Y}
be an
n
-framed refinement map
between closed
n

\ell_{{Y}}:\textup{Exit}({Y})\to\mathcal{C}

\pi:\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}({X})\to\|\Delta[1]\|
the projection from the

\cramped{\textup{deg}}_{\bar{\textup{M}}}(\varphi)
.

\cramped{\textup{deg}}_{\bar{\textup{M}}}(\varphi)

({Y},\ell_{{Y}})

of
\ell_{{Y}}
along the inclusion map

\textup{Exit}({Y})\hookrightarrow\textup{Exit}(\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}({X}))
.
As long as the requisite limits exist in
\mathcal{C}
, we can therefore
compute
\ell

(3.11)

When

, then by Lemma

the identity exit path

has an
\textup{Exit}(\pi)
-cocartesian
lift to an exit path
\gamma:\|\Delta[1]\|\to\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}(\varphi)
starting
at
e
and ending at
\varphi(e)
.
Since the lift is
\textup{Exit}(\pi)
-cocartesian,
this path is an initial object in the slice
\textup{Exit}({Y})_{e/}

and so the limit (
3.11
) exists and evaluates to
\ell(e)\simeq\ell_{{Y}}(\varphi(e))
.

When
e
is not contained within
{X}
, then via the trivialisation
of
\pi
over the stratum
{(0,1]}\subseteq\|\Delta[1]\|
there exists
a stratum-preserving path
\gamma:{|\Delta[1]|}\to\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}(\varphi)
from
e
to
an element
y\in{Y}\subseteq\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}(\varphi)
.
Therefore, the limit (
3.11
) exists and evaluates on
e
to
\ell(e)\simeq\ell_{{Y}}(y)
.
∎
