Proposition 3.4.2.2
.

Suppose that we have a sequence of
n
-framed refinement maps

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}_{0}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cdots}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}_{k-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}_{k}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{0}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cdots}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{k-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{k}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi_{k}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{k-1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{k}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{k}}

between open
n
-mesh bundles.
Then the map
F:\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}^{k}({X}_{\bullet})\to\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}^{k}({B}_{\bullet})

between the
k
-fold open mapping cylinders, equipped with the
n
-framing
from Construction
3.4.1.2
, is an open
n
-mesh bundle.

Proof.

The sequence of
n
-framed refinement maps from the claim gives rise to a sequence
of
n
-framed refinement maps between the compactifications of the open
n
-mesh
bundles:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\bar{{M}}_{0}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\bar{{M}}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cdots}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\bar{{M}}_{k-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\bar{{M}}_{k}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{0}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cdots}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{k-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{k}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{f}_{0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{f}_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi_{k}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{f}_{k-1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{f}_{k}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{k}}

We can then apply Proposition
3.4.1.3
to see that the induced
n
-framed
stratified bundle
\bar{F}:\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}^{k}(\bar{{M}}_{\bullet})\to\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}^{k}({B}_{\bullet})

is a closed
n
-mesh bundle.
The restriction of
\bar{F}
to the constructible
n
-framed stratified subbundle
\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}^{k}({M}_{\bullet})\to\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}^{k}({B}_{\bullet})

then is an open
n
-mesh bundle, which is not identical with but isomorphic
as an
n
-framed stratified bundle to
the map
F
equipped with the framing from Construction
3.4.1.2
.
∎

Definition 3.4.2.3
.

Let
\varphi:{M}\to{N}
be an
n
-framed refinement map
between open
n
-meshes. Then the
degeneracy bordism induced by

\varphi
is the bordism of open
n
-meshes

\cramped{\textup{deg}}_{\dot{\textup{M}}}(\varphi):{M}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{N}

represented by the open
n
-mesh bundle
\cramped{\textup{Cyl}}_{\textup{o}}(\varphi)\to\|\Delta[1]\|
.

Definition 3.4.2.4
.

Let
f:{M}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{N}
be a bordism of open
n
-meshes
represented by an open
n
-mesh bundle
F:{E}\to\|\Delta[1]\|
.
Then
f
is a
degeneracy bordism
if
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({F}):\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}})\to[1]

is the cocartesian fibration associated to a surjective map of posets

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})\to\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{N}})
.

Observation 3.4.2.5
.

Let
f:{M}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{N}
be a bordism of open
n
-meshes.
Then
f
is a degeneracy bordism if and only if its compactification
is a degeneracy bordism of closed
n
-mesh bundles.

Proposition 3.4.2.6
.

Let
f:{M}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{N}
be a bordism of open
n
-meshes.
Then
f
is a degeneracy bordism if and only if it is equivalent to

\cramped{\textup{deg}}_{\dot{\textup{M}}}(\varphi)
for some

n
-framed refinement map

\varphi:{M}\to{N}
.
In that case we have that
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({\varphi}):\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})\to\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{N}})
is the surjective map of posets associated to the degeneracy bordism
f
.

Proof.

Follows from Proposition
3.4.1.6

by using Observation
3.4.2.5
.
∎

Lemma 3.4.2.7
.

Degeneracy bordisms of open
n
-meshes are closed under composition in the

\infty
-category
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.

Proof.

Follows from Lemma
3.4.1.7

∎

Definition 3.4.2.8
.

Suppose that
\mathcal{C}
is a quasicategory and
\pi:\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
the functor which forgets the labels.
Then a bordism
f
of open
n
-meshes with labels in
\mathcal{C}
is a
degeneracy bordism

when
\pi(f)
is a degeneracy bordism and
f
is
\pi
-cartesian.

Lemma 3.4.2.9
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a quasicategory and
\pi:\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}

the functor which forgets the labels.
Then
\pi
admits cartesian lifts of degeneracy maps.

Proof.

Analogous to the proof of Lemma
3.4.1.9
.
∎

3.4.3
Coarsest Refining Meshes

When
\varphi:{E}\to{K}
is an
n
-framed stratified bundle and
f
is an open or closed
n
-mesh bundle that refines
\varphi
,
the singularities in
f
detect the moments at which the arrangement of the strata in
{E}
changes qualitatively with respect to the framing.
It is in this sense that we may see framed combinatorial topology as a form of Morse theory.
Not every
n
-framed stratified bundle can be refined by an
n
-mesh bundle.
Obstructions to meshability include an infinite number of strata and various wild phenomena such as infinitely oscillating curves.
This is less a defect of meshes but a feature,
since meshability provides a criterion for tameness.

Definition 3.4.3.1
.

We say that an
n
-framed stratified bundle
\varphi
is
closed meshable
when there exists a closed
n
-mesh bundle

\xi
together with a refinement map
\xi\to\varphi
of
n
-framed stratified bundles.
Similarly, an
n
-framed stratified bundle
\varphi
is
open meshable
when it is refined by an open
n
-mesh bundle.

Lemma 3.4.3.2
.

Let
\varphi:{E}\to{K}
be a tame
1
-framed stratified bundle
such that
\operatorname{U}(\varphi)
is the projection
{[-1,1]}\times\operatorname{U}({K})\to\operatorname{U}({K})
.
Then there exists a coarsest closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi:{X}_{1}\to{X}_{0}

that refines
\varphi
as a
1
-framed stratified bundle so that
{M}_{0}
is a PL stratified pseudomanifold.

Proof.

We first apply Proposition
2.3.3.4
to obtain the coarsest
refinement
{X}_{0}\to{K}
so that
{X}_{0}
is a PL stratified pseudomanifold
and for each stratum
p\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}})
the closed image
\textup{cl}(f({E}_{p}))

is a constructible subspace of
{X}_{0}
.
Then we apply Lemma
2.3.3.7

to obtain the coarsest refinement

{X}_{1}\to{E}
such that
{X}_{1}
is a PL stratified pseudomanifold
and
\varphi
induces a stratified map
\xi:{X}_{1}\to{X}_{0}
.

The stratified map
\xi:{X}_{1}\to{X}_{0}
inherits the
1
-framing from
\varphi
.
The strata in the fibres of
\xi
consist of
isolated points and open intervals; half open or closed intervals in the interior
are excluded since
{X}_{1}
is a PL stratified pseudomanifold by construction.
The number and type of strata in the fibres is constant over every stratum
of
{X}_{0}
because the closure of the image
\textup{cl}(\varphi({E}_{p}))
is a constructible subspace for each stratum
p\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}})
.
Non-intersecting strata embedded in
\mathbb{R}
can not change their positions relative to each other and so
\xi
must be a stratified fibre bundle.
Since
{X}_{1}
is a PL stratified pseudomanifold, it satisfies the frontier condition,
and so by Lemma
3.2.1.7
the
1
-framed bundle

\xi:{X}_{1}\to{X}_{0}
must be a closed
1
-mesh bundle.
Any other mesh bundle that refines
\varphi
must also satisfy the criteria
that we enforced and so must refine
\xi
.
∎

Lemma 3.4.3.3
.

Let
\varphi:{E}\to{B}
be a tame
n
-framed stratified bundle
such that
\operatorname{U}(\varphi)
is the projection
{[-1,1]}^{n}\times\operatorname{U}({K})\to\operatorname{U}({B})
.
Then there exists a coarsest closed
n
-mesh bundle

\xi:{X}_{n}\to{X}_{0}

so that
\xi
refines
\varphi
as an
n
-framed stratified bundle
and
{X}_{0}
is a PL stratified pseudomanifold.

Proof.

The claim is trivial for
n=0
and covered by Lemma
3.4.3.2

for
n=1
. Suppose for induction that
n\geq 2
.
Using Proposition
2.3.3.4
and
Lemma
2.3.3.7

we can find the coarsest PL stratified pseudomanifold
{D}

with
\operatorname{U}({D})={[-1,1]}^{n-1}\times\operatorname{U}({K})

so that

\pi^{\geq n}:\operatorname{U}({D})\to\operatorname{U}({K})

induces a stratified map
{D}\to{K}
.
Then we find the coarsest PL stratified pseudomanifold
{E}^{\prime}
with a refinement

{E}^{\prime}\to{E}
so that the projection
\pi^{\geq n-1}:E\to D
becomes a stratified map
{E}^{\prime}\to{D}
.
At this point we have constructed the diagram of stratified spaces

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{D}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{K}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{K}}}
id
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi}

(3.12)

which consists of the coarsest refinements with PL stratified pseudomanifolds that make
\varphi:{E}\to{K}

factor through the projection.
The map
{E}^{\prime}\to{D}
inherits a
1
-framing
and satisfies the conditions of Proposition
3.4.3.2
.
We may therefore refine the
1
-framed bundle

{E}^{\prime}\to{D}
with the coarsest refining closed
1
-mesh bundle

{X}_{n}\to{X}_{n-1}
over a PL stratified pseudomanifold

{X}_{n-1}
.
This results in the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{n-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{K}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{D}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{K}}}
id

(3.13)

The map
{X}_{n-1}\to{K}
is an
n
-framed bundle
that satisfies the conditions of this proposition,
and so by induction we can obtain the coarsest refining closed
(n-1)
-mesh bundle

{X}_{n-1}^{\prime}\to{X}_{0}^{\prime}
.
By Lemma
3.2.1.8
closed
1
-mesh bundles are closed under pullback, which we use to fill
in the left square in the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}^{\prime}_{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}^{\prime}_{n-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}^{\prime}_{0}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{n-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{K}}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}

(3.14)

This finishes the construction of a closed
n
-mesh bundle

{X}_{n}^{\prime}\to{X}_{0}

that refines the given
n
-framed bundle
\varphi
.
Our construction guarantees that this closed
n
-mesh bundle is also the
coarsest one over a base space that is a PL stratified pseudomanifold, which can be checked by observing how any other such closed
n
-mesh bundle
is consecutively refined by the maps in the diagrams
(
3.12
), (
3.13
) and (
3.14
).
∎

Proposition 3.4.3.4
.

Let
\varphi:{E}\to{K}
be an essentially tame
n
-framed stratified bundle such that
\operatorname{U}(\varphi)
is the projection
\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\operatorname{U}({K})\to\operatorname{U}({K})
.
Then there exists a coarsest open
n
-mesh bundle

f:{M}_{n}\to{M}_{0}

so that
f
refines
\varphi
as an
n
-framed stratified bundle
and
{M}_{0}
is a PL stratified pseudomanifold.

Proof.

We pick any order-preserving and piecewise linear isomorphism
{(-1,1)}\to\mathbb{R}
.
Then the
n
-framed stratified bundle
\varphi
is isomorphic
to a tame
n
-framed stratified bundle
\varphi^{\prime}:{E}^{\prime}\to{K}

where
\operatorname{U}({E}^{\prime})={(-1,1)}^{n}\times\operatorname{U}({K})
.
Then we can construct the coarsest stratification
{E}^{\prime\prime}
of

{[-1,1]}^{n}\times\operatorname{U}({K})
so that
{E}^{\prime}
is a constructible
subspace of
{E}^{\prime\prime}
.
The projection map
\varphi^{\prime\prime}:{E}^{\prime\prime}\to{K}
with the induced

n
-framing then satisfies the conditions of Lemma
3.4.3.3
.
Hence there exists a coarsest closed
n
-mesh bundle
\xi:{X}_{n}\to{X}_{0}

that refines
\varphi^{\prime\prime}
so that
{X}_{0}
is a PL stratified pseudomanifold.
We write
{M}_{0}:={X}_{0}
and let
{M}_{n}
be the intersection

{X}_{n}\cap({(-1,1)}^{n}\times\operatorname{U}({K}))
.
Rescaling the framing then induces the open
n
-mesh bundle
f:{M}_{n}\to{M}_{0}
as desired.
∎

Observation 3.4.3.5
.

By Observation
2.3.3.5
the coarsest subdivisions
obtained via Proposition
2.3.3.4
are determined locally.
Going through the constructions in Lemma
3.4.3.2

and Lemma
3.4.3.3
we see that the coarsest
open
n
-mesh obtained in Proposition
3.4.3.4

is also determined locally.
Concretely, suppose that
\varphi:{E}\to{K}
is an
n
-framed stratified
bundle that satisfies the conditions of Proposition
3.4.3.4
and let

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{K}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{K}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi^{\prime}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi}

be the restriction of
\varphi
over an open subspace
{K}^{\prime}\subseteq{K}
.
Let
f
,
f^{\prime}
are the coarsest open
n
-mesh bundles over PL stratified pseudomanfolds
which refine
\varphi
and
\varphi^{\prime}
, respectively,
as produced by Proposition
3.4.3.4
.
Then
f
restricts to
f^{\prime}
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}

Remark 3.4.3.6
.

Coarsest refining meshes have been discussed before in
[
DD21
]

using a different approach.
While we have constructed a coarsest refining mesh for PL framed stratified spaces
directly, Dorn and Douglas show that there exists some refining mesh
that is not necessarily the coarsest.
They then demonstrate that every meshable framed stratified space admits
a coarsest mesh refinement by calculating the join of all refining meshes.
The techniques of
[
DD21
]
likely generalise
to bundles as well, but this is not discussed in detail.

3.4.4
Normal Forms

For an unlabelled open
n
-mesh
{M}
there always exists a refinement
map
{M}\to\mathbb{R}^{n}
which forgets all strata of
{M}
, and therefore
a degeneracy bordism
{M}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}\mathbb{R}^{n}
. However, when
{M}
is equipped
with labels in some quasicategory
\mathcal{C}
, not every refinement map out of

{M}
is compatible with the labelling.

Example 3.4.4.1
.

Consider the following
1
-mesh
{M}
with labels in
[1]
:

1
0
1
1
1
0
1

Because the singular strata of
{M}
on the left and right are labelled differently from their surrounding regular strata, we can not coarsen
{M}
in any way which would forget these two singular strata
while still preserving the labelling.
This is not an issue for the middle singular stratum, and so we
can coarsen
{M}
by merging that singular stratum with its
surrounding regular strata as follows:

1
0
1
0
1

This open
1
-mesh now can not be coarsened further, and therefore
is the normal form
\textup{nf}({M})
of the open labelled
1
-mesh
{M}
.

Proposition 3.4.4.2
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a quasicategory and
{M}\in\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})
an open
n
-mesh with labels
in
\mathcal{C}
. Then the
\infty
-subcategory of the slice
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})_{{M}/}
consisting
of degeneracy maps out of
{M}
has a terminal object

{M}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}\textup{nf}({M})
.

Proof.

Up to equivalence in
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})
we can assume that
{M}
is tame.
We then let
{M}
be the coarsest
n
-framed stratified space with an
n
-framed refinement

\varphi:{M}\to{E}
such that the labelling map
\ell_{{M}}:\textup{Exit}({M})\to\mathcal{C}

factors through
\textup{Exit}(\varphi)
.
While
{E}
itself is not necessarily an open
n
-mesh,
by Proposition
3.4.3.4
there exists a coarsest open
n
-mesh
{N}

with a refinement map
{N}\to{E}
.
Because
{M}
is an open
n
-mesh which also refines
\psi
,
there then must be a refinement map
\psi:{M}\to{N}
.
We then define the labelling map
\ell_{{N}}:\textup{Exit}({N})\to\mathcal{C}

via the induced labelling of
{E}
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({M})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({N})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({E})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\ell_{{M}}}

The refinement map
\psi:{M}\to{N}
then induces
a degeneracy bordism
{M}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{N}
of
n
-meshes with
labels in
\mathcal{C}
. By construction of
{N}
as the
coarsest open
n
-mesh that refines
{E}
this
degeneracy bordism is the claimed terminal object.
∎

Remark 3.4.4.3
.

When
\mathcal{C}
is a Kan complex and
{M}
is an open
n
-mesh with
labels in
\mathcal{C}
, then the normal form of
{M}
is the open
n
-mesh
\mathbb{R}^{n}

with the induced labels.

Remark 3.4.4.4
.

When
{M}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{N}
is a bordism of open
n
-meshes
with labels in some quasicategory
\mathcal{C}
, we do
not
in general
have an induced bordism
\textup{nf}({M})\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}\textup{nf}({N})
between
the normal forms.

Remark 3.4.4.5
.

Via the equivalence
\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})\simeq\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})

the concept of degeneracy maps transfers from open meshes to trusses.
The degeneracy maps of open trusses then agree (up to taking opposites)
with the degeneracy maps in the zigzag category that were discussed in
[
HRV22
]
.
We refer to there for an alternative combinatorial proof of
3.4.4.2
as well as an algorithm that efficiently computes the normal form.

3.5
Embeddings

Similar to framed refinement maps, also constructible embeddings between open or closed
n
-meshes induce bordisms in the respective classifying
\infty
-categories
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
and
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.
We begin in §
3.5.1
by demonstrating how constructible embeddings between closed
n
-meshes correspond to inert bordisms in
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
, using a reversed mapping cylinder construction.
Then in §
3.5.2
we use the duality between open and closed
n
-meshes to discuss constructible embeddings and inert bordisms for open
n
-meshes.
In §
3.5.3
we show that inert bordisms are part of an orthogonal factorisation system on
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
and
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.
Open and closed meshes are covered by atoms and cells, respectively,
which we discuss in §
3.5.4
.
Finally, in §
3.5.5
we characterise atoms and cells
by their singularity type.

3.5.1
Inert Bordisms of Closed Meshes

.

1
-mesh
{X}

subspace

-mesh, as below:

Construction 3.5.1.2
.

Let
{X}
be a closed
n
-mesh and
{Y}\subseteq{X}

a closed constructible
n
-submesh.
The
reversed mapping cylinder
of the inclusion
{Y}\subseteq{X}

is the constructible subbundle

{E}\to\|\Delta[1]\|

of
{X}\times\|\Delta[1]\|\to\|\Delta[1]\|

where

{E}=({X}\times\{0\})\cup({Y}\times{(0,1]})\subseteq{X}\times\|\Delta[1]\|.

To show that the reversed mapping cylinder of any constructible embedding
between closed
n
-meshes is a closed
n
-mesh bundle itself, we use an auxiliary
result that lets us restrict closed
n
-mesh bundles to constructible subbundles.

Lemma 3.5.1.3
.

Let
\xi:{X}\to{B}
be a closed
n
-mesh bundle and

\xi^{\prime}:{X}^{\prime}\to{B}^{\prime}
a closed constructible subbundle
such that each fibre of
\xi^{\prime}
is a closed
n
-mesh.
Then
\xi^{\prime}
is a closed
n
-mesh bundle itself.

Proof.

We begin by writing
\xi:{X}\to{B}
as the composite of
a closed
1
-mesh bundle
\chi:{X}\to{Y}
followed by a
closed
(n-1)
-mesh bundle
\zeta:{Y}\to{B}
.
We can then also factor the closed constructible subbundle
\xi^{\prime}
to obtain
the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta}

The two squares are closed constructible embeddings of framed stratified bundles.
For every
b\in{B}
the fibre of
\xi^{\prime}(b)
is a closed
n
-mesh.
By the pasting lemma for pullbacks, the fibre of
\xi^{\prime}=\zeta^{\prime}\circ\chi^{\prime}
over
b
can be
computed in two stages:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}^{\prime\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}^{\prime\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\{b\}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi^{\prime}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta^{\prime}}

Hence the fibre of
\zeta^{\prime}
over
b
is the closed
(n-1)
-mesh
{Y}^{\prime\prime}
.
Therefore, by induction on
n\geq 0
the
(n-1)
-framed stratified bundle
\zeta^{\prime}

is a closed
(n-1)
-mesh bundle.

It remains to show that
\chi^{\prime}
is a closed
1
-mesh bundle.
Since the closed
1
-mesh bundle
\chi
is a stratified fibre bundle
and
\chi^{\prime}
is a constructible subbundle, it follows that
\chi^{\prime}
is
also a stratified fibre bundle.
Let
y\in{Y}^{\prime}
be any point, then the fibre of
\chi^{\prime}
over

y
is the closed
1
-mesh
{X}^{\prime\prime\prime}
constructed by taking the pullbacks

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}^{\prime\prime\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}^{\prime\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\{y\}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}^{\prime\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\{\chi^{\prime}(y)\}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi^{\prime}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta^{\prime}}

The subspace of singular points
\textup{sing}({X}^{\prime})\subseteq{X}^{\prime}
is
the preimage of the closed subset of singular points
\textup{sing}({X})\subseteq{X}^{\prime}
via the embedding
{X}^{\prime}\hookrightarrow{X}
.
Therefore,
\textup{sing}({X}^{\prime})
is closed in
{X}^{\prime}
.
Moreover the framing map of
\chi^{\prime}
is the composite of the closed embeddings

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{U}({X}^{\prime})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{U}({X})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{R}\times\operatorname{U}({Y}^{\prime})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{fr}(\chi)}

and is therefore closed itself.
∎

Definition 3.5.1.4
.

Let
f:{X}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{Y}
be a bordism of closed
n
-meshes
represented by a closed
n
-mesh bundle
\xi:{E}\to\|\Delta[1]\|
.
Then
f
is
inert
if
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({\xi}):\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}})\to[1]

is the cartesian fibration associated to an inclusion of posets

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{Y}})\hookrightarrow\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})
.

Proposition 3.5.1.5
.

Let
f:{X}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{Y}
be a bordism of closed
n
-meshes.
Then
f
is inert if and only if it is equivalent to the bordism
induced by the reversed mapping cylinder of a constructible embedding
{X}\hookrightarrow{Y}
.

Proof.

Analogous to Proposition
3.4.1.6
.
∎

Lemma 3.5.1.6
.

Inert bordisms of closed
n
-meshes are closed under composition in
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.

Proof.

Suppose that we have inert bordisms
f_{01}:{X}_{1}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{X}_{0}
and
f_{12}:{X}_{2}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{X}_{1}
of closed
n
-meshes.
By Proposition
3.5.1.5
we may assume that
f_{01}
and
f_{12}
arise
as the reversed mapping cylinders of constructible embeddings

\varphi_{01}:{X}_{0}\hookrightarrow{X}_{1}

and
\varphi_{12}:{X}_{1}\hookrightarrow{X}_{2}
.
We then let
\varphi_{02}:{X}_{0}\hookrightarrow{X}_{2}

be the composite
\varphi_{02}=\varphi_{12}\circ\varphi_{01}
.
Consider the closed
n
-mesh bundle

\Xi:{E}\to\|\Delta[2]\|

where
{E}
is the constructible subspace
of
{X}_{2}\times\|\Delta[2]\|
where

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}})
is the subposet of
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}_{2}})\times[2]
defined by

\displaystyle\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}}):=

\displaystyle\ \{(p,0)\mid p\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}_{2}})\}

\displaystyle\cup

\displaystyle\ \{(\varphi_{01}(p),1)\mid p\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}_{1}})\}

\displaystyle\cup

\displaystyle\ \{(\varphi_{02}(p),2)\mid p\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}_{0}})\}

By Lemma
3.5.1.3
we have that
\Xi
is a closed
n
-mesh bundle.
Moreover,
\Xi
restricts to the reversed mapping cylinders of the
inclusions
\varphi_{01}
,
\varphi_{02}
and
\varphi_{12}
.
Therefore,
\Xi
witnesses the composition of the inert bordisms

f_{01}
and
f_{12}
.
∎

Definition 3.5.1.7
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a quasicategory.
A bordism
f
of closed
n
-meshes with labels in
\mathcal{C}
is
inert

if the functor
\pi:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
which forgets the labels
sends
f
to an inert bordism
\pi(f)
and
f
is
\pi
-cocartesian.

When
{Y}\hookrightarrow{X}
is a constructible embedding between
closed
n
-meshes and we have a label functor
\ell:\textup{Exit}({X})\to\mathcal{C}

in some quasicategory
\mathcal{C}
, we can restrict
\ell
to a label functor for

{Y}
. Expressed in the language of inert bordisms, this restriction is
realised by a cocartesian lift of the inert bordism
{X}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{Y}

associated to the constructible embedding.

Lemma 3.5.1.8
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a quasicategory.
Then the functor
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}

which forgets the labels has cocartesian lifts of inert maps.

Proof.

Analogous to Lemma
3.4.2.9
.
∎

Lemma 3.5.1.9
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a quasicategory.
Then the inert bordisms of closed
n
-meshes with labels in
\mathcal{C}

are closed under composition in
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})
.

Proof.

Inert bordisms of closed unlabelled
n
-meshes are closed under composition
by Lemma
3.5.1.6
. The claim then follows since cocartesian maps are also
closed under composition.
∎

constructible embeddings. The inert bordisms of open meshes are dual to those
of closed meshes.

Here we use that the framing on an open
n
-mesh bundle is open, so that
we can gradually move the strata of
{M}_{1}
which are not in the image
of
\varphi
to infinity on either side.

Definition 3.5.2.2
.

Let
f:{M}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{N}
be a bordism of open
n
-meshes
represented by an open
n
-mesh bundle
F:{E}\to\|\Delta[1]\|
.
Then
f
is
inert
if
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({F}):\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}})\to[1]

is the cocartesian fibration associated to an inclusion of posets

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})\hookrightarrow\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{N}})
.

Lemma 3.5.2.3
.

A bordism of open
n
-meshes is inert if and only if it is sent to an inert
bordism of closed
n
-meshes by the duality equivalence
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}\simeq\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n,\textup{op}}
.

Proof.

Suppose that
F:{E}\to\|\Delta[1]\|
is an open
n
-mesh bundle.
Let
\Xi:{X}\to\|\Delta[1]^{\textup{op}}\|
be the closed
n
-mesh bundle
that is dual to
F
via the equivalence
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}\simeq\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n,\textup{op}}
.
We then have
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({F})=\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({\Xi})
.
Therefore,
F
represents an inert bordism of open
n
-meshes precisely when

\Xi
is an inert bordism of closed
n
-meshes.
∎

Corollary 3.5.2.4
.

Inert bordisms of open
n
-meshes are closed under composition in
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.

Proof.

Via Lemma
3.5.2.3
this follows by duality from Lemma
3.5.1.6
.
∎

We can use also use duality to construct open mapping cylinders for every constructible
inclusion between open
n
-meshes, which then represent the appropriate inert bordisms.
Using duality for this purpose is convenient since the resulting open
n
-mesh bundle
does not have the
n
-framing from Construction
3.4.1.2
.
Rather, as we have seen in Example
3.5.2.1
above, the
n
-framing
for an inert bordism of open
n
-meshes sends the parts that are not in the image
of the embedding off to infinity on the sides.

Construction 3.5.2.5
.

Suppose that
{M}
is an open
n
-mesh and
{N}\subseteq{M}

a constructible subspace that is also an open
n
-mesh.
We can then construct an inert map
{N}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{M}
as follows.
Via duality between open and closed
n
-meshes, the dual
{N}^{\dagger}

is a constructible subspace of
{M}^{\dagger}
.
Then by Construction
3.5.1.2
we obtain an inert bordism of closed
n
-meshes

{M}^{\dagger}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{N}^{\dagger}
.
Applying duality again then yields the inert bordism of open
n
-meshes

{N}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{M}
.

3.5.3
Active Bordisms and Factorisations

Definition 3.5.3.1
.

Let
f:{X}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{Y}
be a bordism of closed
n
-meshes
represented by a closed
n
-mesh bundle
\xi:{E}\to\|\Delta[1]\|
.
Then
f
is
active
if for every
p\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})

there exists a
q\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{Y}})
such that
p\leq q
in

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}})
.
A bordism of closed
n
-meshes with labels in a quasicategory
\mathcal{C}

is
active
if it is active after forgetting the labels.

Lemma 3.5.3.2
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a quasicategory.
Active bordisms of closed
n
-meshes with labels in
\mathcal{C}

are closed under composition in
the
\infty
-category
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})
.

Proof.

Suppose that
\xi:{E}\to\|\Delta[2]\|
is a closed
n
-mesh bundle
which represents the composition of two active bordisms:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{0}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{2}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{12}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{02}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{01}}

Let
p_{0}\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}_{0}})
be an element.
Because
f_{01}
is active, there exists an element
p_{1}\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}_{1}})

such that
p_{0}\leq p_{1}
in
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}})
.
Further because
f_{12}
is active, there is an element
p_{2}\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}_{2}})

such that
p_{1}\leq p_{2}
in
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}})
.
Therefore,
p_{0}\leq p_{2}
and
f_{02}
is active.
∎

Lemma 3.5.3.3
.

Let
\xi:{X}\to{B}
be a closed
n
-mesh bundle
and
Q\subseteq\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})
a subposet.
Then there exists a smallest closed
n
-mesh bundle
\xi^{\prime}:{X}^{\prime}\to{B}^{\prime}
with a
closed constructible embedding into
\xi
such that
Q\subseteq\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}^{\prime}})\subseteq\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})
.

Proof.

Without loss of generality we can assume that
Q
is downwards closed.
When
n=0
then
\xi
is the identity map of
{X}={B}

and
\xi^{\prime}
is the identity map of the constructible subspace
{B}^{\prime}\subseteq{B}

with
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{B}^{\prime}})=Q\subseteq\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{B}})
.
Now suppose that we have
n>0
.
We can then write
\xi
as the composite of a closed
1
-mesh bundle

\chi:{X}\to{Y}
followed by a closed
(n-1)
-mesh bundle

\zeta:{Y}\to{X}
.
By induction on
n
there exists a smallest closed
(n-1)
-mesh bundle

\zeta^{\prime}:{Y}^{\prime}\to{B}^{\prime}
together with a closed constructible embedding

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta}

such that
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{Y}^{\prime}})
contains the subposet

Q^{\prime}=\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({\chi})(Q)\subseteq\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{Y}})
.
Let
{X}^{\prime\prime}\subseteq{X}
be the closed constructible subspace
such that
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}^{\prime\prime}})=Q\subseteq\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})
.
Then the closed
1
-mesh bundle
\chi
restricts to the
1
-framed stratified
subbundle
\chi^{\prime\prime}
in the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}^{\prime\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi^{\prime\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta}

The
1
-framed stratified bundle
\chi^{\prime\prime}
is not a closed
1
-mesh bundle
in general: The fibres of
\chi^{\prime\prime}
are closed constructible subspaces
of closed
1
-meshes but may fail to be closed
1
-meshes themselves
by being disconnected. We therefore let
\chi^{\prime}:{X}^{\prime}\to{Y}^{\prime}

be the fibrewise convex closure of
\chi^{\prime\prime}:{X}^{\prime}\to{Y}^{\prime}
.
Then
\chi^{\prime}
is a closed
1
-mesh bundle we can let
\xi^{\prime}=\zeta^{\prime}\circ\chi^{\prime}
.
∎

Lemma 3.5.3.4
.

The inert and active bordisms of closed
n
-meshes form an orthogonal
factorisation system on
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.

Proof.

Let
f:{X}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{Y}
be a bordism of closed
n
-meshes.
We let
\xi:{E}\to\|\Delta[2]\|
be the closed
n
-mesh bundle
that corresponds to the commutative triangle of bordisms

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
id

We then use Lemma
3.5.3.3
and
let
\xi^{\prime}:{E}^{\prime}\to\|\Delta[2]\|
be the smallest
closed
n
-mesh bundle contained within
\xi
such that
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}^{\prime}})\subseteq\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}})

contains the subposet

\{p\mid\exists q\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{Y}}).\ \cramped{\mathbb{P}}({\xi})(q)=2\land p\leq q\}\cup\{p\mid\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({\xi})(p)=0\}\subseteq\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}}).

(3.15)

The closed
n
-mesh bundle
\xi^{\prime}
then represents a diagram of closed
n
-mesh bordisms

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Z}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{0}}

where
f_{0}
is inert and
f_{1}
is active by construction.

Now suppose that we have another factorisation of
f
into an inert map

f_{0}^{\prime}:{X}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{Z}^{\prime}
followed by an active map

f_{1}^{\prime}:{Z}^{\prime}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{Y}
.
Let
\xi^{\prime\prime}:{E}^{\prime\prime}\to\|\Delta[2]\|
be the closed
2
-mesh bundle
which represents this factorisation.
Then there is a natural inert map between the commutative triangles
of closed
n
-mesh bordisms

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Z}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{0}^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{1}^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{0}^{\prime}}

and therefore
\xi^{\prime\prime}
is a constructible subbundle of
\xi
.
Because
f_{1}^{\prime}
is required to be active, we see that the subposet

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}^{\prime\prime}})\subseteq\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}})
must agree with
the subposet (
3.15
).
Therefore,
\xi^{\prime\prime}
and
\xi^{\prime}
must agree by construction of
\xi^{\prime}
.
∎

Proposition 3.5.3.5
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a quasicategory.
Then the inert and active bordisms of closed
n
-meshes with labels in
\mathcal{C}

form an orthogonal factorisation system on the
\infty
-category
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})
.

Proof.

Let
f:{X}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{Y}
be a bordism of closed
n
-meshes
with labels in
\mathcal{C}
and let
\pi:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}

denote the forgetful functor.
By Proposition
3.5.3.4
the unlabelled bordism

\pi(f)
factors essentially uniquely into an inert bordism

f_{0}:\pi({X})\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{Z}
followed by an active bordism

f_{1}:{Z}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}\pi({X})
.
By Lemma
3.5.1.8
the forgetful functor

\pi
has cocartesian lifts of inert bordisms and so we can find
an essentially unique inert bordism
\hat{f}_{0}:{X}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}\hat{{Z}}

with
\pi(\hat{f}_{0})=f_{0}
. By the universal property of cocartesian
maps, we then also have an essentially unique bordism
\hat{f}_{1}:\hat{{Z}}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{Y}
such that
\pi(\hat{f}_{1})=f_{1}
and
f
is the composite
of
\hat{f}_{0}
followed by
\hat{f}_{1}
.
This is the essentially unique inert/active factorisation of
f
.
∎

The inert bordisms of open
n
-meshes are precisely the duals of the inert bordisms
of closed
n
-meshes. We can therefore use the duality equivalence
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})\simeq\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C}^{\textup{op}})^{\textup{op}}
to obtain an active/inert factorisation system on
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})
for each quasicategory
\mathcal{C}
.

Definition 3.5.3.6
.

Let
f:{M}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{N}
be a bordism of open
n
-meshes
represented by an open
n
-mesh bundle
F:{E}\to\|\Delta[1]\|
.
Then
f
is
active
if for every
q\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{N}})

there exists a
p\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})
such that
p\leq q
in

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}})
.
A bordism of open
n
-meshes with labels in a quasicategory
\mathcal{C}

is
active
if it is active after forgetting the labels.

Lemma 3.5.3.7
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a quasicategory.
A bordism of open
n
-meshes with labels in
\mathcal{C}
is active if and only if it is sent to an active
bordism of closed
n
-meshes by the duality equivalence
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})\simeq\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C}^{\textup{op}})^{\textup{op}}
.

Proof.

Analogous to Lemma
3.5.2.3
.
∎

Corollary 3.5.3.8
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a quasicategory.
Active bordisms of open
n
-meshes with labels in
\mathcal{C}
are closed under composition in
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})
.

Proof.

Using Lemma
3.5.3.7
and Lemma
3.5.3.2
.
∎

Corollary 3.5.3.9
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a quasicategory.
The active and inert bordisms of open
n
-meshes with labels in
\mathcal{C}
form an orthogonal factorisation system
on the
\infty
-category
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})
.

Proof.

Using Lemma
3.5.3.7
and Proposition
3.5.3.5
.
∎

3.5.4
Atoms and Cells

Definition 3.5.4.1
.

An open
n
-mesh
{M}
is an
atom
when
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})

has a minimal element. A closed
n
-mesh
{X}
is a
cell
when

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})
has a maximal element.

.

Via Construction
3.2.6.3
we also have an inclusion

\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\bar{\textup{M}}}:\Delta^{n,\textup{op}}\hookrightarrow\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.

[k_{1},\ldots,k_{n}]\in\Delta^{n}
the closed
n
-mesh

\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\bar{\textup{M}}}[k_{1},\ldots,k_{n}]
is a cell if and only if

0\leq k_{i}\leq 1
for all
1\leq i\leq n
.

n=2

Lemma 3.5.4.5
.

The duality equivalence
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}\simeq(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n})^{\textup{op}}

between open and closed
n
-meshes restricts
to an equivalence between the full subcategories of atoms and cells.

Proof.

When
{M}
is an open
n
-mesh and
{X}
a closed
n
-mesh
such that
{M}^{\dagger}\simeq{X}
, we have that

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})\cong\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})^{\textup{op}}
.
In particular
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})
has a minimal element if and only if

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})
has a maximal element.
∎

Remark 3.5.4.6
.

When
{M}
is an open
n
-mesh, the map
\textup{Exit}({M})\to\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})

is an equivalence. Therefore,
{M}
is an atom if and only if
\textup{Exit}({M})

has an initial object.
Analogously, a closed
n
-mesh
{X}
is a cell if and only if
\textup{Exit}({X})

has a terminal object.

Whenever
{X}
is a closed
n
-mesh, every element of the poset

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})
corresponds to a cell that is embedded in
{X}
.
Keeping in mind that the inert bordisms of closed
n
-meshes are oriented
in the opposite direction to embeddings, the assignment from
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})

to the corresponding cell of
{X}
induces a functor into the slice category

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{{X}/}
,
consisting of inert bordisms out of
{X}
and in between the cells of
{X}
.

Construction 3.5.4.7
.

Let
{X}
be a closed
n
-mesh.
For any element
p\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})
we can find the smallest
closed constructible
n
-submesh
\textup{cell}_{{X}}(p)
of
{X}
such
that
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({\textup{cell}_{{X}}(p)})\subseteq\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})

contains
p
.
By varying
p\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})^{\textup{op}}
and sending the initial object
of the left cone
\bot\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})^{\textup{op},\triangleleft}

to
{X}
itself we obtain the
cellular covering functor

\textup{cell}_{{X}}(-):\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})^{\textup{op},\triangleleft}\longrightarrow\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}.

Explicitly this functor is the classifying map of the closed
n
-mesh bundle

{E}\to\|\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})^{\textup{op},\triangleleft}\|

where
{E}
is the constructible subspace
of
{X}\times\|\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})^{\textup{op},\triangleleft}\|

given by the subposet

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}}):=\{(p,q)\mid p\leq q\}\cup\{(p,\bot)\}\subseteq\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})\times\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})^{\textup{op},\triangleleft}.

Lemma 3.5.4.8
.

Let
{X}
be a closed
n
-mesh. Then cellular covering functor

\textup{cell}_{{X}}(-):\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})^{\textup{op},\triangleleft}\longrightarrow\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}

is a limit diagram in
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.

Proof.

Suppose that we have a closed
n
-mesh
{Y}
and a compatible family
of maps
{Y}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}\textup{cell}_{{X}}(x)
for all
x\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})
,
represented by closed
n
-mesh bundles
f_{x}:{F}_{x}\to\|\Delta[1]\|
.
By induction on
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})
we can adjust these closed
n
-mesh bundles
up to equivalence so that
f_{x}
embeds into
f_{y}
for all elements
x\leq y
in
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})
.
Then we obtain a closed
n
-mesh bundle
f:{F}\to\|\Delta[1]\|

representing a map
{Y}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{X}
which is compatible with the maps

{Y}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}\textup{cell}_{{X}}(x)
.
Since
f
is unique up to equivalence this is the universal map into the limit.
∎

Construction 3.5.4.9
.

Let
{M}
be an open
n
-mesh.
For any element
p\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})
we can find the smallest
open constructible
n
-submesh
\textup{atom}_{{M}}(p)
of
{M}
such
that
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({\textup{atom}_{{M}}(p)})\subseteq\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})

contains
p
.
By varying
p\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})
and sending the terminal object
of the right cone
\bot\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})^{\triangleright}

to
{M}
itself we obtain the
atomic covering functor

\textup{atom}_{{M}}(-):\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})^{\triangleright}\longrightarrow\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}.

Explicitly this functor is the classifying map of the open
n
-mesh bundle

{E}\to\|\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})^{\triangleright}\|

where
{E}
is the constructible subspace
of
{X}\times\|\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})^{\triangleright}\|

given by the subposet

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{E}}):=\{(p,q)\mid p\geq q\}\cup\{(p,\top)\}\subseteq\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})\times\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})^{\triangleright}.

Observation 3.5.4.10
.

When
{M}
is an open
n
-mesh and
{X}={M}^{\dagger}
its dual
closed
n
-mesh, then the atomic covering diagram of
{X}
and the cellular
covering diagram of
{M}
are dual to each other as well:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})^{\triangleright,\textup{op}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})^{\textup{op},\triangleleft}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n,\textup{op}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{atom}_{{M}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{cell}_{{X}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces-^{\dagger}}

Lemma 3.5.4.11
.

Let
{M}
be an open
n
-mesh. Then the atomic covering functor

\textup{atom}_{{M}}(-):\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})^{\textup{op},\triangleright}\longrightarrow\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}

is a colimit diagram in
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.

Proof.

Using Lemma
3.5.4.8
and duality.
∎

Lemma 3.5.4.12
.

Let
f:{A}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{M}
be a degeneracy map of open
n
-meshes
so that
{A}
is an atom. Then
{M}
is again an atom.
Moreover when
\varphi:{A}\to{M}
is a refinement map so
that
f
is the open mappying cylinder of
\varphi
, then the induced map

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({\varphi})

sends the minimal element of
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{A}})
to minimal element of

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})
.

Proof.

Since
\varphi
is a refinement map
the induced map
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({\varphi})
must be surjective.
The claim then follows since surjective order-preserving maps must preserve the minimal element.
∎

3.5.5
Singularity Types

Definition 3.5.5.1
.

Let
{X}
be an
n
-framed stratified space that is either an atom or a cell.
We then have a sequence of projection maps

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{X}={X}_{n}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{X}_{n-1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cdots}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{X}_{i}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{X}_{0}=\|\Delta[0]\|}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{n}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{1}}

which are each
1
-framed stratified bundles.
The
singularity type
of
{X}
is the object

\textup{stype}({X}):=[k_{1},\ldots,k_{n}]\in\Delta^{n}

such that
k_{i}=0
if

f_{i}:{X}_{i}\to{X}_{i-1}

is an
n
-framed stratified trivial bundle
and
k_{i}=1
otherwise.
The
singular depth
of
{X}
is the largest
\textup{sdepth}({X}):=d\in[k]

such that
f_{i}:{X}_{i}\to{X}_{i-1}
is an
n
-framed stratified
trivial bundle for all
1\leq i\leq d
.

Observation 3.5.5.2
.

Suppose that
{A}
is an atom.
Then the singular depth of
{A}
is equivalently the largest
d\geq 0

such that there exists an
(n-d)
-framed stratified space
{B}

and an isomorphism
{B}\rtimes\mathbb{R}^{d}\cong{A}
of
n
-framed
stratified spaces.

Remark 3.5.5.3
.

Suppose that
{M}
is an open
n
-mesh whose strata are smooth
submanifolds of
\mathbb{R}^{n}
via the
n
-framing.
Let
p\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})
be a stratum and
\tau:{M}_{p}\to\textup{Gr}_{k}(\mathbb{R}^{n})

the continuous map into the Grassmannian which classifies the tangent bundle of

{M}_{p}
as embedded into
\mathbb{R}^{n}
.
Then the singularity type of the atom
\textup{atom}_{{M}}(p)
corresponds to the
Schubert cell of
\textup{Gr}_{k}(\mathbb{R}^{n})
through which
\tau
factors.

Construction 3.5.5.4
.

The
singular shape
of an atom
{A}
is the atom

\square{{A}}:=\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\dot{\textup{M}}}(\textup{stype}({A})).

Analogously the
singular shape
of a cell
{X}
is the cell

\square{{X}}:=\cramped{\boxplus}_{\scriptscriptstyle\bar{\textup{M}}}(\textup{stype}({X})).

Construction 3.5.5.5
.

Let
{A}
be an
n
-mesh atom such that
0\in\textup{Exit}({A})
.
We construct an active map of
n
-mesh atoms
\square{{A}}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{A}

such that
\square{{A}}
is the geometric realisation of the open
n
-truss
\textup{stype}({A})
.
We first equip the set
\{-1,0,+1\}
with the smallest partial order
\preceq

such that
0\preceq-1
and
0\preceq+1
.
For every
1\leq i\leq n
we define a poset
P_{i}
by

\displaystyle P_{i}

\displaystyle:=(\{-1,0,+1\},\preceq)

(if
\textup{stype}(A)_{i}=[1]
)

\displaystyle P_{i}

\displaystyle:=\{0\}

(if
\textup{stype}(A)_{i}=[0]
)

Then we realise
\square{{A}}
as the stratification of
\mathbb{R}^{n}

with poset
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({\square{{A}}})=P_{1}\times\cdots\times P_{n}

so that the stratifying map is defined in components by

\displaystyle\cramped{\mathbb{s}}({\square{{A}}})(x)_{i}

\displaystyle:=\operatorname{sgn}(x_{i})

(if
\textup{stype}(A)_{i}=[1]
)

\displaystyle\cramped{\mathbb{s}}({\square{{A}}})(x)_{i}

\displaystyle:=0

(if
\textup{stype}(A)_{i}=[0]
)

for every
1\leq i\leq n
.
To construct the map
\square{{A}}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{A}
,
let
{M}

be the unique stratification of
\mathbb{R}^{n}\times{|\Delta[1]|}

so that
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})
contains
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{A}})\sqcup\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({\square{{A}}})
and

\displaystyle\cramped{\mathbb{s}}({{M}})(x,t)

\displaystyle:=\cramped{\mathbb{s}}({{A}})(\tfrac{1}{t}x)

(when
0<t\leq 1
)

\displaystyle\cramped{\mathbb{s}}({{M}})(x,t)

\displaystyle:=\cramped{\mathbb{s}}({\square{{A}}})(x)

Then the projection map
{M}\to\|\Delta[1]\|
with the canonical

n
-framing defines an open
n
-mesh bundle that induces the map

\square{{A}}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{A}
.

Construction 3.5.5.7
.

Let
{C}
be an
n
-mesh cell such that
0\in\textup{Exit}({C})

is terminal and
\operatorname{U}({C})\subset{(-1,1)}^{n}
.
We can then construct a bordism of closed
n
-meshes

{C}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}\square{{C}}
as follows.
We first equip the stratified projection map
\xi^{\prime}:\square{{C}}\times{(0,1]}\to{(0,1]}

with the
n
-framing induced by linear interpolation between the framings of
\square{{C}}
and

{C}
via the framed projection:

\operatorname{fr}(\xi^{\prime})(x,t):=t\operatorname{fr}(\square{{C}})(x)+(1-t)\operatorname{fr}({C})(\operatorname{proj}_{\textup{fr}}({C},x))

Then
\xi^{\prime}
extends to an
n
-framed stratified bundle
\xi:{X}\to\|\Delta[1]\|

which represents the closed
n
-mesh bordism
{C}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}\square{{C}}
.

3.6
Transverse Configurations

Definition 3.6.0.1
.

Let
{B}
be a stratified space and
(\xi,f)
a pair consisting of a
closed
1
-mesh bundle
\xi:{X}\to{B}
together with an
open
1
-mesh bundle
f:{M}\to{B}
.
The pair
(\xi,f)
is a
transverse configuration of
1
-meshes

when every point
e\in{X}\cap{M}

is singular in at most one of
{X}
and
{M}
.
In this case we write
\xi\pitchfork f
.

Example 3.6.0.2
.

The following is a transverse configuration of an open
1
-mesh
{M}
and a closed
1
-mesh
{X}
.
By convention we will always render the open mesh in black and the closed mesh in red.

{M}
{X}

We can interpret the singular strata of the closed mesh
{X}
as parentheses
which collect the the singular strata of the open mesh
{M}
into groups:

(
)(
)(
)

We have that
\textup{sing}({X})=[3]
is the finite ordinal with one element
for each singular stratum of
{X}
. Dually we have
\textup{reg}({M})=[4]

corresponding to the regular strata of
{M}
.
We number the singular and regular strata of
{X}
and
{M}
, respectively:

{M}
{X}
0
1
2
3
4
0
1
2
3

A singular stratum of
{X}
contains a single point
x\in{X}
.
Transversality then guarantees that
x
is contained in a regular stratum of
{M}
.
The transverse configuration
({X},{M})
induces an order-preserving
map
\alpha:\textup{sing}({X})\to\textup{reg}({M})
which sends the index of a singular stratum
of
{X}
to the index of the regular stratum of
{M}
that contains its point.
In our example, this is the map
\alpha=\langle 1,3,3,4\rangle
.

Definition 3.6.0.3
.

Let
{B}
be a stratified space and
(\xi,f)
a pair consisting of a
closed
n
-mesh bundle
\xi:{X}_{n}\to{B}
together with an
open
n
-mesh bundle
f:{M}_{n}\to{B}
.
We write
\xi
and
f
as a composite of
1
-mesh bundles

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\xi:{X}_{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{n-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cdots}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{0}={B}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{f:{M}_{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}_{n-1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cdots}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}_{0}={B}}}

The pair
(\xi,f)
is a
transverse configuration of
n
-meshes

when every point

e\in{X}_{i}\cap{M}_{i}

is singular in at most one of
{X}_{i}
and
{M}_{i}

for every
1\leq i\leq n
.
In this case we write
\xi\pitchfork f
.

Example 3.6.0.4
.

This is an example of a transverse configuration of a closed
2
-mesh
{X}
,
by convention drawn in red, and an open
2
-mesh
{M}
, drawn in black:

The closed mesh
{X}
can be thought of as generalised higher-dimensional
parentheses which are placed around the elements of the open mesh
{M}
.

Example 3.6.0.5
.

We illustrate a few examples of pairs of
2
-meshes which do
not
form
transverse configurations.

In this section we show that every transverse configuration of
n
-meshes

{X}\pitchfork{M}
determines a bordism of open
n
-trusses
between the truss nerves

\textup{N}_{\bar{\textup{T}}}({X})^{\dagger}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}\textup{N}_{\dot{\textup{T}}}({M})

and, conversely, that every open
n
-truss bordism arises in this way.
Moreover, the bordism of open
n
-trusses arising from a transverse configuration

{X}\pitchfork{M}
is natural in both
{X}
and
{M}
.
This is realised by constructing a quasicategory
\textup{Conf}^{n}
which classifies
transverse configurations of
n
-meshes, and then demonstrating that it is
equivalent to the twisted arrow category
\operatorname{Tw}(\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n})
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{Tw}(\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}\times\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{n}\times\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}

3.6.1
Classifying Category for Transverse Configurations

Lemma 3.6.1.1
.

Let
(\xi,f)
be a transverse configuration of
n
-mesh bundles over
a stratified space
{B}
.
When
\varphi:{A}\to{B}
is a map of stratified spaces, then
the pulled back
n
-mesh bundles
(\varphi^{*}\xi,\varphi^{*}f)

form a transverse configuration of
n
-mesh bundles over
{A}
.

Definition 3.6.1.2
.

We let
\textup{Conf}^{n}
denote the simplicial set whose
k
-simplices
consist of a transverse configuration
(\xi,f)
of a closed

n
-mesh bundle
\xi
and an open
n
-mesh bundle
f
over
the stratified
k
-simplex
\|\Delta[k]\|
.
An order-preserving map
[k^{\prime}]\to[k]
acts via pullback
of
\xi
and
f
along the induced map
\|\Delta[k^{\prime}]\|\to\|\Delta[k]\|
.

Observation 3.6.1.3
.

A
k
-simplex of
\textup{Conf}^{0}
is a transverse configuration of
a closed
0
-mesh bundle
\xi:{X}\to\|\Delta[k]\|
and an open

0
-mesh bundle
f:{M}\to\|\Delta[k]\|
.
Both
\xi
and
f
are the identity map on
\|\Delta[k]\|
.
Therefore
\textup{Conf}^{0}\cong*
.

3.6.1.4
.

A
k
-simplex of
\textup{Conf}^{n}
contains both a closed an an open
n
-mesh
bundle over the stratified
k
-simplex
\|\Delta[k]\|
.
These mesh bundles individually represent a
k
-simplex of

\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
and
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
respectively.
We therefore have projection maps

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\xi}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{(\xi,f)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{f}}

Lemma 3.6.1.5
.

The projection map
\textup{Conf}^{n}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}

is a cocartesian fibration
so that a map is cocartesian
when it is sent to an equivalence
by the other projection

\textup{Conf}^{n}\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.
In particular
\textup{Conf}^{n}
is a quasicategory.
Moreover the dual claim holds for

\textup{Conf}^{n}\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.

Proof.

We prove the claim for the projection onto the closed
n
-mesh bundle;
the other part follows similarly.
Suppose that we have a lifting problem

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Lambda^{i}[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\tau}

(3.16)

Unpacking the definitions, we are given transverse configuration

(\xi^{\prime},f^{\prime})
of
n
-mesh bundles over
\|\Lambda^{i}[k]\|
as well as a
closed
n
-mesh bundle
\xi
over
\|\Delta[k]\|
so that

\xi
restricts to
\xi^{\prime}
.
The open
n
-mesh bundle
f^{\prime}
classifies a horn in
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Lambda^{i}[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}

(3.17)

We can find a lift for (
3.17
)
in the following cases since
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is a quasicategory:

1.

0<i<k
.

2.

k=1
and
i=0
. We can pick the filler to be an equivalence.

3.

k\geq 1
and the first edge of
\Lambda^{i}[k]\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is an equivalence.

A solution to the lifting problem (
3.17
)
classifies an open
n
-mesh bundle
f
over
\|\Delta[k]\|
which extends
f^{\prime}
.
The pair
(\xi,f)
is not a transverse configuration in general;
however there must exist a small open neighbourhood

\|\Lambda^{i}[k]\|\subset{U}\subset\|\Delta[k]\|

such that
\xi
and
f
are transverse after being restricted to
{U}
.
Using the trivialisation of
\xi
over the interior,
we can then adjust
f
to an open
n
-mesh bundle
\hat{f}

over
\|\Delta[k]\|
which agrees with
f
over
{U}
and
is transverse to
\xi
.
The pair
(\xi,\hat{f})
is a solution to the lifting problem.
∎

Remark 3.6.1.6
.

As a simplicial set
\textup{Conf}^{n}
is a subobject of the product

\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}\times\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.
However the inclusion map

\textup{Conf}^{n}\hookrightarrow\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}\times\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}

is
not
an inner fibration so we can not see
\textup{Conf}^{n}
as a subcategory of the product.

Construction 3.6.1.7
.

Suppose that
(\xi,f)
is a transverse configuration of

n
-mesh bundles over a stratified space
{B}
.
Individually, we have classifying maps

{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}:\textup{Exit}({B})\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}\qquad{\llbracket f\rrbracket}:\textup{Exit}({B})\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}

Since by Lemma
3.6.1.1
transversality is preserved by pullbacks, the map

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})\times\textup{Exit}({B})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}\times\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket}\times{\llbracket f\rrbracket}}

factors through
\textup{Conf}^{n}
. This defines the
classifying map

{\llbracket\xi,f\rrbracket}:\textup{Exit}({B})\longrightarrow\textup{Conf}^{n}.

Proposition 3.6.1.8
.

Let
{B}
be a triangulable stratified space and
I:{A}\hookrightarrow{B}
a closed triangulable subspace.
Suppose that
\varphi:\textup{Exit}({B})\to\textup{Conf}^{n}
is a map and

\xi^{\prime}\pitchfork f^{\prime}
a transverse configuration of
n
-mesh bundles over

{A}
such that
{\llbracket\xi^{\prime},f^{\prime}\rrbracket}=\varphi\circ\textup{Exit}(I)
.
Then there exists a transverse configuration
\xi\pitchfork f
of
n
-mesh bundles
over
{B}
together with an equivalence
\varphi\simeq{\llbracket\xi,f\rrbracket}

relative to
{\llbracket\xi^{\prime},f^{\prime}\rrbracket}
.

Proof.

It suffices to address the case where
I=\|i\|^{+}
for an inclusion
of marked simplicial sets
i:R\hookrightarrow S
.
We define maps
\bar{\varphi}
and
\dot{\varphi}
from
\varphi
via

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\dot{\varphi}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\varphi}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi}

Then Lemma
3.2.2.10
produces a unique
closed
n
-mesh bundle
\xi
over
\|S\|^{+}
which makes the following diagram commute:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}^{+}(\|R\|^{+})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}^{+}(\|S\|^{+})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces R}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces S}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n})^{\natural}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n})^{\natural}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\eta_{R}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\eta_{S}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{\varphi}\circ\eta_{S}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textup{Exit}^{+}(I)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi^{\prime}\rrbracket^{+}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi\rrbracket^{+}}}

Similarly via the map
\dot{\varphi}
there is a unique open
n
-mesh bundle

f
over
\|B\|^{+}
which fits the analogous diagram.
For any marked flag
\sigma
of
B
the bundles
\xi
and
f
restrict to

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}_{\sigma}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|(\Delta[k],T)\|^{+}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|S\|^{+}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi_{\sigma}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}_{\sigma}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|(\Delta[k],T)\|^{+}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|S\|^{+}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{\sigma}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}

where
\xi_{\sigma}
and
f_{\sigma}
are the
n
-mesh bundles represented by

\bar{\varphi}\circ\sigma
and
\dot{\varphi}\circ\sigma
.
Since
\bar{\varphi}
and
\dot{\varphi}
together arise from
\varphi
,
which classifies a transverse configuration, we have
\xi_{\sigma}\pitchfork f_{\sigma}
.
Because this holds for all marked flags of
S
, we have
\xi\pitchfork f
.

Now both
{\llbracket\xi,f\rrbracket}
and
\varphi
are solutions to the lifting problem

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}^{+}(\|R\|^{+})\sqcup_{R}S}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{1})^{\natural}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}^{+}(\|S\|^{+})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}

Therefore there exists an equivalence
{\llbracket\xi,f\rrbracket}\simeq\varphi

relative to
{\llbracket\xi^{\prime},f^{\prime}\rrbracket}
.
∎

3.6.2
Attaching Labels to Transverse Configurations

Construction 3.6.2.1
.

Suppose that
\xi\pitchfork f
is a transverse configuration of a closed
n
-mesh bundle

\xi:{X}\to{B}

and an open
n
-mesh bundle

f:{M}\to{B}
.
Via the maps induced by the framing, we define the intersection
{X}\cap{M}

as the pullback of stratified spaces

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}\cap{M}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\operatorname{U}({B})}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}

The underlying unstratified space
\operatorname{U}({X}\cap{M})
is
isomorphic to
{X}
, but the stratification of
{X}\cap{M}

is finer than that of
{X}
.
We let
\xi\cap f:{X}\cap{M}
denote the induced
n
-framed stratified bundle which fits into the diagrams

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}\cap{M}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi\cap f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}\cap{M}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi\cap f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}

The
n
-framed stratified bundle
\xi\cap f:{X}\cap{M}\to{B}

then is a closed
n
-mesh bundle refining
\xi
.
A section
s:{B}\to{X}\cap{M}
of
\xi\cap f

simultaneously determines
a section of
\xi
and
f
; conversely any pair of sections of
\xi
and
f

that agree in framing coordinates arises from a section of the closed
n
-mesh bundle
\xi\cap f
.

Definition 3.6.2.2
.

A labelling of a transverse configuration
\xi\pitchfork f
of
a closed
n
-mesh

\xi:{X}\to{B}
and an open
n
-mesh

f:{M}\to{B}

with a simplicial set of labels
X

consists of maps
(L_{0},L,L_{1})
which together fit into the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X}\cap{M})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({M})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{X^{\textup{op}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{Tw}(X)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{X}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{1}}

Observation 3.6.2.3
.

In the situation of Definition
3.6.2.2
,
the map
L_{0}
determines a labelling of the closed
n
-mesh
\xi

in
X^{\textup{op}}
while the map
L_{1}
is a labelling of the open
n
-mesh in
X
.
The map
L
assigns to every point
x\in{X}\cap{M}

that is common to both meshes a map
L_{0}(x)\to L_{1}(x)
in
X
.
This assignment is functorial in
x
in that an exit path in
{X}\cap{M}

acts contravariantly on the domain and covariantly on the codomain.
This twist in the direction of the labelling is consistent with
the duality equivalence

\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C}^{\textup{op}})\simeq(\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C}))^{\textup{op}}
.

In §
3.2.3
we defined the simplicial set
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}(X)

of closed
n
-mesh bundles with labels in some simplicial set
X
as a polynomial functor.
This polynomial functor was induced by a forgetful map

\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{M}}}^{n}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}

from the simplicial set
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}
that classifies closed
n
-mesh bundles that are additionally equipped with a section.
While we do not expect that we can define a simplicial set
\textup{Conf}^{n}(X)
classifying transverse configurations of
n
-meshes with labels in
X
as a polynomial functor directly, we rely on a similar idea.
We define three different polynomial functors, based on transverse configurations

\xi\pitchfork f
equipped with sections of
\xi
,
\xi\cap f
and
f
, respectively.

Definition 3.6.2.4
.

We let
\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{LR}}
denote the simplicial set whose
k
-simplices
consist of a transverse configuration
\xi\pitchfork f
of a closed

n
-mesh bundle
\xi
and an open
n
-mesh bundle
f
over
the stratified
k
-simplex
\|\Delta[k]\|

together with a section
s

of
\xi\cap f:{X}\cap{M}\to\|\Delta[k]\|
.
An order-preserving map
[k^{\prime}]\to[k]
acts via pullback
of
\xi
and
f
along the induced map
\|\Delta[k^{\prime}]\|\to\|\Delta[k]\|

and adjusts the section accordingly.

3.6.2.5
.

We get a family of projection maps which together fit into the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{LR}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{M}}}^{n}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathfrak{C}\textup{onf}^{n}_{\textup{LR}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\dot{\mathfrak{M}}}^{n}}

The left and right squares then factor through the pullbacks:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{L}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{LR}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{R}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{M}}}^{n}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathfrak{C}\textup{onf}^{n}_{\textup{L}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\llcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathfrak{C}\textup{onf}^{n}_{\textup{LR}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathfrak{C}\textup{onf}^{n}_{\textup{R}}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\dot{\mathfrak{M}}}^{n}}

(3.18)

Unwrapping the definitions, a
k
-simplex of the simplicial set

\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{L}}
is a transverse configuration
of
k
-mesh bundles over
\|\Delta[k]\|
together with a section of the closed
n
-mesh bundle. The map
\mathfrak{C}\textup{onf}^{n}_{\textup{L}}:\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{L}}\to\textup{Conf}^{n}
forgets the section.
Analogously, a
k
-simplex of
\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{R}}
is a transverse configuration with a section
of the open
n
-mesh bundle with
\mathfrak{C}\textup{onf}^{n}_{\textup{R}}:\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{R}}\to\textup{Conf}^{n}
forgetting the section.

Observation 3.6.2.6
.

When
\xi\pitchfork f
is a transverse configuration of
n
-mesh bundles
over the same stratified space
{B}
,
the intersection
\xi\cap f
is a closed
n
-mesh bundle over
{B}

and so by Lemma
3.2.2.4

the forgetful map
\mathfrak{C}\textup{onf}^{n}_{\textup{LR}}:\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{LR}}\to\textup{Conf}^{n}
is a categorical fibration.
Since the maps
\cramped{\bar{\mathfrak{M}}}^{n}:\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
and

\cramped{\dot{\mathfrak{M}}}^{n}:\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}_{*}\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
are categorical fibrations,
so are the maps
\mathfrak{C}\textup{onf}^{n}_{\textup{L}}:\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{L}}\to\textup{Conf}^{n}
and

\mathfrak{C}\textup{onf}^{n}_{\textup{R}}:\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{R}}\to\textup{Conf}^{n}
defined by the pullbacks.

Lemma 3.6.2.7
.

Let
\xi\pitchfork f
be a transverse configuration of a closed
n
-mesh bundle

\xi:{X}\to{B}
and an open

-mesh bundle

. Then there are pullback squares of simplicial sets

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi_{*}}

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces(\xi\cap f)_{*}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}

Proof.

Analogous to the proof of Lemma
3.2.3.5
.
∎

Construction 3.6.2.8
.

The maps

,

and

define polynomial

\displaystyle\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{L}}(-)

\displaystyle:\textup{sSet}\to\textup{sSet}

\displaystyle:\textup{sSet}\to\textup{sSet}

\displaystyle\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{R}}(-)

\displaystyle:\textup{sSet}\to\textup{sSet}

Moreover Construction

defines natural transformations

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}}}

Lemma 3.6.2.9
.

Let
\xi\pitchfork f
be a transverse configuration of
n
-mesh bundles

\xi:{X}\to{B}
and
f:{M}\to{B}

and let
C
be a simplicial set. We then have:

1.

There is a bijection between the set of maps of simplicial sets

\textup{Exit}({X})\to C

and the set of lifts in the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{L}}(C)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi,f\rrbracket}}

2.

There is a bijection between the set of maps of simplicial sets

\textup{Exit}({X}\cap{M})\to C

and the set of lifts in the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{LR}}(C)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi,f\rrbracket}}

There is a bijection between the set of maps of simplicial sets

\textup{Exit}({M})\to C

and the set of lifts in the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{R}}(C)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi,f\rrbracket}}

Proof.

3.6.2.7
.
∎

Definition 3.6.2.10
.

When
C
is a simplicial set, we write
\textup{Conf}^{n}(C)

for the limit of the following diagram of simplicial sets:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{L}}(C^{\textup{op}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{LR}}(C^{\textup{op}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{LR}}(\operatorname{Tw}(C))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{LR}}(C)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{R}}(C)}}

(3.19)

The two maps on the inside are induced via functoriality by the forgetful
maps
\operatorname{Tw}(C)\to C^{\textup{op}}
and
\operatorname{Tw}(C)\to C
that send a twisted arrow to its
domain and codomain. The two outer maps are the components at
C^{\textup{op}}
and
C

of the natural transformations

\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{LR}}(-)\to\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{L}}(-)
and

\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{LR}}(-)\to\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\textup{R}}(-)
, respectively.
By naturality of the limit this defines a functor

\textup{Conf}^{n}(-):\textup{sSet}\to\textup{sSet}
together with a natural transformation

\textup{Conf}^{n}(-)\to\textup{Conf}^{n}
.

Observation 3.6.2.11
.

Similar to Observation
3.2.3.3
we have

\textup{Conf}^{0}_{\textup{L}}\cong\textup{Conf}^{0}_{\textup{LR}}\cong\textup{Conf}^{0}_{\textup{R}}\cong*.

Therefore for any simplicial set
C
we have natural isomorphisms of
simplicial sets

\textup{Conf}^{0}_{\textup{L}}(C)\cong\textup{Conf}^{0}_{\textup{LR}}(C)\cong\textup{Conf}^{0}_{\textup{R}}(C)\cong C

Then the diagram (
3.19
) specialises to

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{0}_{\textup{L}}(C^{\textup{op}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{0}_{\textup{LR}}(C^{\textup{op}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{0}_{\textup{LR}}(\operatorname{Tw}(C))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{0}_{\textup{LR}}(C)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{0}_{\textup{R}}(C)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{C^{\textup{op}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{C^{\textup{op}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{Tw}(C)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{C}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{C}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}

Hence we have a natural isomorphism
\textup{Conf}^{0}(C)\cong\operatorname{Tw}(C)
.

Observation 3.6.2.12
.

Suppose that
\xi\pitchfork f
is a transverse configuration of
n
-mesh bundles

\xi:{X}\to{B}
and

.
Let
C
be any simplicial set.
Via the characterisation of lifts from Lemma
3.6.2.9
,
we see that a lift in the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}(C)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({B})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\llbracket\xi,f\rrbracket}}

corresponds exactly to a diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({X}\cap{M})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Exit}({M})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{C^{\textup{op}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{Tw}(C)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{C}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{0}^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{1}^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{1}}

The five maps
L_{0}
,

,

,

and

are each induced by one
of the five simplicial sets in the limit diagram (

)
which defines

.
Therefore the simplicial set
\textup{Conf}^{n}(C)
classifies transverse configurations
of
n
-meshes with labels in
