\square{{X}}=\square_{1}{{X}}\end{gathered}

Lemma 4.2.5.7
.

Let
{X}
be an
n
-cell and
\varepsilon>0
.
Then there exists a
0<t\leq 1
so that

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\square_{t}{{X}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\partial{X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\partial\square_{t}{{X}})}}

restricts along the natural inclusion
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n,\varepsilon}(-)\hookrightarrow\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(-)

to a pullback square of simplicial sets

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n,\varepsilon}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n,\varepsilon}(\square_{t}{{X}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n,\varepsilon}(\partial{X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n,\varepsilon}(\partial\square_{t}{{X}})}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}

Proof.

The bordism of closed
n
-meshes
{X}\to\square{{X}}
is represented
by the closed
n
-mesh bundle
\square_{\bullet}{{X}}\to\|\Delta[1]\|
.
The fibre
\square_{t}{{X}}
over any
0<t\leq 1
is framed isomorphic to
\square{{X}}
,
but as
t\to 0
it converges to the shape of
{X}
.
In particular there must be a
0<t\leq 1
such that

\operatorname{U}(\partial{X})\subseteq\{e\mid\exists x\in\partial\square_{t}{{X}}.\ \|e-x\|_{\infty}<\varepsilon\}.

Then the square must be a pullback square due to
\varepsilon
-orthogonality.
∎

Lemma 4.2.5.8
.

Let
{X}
be an
n
-cell.
Then
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}({X})\to\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\partial{X})
is a Kan fibration.

Proof.

By Lemma
4.2.5.7
for any
\varepsilon>0
there exists a
t>0
such that
we have a diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n,\varepsilon}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n,\varepsilon}(\square_{t}{{X}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\square_{t}{{X}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\square{{X}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n,\varepsilon}(\partial{X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n,\varepsilon}(\partial\square_{t}{{X}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\partial\square_{t}{{X}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\partial\square{{X}})}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}

where the first square is a pullback square, the second a retract and the third an isomorphism of maps.
By Lemma
4.2.5.5
the map on the right
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\square{{X}})\to\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\partial\square{{X}})

is a Kan fibration, and therefore so is the map on the left

\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n,\varepsilon}({X})\to\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n,\varepsilon}(\partial{X})
.
Since Kan fibrations are closed under filtered colimits, it follows that

\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}({X})\to\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\partial{X})

is a Kan fibration.
∎

Lemma 4.2.5.9
.

Let
{X}
be a closed
n
-mesh and let

U:\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})^{\textup{op},\triangleleft}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}

be its cellular covering diagram.
Then the diagram
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(U(-)):\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})^{\textup{op},\triangleleft}\to\textup{sSet}

induces a limit diagram of spaces.
In particular the functor
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(-):\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}\to\textup{S}
satisfies the Segal condition.

Proof.

Every closed
n
-mesh is essentially tame, and so up
to equivalence we can ensure that
{X}
and each of its
cells is tame.
For every tame closed
n
-mesh
{Y}
we have a deformation retract

\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{tame}}^{n}({Y})
of
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}({Y})
consisting
only of those
n
-manifold diagrams on
{Y}
that are tame as

n
-framed stratified spaces.
It therefore suffices to show that
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{tame}}^{n}(U(-))
induces a limit
diagram of spaces.
By gluing together the
n
-manifold diagrams on the cells of
{X}
,
the diagram
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{tame}}^{n}(U(-))
is a limit diagram of simplicial sets.
Kan fibrations are closed under retract, and so
by Lemma
4.2.5.8
the diagram is Reedy fibrant.
Therefore, the limit diagram of simplicial sets
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{tame}}^{n}(U(-))

represents a limit diagram of spaces.
∎

Lemma 4.2.5.10
.

Let
{X}
be an
n
-cell. Then

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\square{{X}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\partial{X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\partial\square{{X}})}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}

is a pullback square of spaces.
In particular the functor
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(-):\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}\to\textup{S}
satisfies the regularity condition.

Proof.

This follows from Lemma
4.2.5.7

and Observation
4.2.3.9
.
∎

4.2.6
Extended Manifold Diagrams

An
n
-manifold diagram on a closed
n
-mesh
{X}
is defined within an arbitrary small open neighbourhood of
{X}
.
Extended
n
-manifold diagrams
{M}
on
{X}
are an alternative presentation
for which we require
{M}
to be defined everywhere on
\mathbb{R}^{n}
.
Extended
n
-manifold diagrams organise into an
n
-diagrammatic space

\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(-):\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}\to\textup{S}
that is equivalent to
the
n
-diagrammatic space of
n
-manifold diagrams
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(-)
.

Definition 4.2.6.1
.

We write
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}
for the simplicial set of
extended
n
-manifold diagrams

whose
k
-simplices consist
of a pair
(\xi,p)
where
\xi:{X}\to\|\Delta[k]\|
is a closed

n
-mesh bundle and
p:{E}\to{|\Delta[k]|}
is an
n
-manifold diagram
bundle orthogonal to
\xi
such that

\operatorname{U}({E})=\mathbb{R}^{n}\times{|\Delta[k]|}
.
There is a projection map
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
which sends
a pair
(\xi,p)
to the closed
n
-mesh bundle
\xi
.

Proposition 4.2.6.2
.

The map
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is a left fibration.

Proof.

The proof is analogous to that of Proposition
4.2.4.3
,
except that this time we do not take equivalence classes.
∎

Observation 4.2.6.3
.

Since
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is a left fibration it induces a
functor of
\infty
-categories

\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(-):\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}\longrightarrow\textup{S}.

The space
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}({X})
for any closed
n
-mesh
{X}
is presented
as a Kan complex via the pullback of simplicial sets

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[0]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{X}}

In particular a
k
-simplex of
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}({X})
is an

n
-manifold diagram bundle
p:{E}\to{|\Delta[k]|}
with

\operatorname{U}({E})=\mathbb{R}^{n}\times{|\Delta[k]|}

that is fibrewise orthogonal to
{X}
.

Example 4.2.6.4
.

An extended
2
-manifold diagram on the
2
-cube
\mathbb{I}^{2}
resembles a string diagram
but can have non-trivial geometry outside the bounds of
\mathbb{I}^{2}
:

Up to isotopy the diagram is fully determined by its intersection with
\mathbb{I}^{2}
.
To see this we first move the parts of the string diagram that are above

\mathbb{I}^{2}
to infinity and off the top of the diagram, using that
\mathbb{R}^{2}
is open:

The closed
n
-mesh changes while the diagram itself remains untouched.
However, we can still interpret this as a restriction of the string diagram
to the subcell.
While the rest of the string diagram is still there, it is now no longer
contained within the closed
2
-mesh, and we are therefore free to move it aside,
as we did in Example
4.2.6.4
.

Example 4.2.6.6
.

Even when the closed
n
-mesh
{X}
has more exotic shapes, we can
move aside the parts of the diagram that are not contained within
{X}
.

Observation 4.2.6.7
.

There is a map of simplicial sets
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}\to\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}

which restricts extended
n
-manifold diagrams to an open neighbourhood around
the closed
n
-mesh.
This map commutes with the projections onto
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
and therefore
induces a natural transformation
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(-)\to\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(-)
of
functors
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}\to\textup{S}
.

Proposition 4.2.6.8
.

The natural transformation
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(-)\to\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(-)
is an equivalence
of functors
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}\to\textup{S}
.
In particular
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(-)
is an
n
-diagrammatic space.

Proof.

This follows directly from Lemma
4.2.6.11
below.
∎

We first demonstrate the equivalence between extended and non-extended
n
-manifold
diagrams on the closed
n
-cube
\mathbb{I}^{n}
.

Lemma 4.2.6.9
.

The map
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(\mathbb{I}^{n})\to\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\mathbb{I}^{n})
is a trivial fibration.

Proof.

Suppose we have a lifting problem

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(\mathbb{I}^{n})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\mathbb{I}^{n})}}

Unpacking the given data and choosing representatives, we have an
\varepsilon>0

and an
n
-manifold diagram bundle
f_{0}:{E}_{0}\to{|\Delta[k]|}
that
is fibrewise
\varepsilon
-orthogonal to
\mathbb{I}^{n}
and defined on

\operatorname{U}({E}_{0})=\{(e,b)\mid\|e\|_{\infty}<1+\varepsilon\}\cup(\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\partial{|\Delta[k]|})\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n}\times{|\Delta[k]|}.

Let
N:\partial{|\Delta[k]|}\times{[0,1)}\hookrightarrow{|\Delta[k]|}

be a collar neighbourhood of the boundary
\partial{|\Delta[k]|}
.
We then define a continuous function
P:\mathbb{R}^{n}\times{|\Delta[k]|}\to\mathbb{R}^{n}
as follows:

\displaystyle P(e,b)

\displaystyle:=(1-t)e+t\|e\|_{\infty}^{-1}e

(when
\|e\|_{\infty}>1
and
N(b^{\prime},t)=b
)

\displaystyle P(e,b)

\displaystyle:=\|e\|_{\infty}^{-1}e

(when
\|e\|_{\infty}>1
and
b\not\in\textup{im}(N)
)

\displaystyle P(e,b)

\displaystyle:=e

(when
\|e\|_{\infty}\leq 1
)

In particular we have
P(e,b)=e
whenever
b\in\partial{|\Delta[k]|}
.
We let
{E}_{1}
be the stratification of
\mathbb{R}^{n}\times{|\Delta[k]|}

such that

\cramped{\mathbb{s}}({{E}_{1}})(e,b)=\cramped{\mathbb{s}}({{E}_{0}})(P(e,b),b)
.
Then the projection
f_{1}:{E}_{1}\to{|\Delta[k]|}
is an
n
-manifold diagram bundle
that extends
f_{0}
and is fibrewise orthogonal to
\mathbb{I}^{n}
.
∎

Construction 4.2.6.10
.

Let
\xi:{X}\to{B}
be a closed
n
-mesh bundle.
The
m
-fold cylinder
of
\xi
is the closed
(n+m)
-mesh bundle

\textup{C}^{m}(\xi):\mathbb{I}^{m}\times{X}\to{B}

that arises as the stacked product (see Definition
3.2.6.1
)
of
\xi
followed by the closed
m
-mesh bundle
\mathbb{I}^{m}\to\|\Delta[0]\|
.

Lemma 4.2.6.11
.

The map
\operatorname{core}(\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n})\to\operatorname{core}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n})
is a trivial fibration.

Proof.

We need to show that every lifting problem of the form

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{core}(\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{core}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n})}}

has a solution.
We do this by induction on
n,m\geq 0
such that
0\leq n\leq m

for the cases where the closed
n
-mesh bundle induced by the
k
-simplex

\Delta[k]\to\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n,\simeq}
is framed isomorphic to
the
m
-fold cylinder
\textup{C}^{m}(\xi)
of a closed
(n-m)
-mesh bundle over
{|\Delta[k]|}
.

The case
n=0
is trivial and the case that
n=m
follows from Lemma
4.2.6.9
.
Therefore, for now we assume that
0\leq m<n
.
Unpacking the definitions and making convenient choices of representatives
the lifting problem provides the following data:
We are given a closed
(n-m-1)
-mesh bundle

\xi:{X}\to{Y}

and a closed
1
-mesh bundle

\zeta:{Y}\to{|\Delta[k]|}
.
Without loss of generality we can assume that the closed
n
-mesh bundle
is equal and not just framed isomorphic to the
m
-fold cylinder

\textup{C}^{m}(\zeta\circ\xi):\mathbb{I}^{m}\times{X}\to{|\Delta[k]|}
.

Let
s+1
be the number of singular strata of
{Y}
and for every
i\in[s]
let
h_{i}:{|\Delta[k]|}\to\mathbb{R}
be the height function of the
i
th singular stratum.
We further have an
\varepsilon>0
and an
n
-manifold diagram bundle

f_{0}:{E}_{0}\to{|\Delta[k]|}

which is
2\varepsilon
-orthogonal to the closed
n
-mesh bundle
\textup{C}^{m}(\zeta\circ\xi):\mathbb{I}^{m}\times{X}\to{|\Delta[k]|}
and defined on

\operatorname{U}({E}_{0})=\{(e,b)\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\times{|\Delta[k]|}\mid\exists x\in\mathbb{I}^{m}\times{X}.\ \|e-x\|_{\infty}<\varepsilon\}\cup(\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\partial{|\Delta[k]|})

Shrinking
{E}_{0}
if necessary we also ensure that
4\varepsilon<h_{i+1}(b)-h_{i}(b)
for all
i\in[s]
with
i<s
and
b\in{|\Delta[k]|}
.
We then gradually extend
f_{0}
as follows.

1.

We extend
f_{0}
in a neighbourhood around the singular slices of
{Y}
.
Let
i\in[s]
be the index of a singular slice and

\sigma_{i}:{S}_{i}\to{|\Delta[k]|}
be the closed
(n-m-1)
-mesh bundle obtained via the pullback

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{S}_{i}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{|\Delta[k]|}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces h_{i}}

Moreover we let
{D}_{i}
be the stratified subspace of
{E}_{0}

given by

{D}_{i}:={E}_{0}\cap\{(e_{1},\ldots,e_{n},b)\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\times{|\Delta[k]|}\mid e_{n-m}=h_{i}(b)\}

We interpret
\operatorname{U}({D}_{i})
as a subspace of
\mathbb{R}^{n-1}\times{|\Delta[k]|}
,
such that the projection map
g_{i}:{D}_{i}\to{|\Delta[k]|}
is an

(n-1)
-manifold diagram bundle that is fibrewise
2\varepsilon
-orthogonal to
the closed
(n-1)
-mesh bundle
\textup{C}^{m}(\sigma_{i})
.
Then
g_{i}
induces a lifting problem

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{core}(\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n-1})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{core}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n-1})}}

which by induction on
n
has a solution.
By assembling these solutions for all singular slices
i\in[s]

and using orthogonality of
f_{0}
and
\textup{C}^{m}(\zeta\circ\xi)

we can extend
f_{0}
to an
n
-manifold diagram bundle

f_{1}:{E}_{1}\to{|\Delta[k]|}
that is defined within a neighbourhood
of the singular slices of
{X}
:

\operatorname{U}({E}_{1})=\operatorname{U}({E}_{0})\cup\{(e_{1},\ldots,e_{n},b)\mid\exists i\in[s].\ |e_{n-m}-h_{i}(b)|<\varepsilon_{0}\}

2.

We now extend
f_{1}
between the singular slices, but leaving a gap to the extension around the singular slices.
Let
i\in[s]
be the index of a singular slice of
{Y}
such that
i<s
. We define a stratified space
{B}_{i}
whose underlying space is

\operatorname{U}({B}_{i}):=\{(t,b)\in{Y}\mid h_{i}(b)+2\varepsilon\leq t\leq h_{i+1}(b)-2\varepsilon\}\subseteq\operatorname{U}({Y})

and whose three strata are the subspaces where one or none of the inequalities is tight.
There is a canonical map
{B}_{i}\to{Y}
which is the inclusion on the underlying topological spaces.
We construct a closed
(n-m-1)
-mesh bundle
\rho_{i}
via the pullback
along this map:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{R}_{i}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{X}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{i}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{Y}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\rho_{i}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi}

We note that the projection map
\beta_{i}:{B}_{i}\to{|\Delta[k]|}
is a closed
1
-mesh bundle and isomorphic as such to the projection
\mathbb{I}\times{|\Delta[k]|}\to{|\Delta[k]|}
.
We therefore have that the
m
-fold cylinder
\textup{C}^{m}(\beta_{i}\circ\rho_{i})
is isomorphic as an
n
-framed stratified bundle to the
(m+1)
-fold cylinder
\textup{C}^{m+1}(\rho_{i})
.

We let
{D}_{i}
be the stratified subspace of
{E}_{1}
such that

\operatorname{U}({D}_{i})=\{(e_{1},\ldots,e_{n},b)\mid h_{i}(b)+\varepsilon<e_{n-m}<h_{i+1}(b)-\varepsilon\}

and let
g_{i}:{D}_{i}\to{|\Delta[k]|}
denote the projection map.
Then
g_{i}
is
\varepsilon
-orthogonal to the
(m+1)
-fold cylinder

\textup{C}^{m+1}(\rho_{i})
,
defining a lifting problem

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{core}(\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{core}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n})}}

By induction on
m
this lifting problem has a solution.
These solutions for all
i\in[s]
with
i<s

then assemble into an extension

f_{2}:{E}_{2}\to{|\Delta[k]|}
of
f_{1}
defined on

\operatorname{U}({E}_{2})=\operatorname{U}({E}_{1})\cup\{(e_{1},\ldots,e_{n},b)\mid\exists i\in[s].\ i<s\land h_{i}+\varepsilon<e_{n-m}<h_{i+1}-\varepsilon\}

3.

Since
\varepsilon_{0}<\varepsilon
there is an
(\varepsilon-\varepsilon_{0})
-sized gap
between the extensions constructed around the singular slices
in step 1
and the extensions constructed between the singular slices in step 2.
Since
f_{0}
is
2\varepsilon
-orthogonal to
\textup{C}^{m}(\zeta\circ\xi)

we can fill these gaps by solving lifting problems of the form

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[1]\times\partial\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{core}(\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n-1})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[1]\times\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{core}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n-1})}}

It is always possible to find a solution since by induction on
n
the map

\operatorname{core}(\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n-1})\to\operatorname{core}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n-1})
is a trivial fibration.
We therefore have an extension
f_{2}:{E}_{2}\to{|\Delta[k]|}

of
f_{1}
defined on the space

\operatorname{U}({E}_{2})=\operatorname{U}({E}_{1})\cup\{(e_{1},\ldots,e_{n},b)\mid h_{0}-\varepsilon_{0}<e_{n-m}<h_{s}+\varepsilon_{0}\}

4.

Finally, it suffices to extend the diagram above the largest singular height

h_{m}
and below the smallest singular height
h_{0}
.
This can be done analogously as in the proof of Lemma
4.2.6.11
.∎

4.3
Combinatorial Manifold Diagrams

Meshes are designed to bridge between geometric and combinatorial descriptions of framed stratified spaces.
Any extended
n
-manifold diagram is essentially tame, and therefore can be refined by an open
n
-mesh with labels
in
[n]
.
In this section we show how to use this in order to derive a combinatorial description
of the
n
-diagrammatic space of
n
-manifold diagrams
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(-)
.
In particular, we define functors
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(-)
and
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{T}}^{n}(-)
based on
open
n
-meshes and trusses that present
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(-)
by taking classifying spaces:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{T}}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
Cat
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Cat}_{\infty}}}
S
S
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{T}}^{n}(-)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(-)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(-)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(-)}
k

In §
4.3.1
we characterise those open
n
-mesh bundles
that refine
n
-manifold diagram bundles and show that they form an
\infty
-subcategory

\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
of
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}{[n]}
.
Via orthogonal configurations between these diagrammatic
n
-mesh bundles and
closed
n
-mesh bundles, we then introduce the functor
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(-)

in §
4.3.2
classifying extended meshed
n
-manifold diagrams.
For every closed
n
-mesh
{X}
the space
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}({X})

is the classifying space
\textup{k}(\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X}))
.
Finally, in §
4.3.3
we use the equivalence
\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\perp}\simeq\operatorname{Tw}(\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n})

between orthogonal configurations of
n
-meshes and the twisted arrow category
from §
3.6.5
to define the functor
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{T}}^{n}(-)
.

4.3.1
Diagrammatic Meshes

Definition 4.3.1.1
.

Suppose that
{M}
is an open
n
-mesh with labels in
[n]
.
We say that
{M}
is a
diagrammatic
n
-mesh
when there exists
an extended
n
-manifold diagram
{E}
and a refinement map of labelled
n
-framed stratified
spaces
r:{M}\to{E}
.

Definition 4.3.1.2
.

Suppose that
f:{M}\to{B}
is an open
n
-mesh bundle
with labels in
[n]
.
We say that
f
is a
diagrammatic
n
-mesh bundle
when there
exists an
n
-manifold diagram bundle
p:{E}\to\operatorname{U}({B})

with a refinement map of labelled
n
-framed stratified bundles

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{U}({B})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p}

The diagrammatic
n
-mesh bundles form a simplicial subset

\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
of
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}([n])
.

Definition 4.3.1.3
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a quasicategory and

f:{S}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{T}

a bordism of open
n
-meshes with labels in
\mathcal{C}
.
We say that
f
is
submersive
when, for every submesh

i:{S}^{\prime}\hookrightarrow{S}

whose normal form
\textup{nf}({S}^{\prime})
is an atom,
the active part of the active/inert factorisation of
f\circ i
normalises to an equivalence:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{nf}({S}^{\prime})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{S}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{S}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{nf}({T}^{\prime})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{T}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{T}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}

Proposition 4.3.1.4
.

Let
f:{S}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{T}
be a bordism of
open
n
-meshes with labels in
[n]
such that both

{S}
,
{T}
are diagrammatic
n
-meshes.
Then the bordism
f
is in
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
if and only if it is submersive.

Proof.

The backwards implication is clear.
Suppose therefore that
f
is in
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
and let

i:{S}^{\prime}\hookrightarrow{S}

such that the normal form
\textup{nf}({S}^{\prime})
is an atom.
We need to show that there exists an equivalence

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{nf}({S}^{\prime})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{S}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{S}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{nf}({T}^{\prime})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{T}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{T}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}

where the right square is the active/inert factorisation of
f\circ i
.
We rephrase the problem in terms of bundles as follows.

Let
F:{M}\to\|\Delta[1]\|
be the open
n
-mesh bundle that
represents the bordism
f
and analogously let
F^{\prime}:{M}^{\prime}\to\|\Delta[1]\|

be the open
n
-mesh bundle representing the active bordism
f^{\prime}
.
By the definition of
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
there exists an
n
-diagrammatic bundle

p:{E}\to{|\Delta[1]|}
determined by the dimension labelling
so that
f
refines
p
.
The
n
-diagrammatic bundle
p
restricts to an
n
-diagrammatic bundle

p^{\prime}:{E}^{\prime}\to{|\Delta[1]|}
that refines
f^{\prime}
.
The submesh
{S}^{\prime}
refines a stable framed basic
{U}
.
All of this data organises into the following diagram of
n
-framed stratified bundles:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{U}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{S}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{|\Delta[0]|}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{|\Delta[1]|}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{|\Delta[1]|}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[0]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[1]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[1]\|}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F}

To construct the equivalence between the normal forms, it suffices to show
that
F^{\prime}
refines a trivial
n
-diagrammatic
n
-mesh bundle.
Because the framed basic
{U}
is stable, there exists an
\varepsilon>0

such that the
n
-diagrammatic bundle
p^{\prime}
restricts to a trivial
n
-framed
stratified bundle over
{[0,\varepsilon)}
.
When we restrict the open
n
-mesh bundle
F^{\prime}
accordingly, we obtain the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{U}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{U}\times{[0,\varepsilon)}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{S}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}^{\prime\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{|\Delta[0]|}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{[0,\varepsilon)}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[1]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[0]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[1]\|\cap{[0,\varepsilon)}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\Delta[1]\|}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p^{\prime\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F^{\prime\prime}}

In this diagram the top, back and bottom squares of the cube are pullback
squares. It follows that the front squares are pullback squares as well,
and therefore
F^{\prime\prime}
is an open
n
-mesh bundle.
Because
F^{\prime\prime}
refines the trivial
n
-diagrammatic bundle
p^{\prime\prime}
,
it refines a trivial diagrammatic
n
-mesh bundle when equipped with the induced labelling.
The inclusion
\|\Delta[1]\|\cap{[0,\varepsilon)}\hookrightarrow\|\Delta[1]\|
is a
stratified homotopy equivalence. Therefore,
F^{\prime}
also refines a trivial diagrammatic
n
-mesh bundle.
∎

Remark 4.3.1.5
.

The characterisation of maps in
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
as submersive mesh bordisms
depends essentially on the framed basics to be stable.

Lemma 4.3.1.6
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a quasicategory.
Then the submersive bordisms of open
n
-meshes with labels in
\mathcal{C}

are closed under composition in
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})
.

Proof.

Suppose we have two composable mesh bordisms

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{R}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{S}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{T}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces g}

in
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathcal{C})

such that both
f
and
g
are submersive.
Let
{R}^{\prime}
be a submesh of
{R}
that normalises
to an atom.
We then have a diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{nf}({R}^{\prime})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{R}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{R}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{nf}({S}^{\prime})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{S}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{S}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{nf}({T}^{\prime})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{T}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{T}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces g^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces g}

where
f^{\prime}
and
g^{\prime}
are produced by the active/inert factorisation.
The first equivalence between normal forms exists since
f
is submersive
and
{R}^{\prime}
normalises to an atom.
But then
{S}^{\prime}
also normalises to an atom and so
the second equivalence between normal forms exists because
g
is submersive.
By functoriality of the active/inert factorisation it then follows
that the composite
g\circ f
is submersive.
∎

Corollary 4.3.1.7
.

The simplicial set of diagrammatic
n
-meshes
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
is a quasicategory.
Moreover, the inclusion map

\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}\hookrightarrow\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}([n])
is a categorical fibration
that exhibits
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
as an
\infty
-subcategory of
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}([n])
.

Proof.

Combining Proposition
4.3.1.4
with Lemma
4.3.1.6
.
∎

Observation 4.3.1.8
.

Let
f:{S}\to{T}
be a bordism of diagrammatic
n
-meshes.
Suppose that
f
fits into a diagram of bordisms of open
n
-meshes with labels
in
[n]
of the form

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{R}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{S}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{T}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{0}}

where
f_{1}
is an inert bordism.
Then
f_{0}
and
f_{1}
are both bordisms of diagrammatic
n
-meshes.
This closure property allows us to lift the active/inert factorisation from
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}([n])

to the
\infty
-category
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
of diagrammatic
n
-meshes.

4.3.2
Meshed Manifold Diagrams

We can find an alternative construction of the
n
-diagrammatic space of
manifold diagrams by using
n
-diagrammatic meshes.

Definition 4.3.2.1
.

We write
\mathfrak{m}:\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
for the composite
of the inclusion map
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}\hookrightarrow\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}([n])

followed by the forgetful map
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}([n])\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.
Consider the diagram of simplicial sets

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\perp}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathfrak{m}}

(4.2)

in which the square is a pullback square.
Then
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}
is the simplicial set of
extended meshed
n
-manifold diagrams
.
The top row of the diagram composes into a map
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.

Observation 4.3.2.2
.

Concretely a
k
-simplex of
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}
consists of a closed
n
-mesh
bundle
\xi:{X}\to\|\Delta[k]\|
together with a diagrammatic
n
-mesh bundle

f:{M}\to\|\Delta[k]\|
such that
\xi
and
f
are orthogonal.
The map
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}
sends the pair
(\xi,f)
to
\xi
.

Lemma 4.3.2.3
.

The map
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is a cocartesian fibration.
Moreover, a map is cocartesian for
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
if and only if it is
sent to an equivalence by
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}\to\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
.

Proof.

The inclusion map
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}\hookrightarrow\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathbb{N}^{\textup{op}})
is a categorical fibration by Corollary
4.3.1.7
and the forgetful map
\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}(\mathbb{N}^{\textup{op}})\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is a categorical
fibration. Therefore, the composite map
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}

is again a categorical fibration.
The map
\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\perp}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is a cocartesian fibration by Lemma
3.6.5.8
and a map is cocartesian if and only if
\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\perp}\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}

sends it to an equivalence.
The claim then follows Lemma
2.1.3.19
.
∎

Observation 4.3.2.4
.

The cocartesian fibration
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
induces a functor

\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(-):\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}\to\textup{Cat}_{\infty}

sending each closed
n
-mesh
{X}
to an
\infty
-category

\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})
.
We can compute this
\infty
-category concretely as a quasicategory by taking
the pullback of simplicial sets

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[0]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{X}}

More concretely, a
k
-simplex of
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})
consists of an
diagrammatic
n
-mesh bundle
f:{M}\to\|\Delta[k]\|
that
is fibrewise orthogonal to
{X}
.

Observation 4.3.2.5
.

There is a canonical map of simplicial sets
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}\to\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}
which sends
a pair
(\xi,f)
to the pair
(\xi,p)
where
p
is the

n
-manifold diagram bundle that is refined by the diagrammatic
n
-mesh bundle
f
.
Because this map preserves the closed
n
-mesh bundle
\xi
, it commutes with the
projections to
\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}

We therefore have a natural transformation

\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(-)\to\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(-)
.
The component of this natural transformation on a closed
n
-mesh
{X}

sends the
\infty
-category
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})

of extended diagrammatic
n
-meshes on
{X}
to the space

\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}({X})

of extended
n
-manifold diagrams on
{X}
.

Lemma 4.3.2.6
.

The map of cocartesian fibrations

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}

exhibits
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
as the free left fibration
induced by
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.

Proof.

We check that for each closed
n
-mesh
{X}

the induced map on fibres

\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})\to\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}({X})

is a Kan equivalence.
The map

\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})\to\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}({X})

canonically extends to a map on the Kan fibrant replacement

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X}))}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}

and it suffices to show that
\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X}))\to\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}({X})

is a Kan equivalence.
For this purpose we solve lifting problems of the form

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}({X})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}

(4.3)

where the lower right square needs to commute up to equivalence.

When
k=0
we have an
n
-manifold diagram
{E}
which is orthogonal to
{X}
.
Then by Observation
3.6.5.5
the coarsest refining mesh
{M}
of
{E}
remains orthogonal to
{X}
.
Therefore, the pair
({X},{M})
is a
0
-simplex of
\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X}))
which solves our lifting problem.

When
k>0
we have an
n
-manifold diagram bundle
p:{E}\to{|\Delta[k]|}

that is fibrewise orthogonal to
{X}
.
We also have an
i\geq 0
and an
n
-manifold diagram bundle
f^{\prime}:{M}^{\prime}\to\partial\|\textup{sd}^{i}[k]\|
that is fibrewise orthogonal to
{X}
.
We write
p^{\prime}:{E}^{\prime}\to\partial{|\Delta[k]|}
for the restriction of
p

over the boundary. Then
p^{\prime}
is refined by
f^{\prime}
.

Since the lower right corner of the lifting problem (
4.3
)
only needs to commute up to equivalence, we are free to replace
p
up to equivalence
of
k
-simplices in
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}({X})
relative to the boundary.
We use this affordance to assume without loss of generality that there exists
an open collar neighbourhood
\partial{|\Delta[k]|}\times({|\Delta[1]|}\setminus\{1\})\hookrightarrow{|\Delta[k]|}
such that

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}^{\prime}\times({|\Delta[1]|}\setminus\{1\})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial{|\Delta[k]|}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial{|\Delta[k]|}\times({|\Delta[1]|}\setminus\{1\})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{|\Delta[k]|}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p^{\prime}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\llcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p}

By Proposition
3.4.3.4
there is a coarsest open
n
-mesh bundle

g_{0}:{N}_{0}\to{B}_{0}

which refines
p
. By our setup the restriction of
p
to the collar neighbourhood
is refined by the open
n
-mesh bundle obtained from thickening
f^{\prime}
to the collar:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}^{\prime}\times(\|\Delta[1]\|\setminus\{1\})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}^{\prime}\times({|\Delta[1]|}\setminus\{1\})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial\|\textup{sd}^{i}[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial\|\textup{sd}^{i}[k]\|\times(\|\Delta[1]\|\setminus\{1\})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial{|\Delta[k]|}\times({|\Delta[1]|}\setminus\{1\})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{|\Delta[k]|}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f^{\prime}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\llcorner}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p}

Since by Observation
3.4.3.5
the coarsest open
n
-mesh bundles that refine tame stratifications are determined locally, the restriction of the open
n
-mesh bundle
g_{0}:{N}_{0}\to{B}_{0}
to the collar must be coarser than the thickening of
f^{\prime}
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}^{\prime}\times(\|\Delta[1]\|\setminus\{1\})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{N}^{\prime}_{0}\times(\|\Delta[1]\|\setminus\{1\})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{N}_{0}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial\|\textup{sd}^{i}[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial\|\textup{sd}^{i}[k]\|\times(\|\Delta[1]\|\setminus\{1\})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\partial{B}_{0}\times(\|\Delta[1]\|\setminus\{1\})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{0}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f^{\prime}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\llcorner}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces g_{0}}

We can therefore further refine
g_{0}:{N}_{0}\to{B}_{0}
to an open
n
-mesh bundle

g_{1}:{N}_{1}\to{B}_{1}

which restricts to
f^{\prime}:{M}^{\prime}\to\partial\|\textup{sd}^{i}[k]\|

on the boundary
\partial{B}_{1}=\partial\|\textup{sd}^{i}[k]\|
.
Then there exists a
j\geq i
and a refinement map
s:\|\textup{sd}^{j}[k]\|\to{B}_{1}
that is the identity on the boundary.
We then take the pullbacks

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{N}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\|\textup{sd}^{j}[k]\|}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces g_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces s}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{D}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{E}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{|\Delta[k]|}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{|\Delta[k]|}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces q}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces p}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{U}(s)}

The
n
-manifold diagram bundles
p
and
q
are equivalent relative to the boundary.
Therefore, the open
n
-mesh bundle
f:{M}\to\|\textup{sd}^{j}[k]\|

is a solution to the lifting problem.
∎

.

on an example. We begin with the

Because
{B}
is a refinement of
{|\Delta[1]|}
, there exists a

j\geq 0
and a refinement
\|\textup{sd}^{j}[1]\|\to{B}
.
In our case
j=2
is sufficient.
Pulling back
f
along this refinement then yields a diagrammatic
2
-mesh
bundle over
\|\textup{sd}^{2}[1]\|
, and therefore a
1
-simplex
of
\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{2}(\mathbb{I}^{2}))
:

4.3.4
Active Bordisms and Non-Extended Diagrams

An
n
-manifold diagram on a closed
n
-mesh
{X}

is completely determined
by its intersection with
{X}
. To facilitate the equivalence
with meshed manifold diagrams we
introduced extended manifold diagrams
that spill over the closed
n
-mesh to fill all of
\mathbb{R}^{n}
.
Using active bordisms we can find non-extended
variants of
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(-)
and
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{T}}^{n}(-)
.

Construction 4.3.4.1
.

Let
X
be a closed
n
-truss.
We let
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{T}}^{n}(X)
denote the full subcategory of
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{T}}^{n}(X)

whose objects consist of a diagrammatic
n
-truss
S
together
with an active bordism
T^{\dagger}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}S
of open unlabelled
n
-trusses.

Lemma 4.3.4.2
.

Let
X
be a closed
n
-truss.
The inclusion
i:\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{T}}^{n}(X)\hookrightarrow\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{T}}^{n}(X)

admits a retraction
r
together with a natural transformation

\varepsilon:i\circ r\to\textup{id}
.

Proof.

An object of
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{T}}^{n}(X)
consists of a diagrammatic
n
-truss

S
together with a bordism of open unlabelled
n
-trusses
f:X^{\dagger}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}S
.
The bordism
f
then factors into an active bordism
f_{0}
followed by an inert bordism
f_{1}
as follows:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{X^{\dagger}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{S^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{S}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{1}}

Since
f_{1}:S^{\prime}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}S
is inert, there is a canonical labelling of
S^{\prime}

such that
f_{1}
induces a map of diagrammatic
n
-trusses

S^{\prime}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}S
.
We define
r(S,f):=(S^{\prime},f_{0})
and let
f_{1}
be the component
of the natural transformation
\varepsilon:i\circ r\to\textup{id}
on
(S,f)
.

A map in
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{T}}^{n}(X)
consists of a bordism of diagrammatic
n
-trusses
\alpha:S\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}R
which fits into a diagram of unlabelled open
n
-trusses

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{X^{\dagger}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{S}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{R}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces g}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha}

When we factor
f
and
g
into inert bordisms followed by active bordisms,
functoriality of the factorisation yields a diagram of unlabelled open
n
-trusses

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{S^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{R^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{X^{\dagger}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{X^{\dagger}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces S}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces R}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces g_{0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces g}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces g_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha}

The labels of the bordism of diagrammatic
n
-trusses

then
restrict to labels for
\alpha^{\prime}
, making
\alpha^{\prime}
itself into a bordism
of diagrammatic
n
-trusses.
This is the value of
r
on the map in
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{T}}^{n}(X)
,
and the inert maps
f_{1},g_{1}
together form the component of
\eta
on this map.
Finally, functoriality of
