follows from functoriality of the active/inert factorisation.
∎

Construction 4.3.4.3
.

Suppose that
{X}
is a closed
n
-mesh.
By Observation
4.3.3.5
we have an equivalence

\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})\simeq\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{T}}^{n}(\textup{N}_{\bar{\textup{T}}}({X}))
.
We can then take the pullback of simplicial sets along this equivalence
to define the meshed version
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})
of
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{T}}^{n}({X})
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{T}}^{n}(\textup{N}_{\bar{\textup{T}}}({X}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{T}}^{n}(\textup{N}_{\bar{\textup{T}}}({X}))}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}

Because the inclusion map
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{T}}^{n}(\textup{N}_{\bar{\textup{T}}}({X}))\hookrightarrow\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{T}}^{n}(\textup{N}_{\bar{\textup{T}}}({X}))

is both a categorical fibration and categorical equivalence,
it follows that
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})
is a quasicategory
and equivalent to
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})
.

Corollary 4.3.4.4
.

Let
{X}
be a closed
n
-mesh.
The inclusion
i:\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(X)\hookrightarrow\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(X)

admits a retraction
r
together with a natural transformation

\varepsilon:i\circ r\to\textup{id}
.

4.4
Manifold Diagrams with Labels

The
n
-diagrammatic space
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(-)
is freely generated by one generator
for each framed isomorphism class of framed basics.
In this section we explore how to freely generate
n
-diagrammatic spaces,
and therefore
(\infty,n)
-categories,
by attaching labels to manifold diagrams.

4.4.1
Diagrammatic Computads

For manifold diagrams to represent pasting diagrams for higher categories,
we need a way to attach labels to a manifold diagram.
Seeing a manifold diagram
{M}
as a stratified space, we could ask
for a functor
\textup{Exit}({M})\to\mathcal{C}
into some
\infty
-category

\mathcal{C}
, but that approach would not enforce compatibility of the labelling
with the local shape of the diagram;
nothing would stop us, e.g., from assigning a label meant to represent a
1
-morphism
to a surface in a
2
-manifold diagram.
We therefore take a different approach, by making use of our characterisation
of manifold diagrams via diagrammatic meshes.

A label schema should assign to every manifold diagram a collection of ways
in that the diagram can be labelled.
To embed our theory into the wider world of homotopy coherent mathematics
and with a view towards the comparison with
n
-diagrammatic spaces,
this collection of admissible labellings should be a space.
An isotopy of manifold diagrams should act on its labelling;
this is achieved by space-valued presheaves
\Sigma:\textup{M}^{n,\textup{op}}_{\textup{d}}\to\textup{S}
.
The space of labellings should be independent of the mesh that we used to
refine the manifold diagram and invariant under isotopy of manifold diagrams;
the presheaf
\Sigma
therefore should send active maps to equivalences.
Finally, a labelling should be local in that it is completely determined by assigning labels to the individual parts that make up a manifold diagram.
This requirement translates into the presheaf
\Sigma
being a sheaf.

Definition 4.4.1.1
.

A presheaf
\Sigma:\textup{M}^{n,\textup{op}}_{\textup{d}}\to\textup{S}
is a

diagrammatic
n
-computad

when it satisfies the following conditions:

1.

Isotopy
: Every active bordism of diagrammatic
n
-meshes

{M}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{N}

induces an equivalence of spaces

\Sigma({N})\to\Sigma({M})
.

2.

Sheaf:
For every diagrammatic
n
-mesh
{M}
,
the atomic covering diagram

U:\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})^{\textup{op},\triangleright}\longrightarrow\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}

induces a limit diagram of spaces

\Sigma(U(-)):\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})^{\triangleleft}\longrightarrow\textup{S}.

We denote by
\cramped{\textup{Cptd}}_{(\infty,n)}
the reflective
\infty
-subcategory of
\textup{P}(\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}})

whose objects are the diagrammatic
n
-computads.

Observation 4.4.1.2
.

Via the equivalence
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}\simeq\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
between diagrammatic

n
-meshes and diagrammatic
n
-trusses we can equivalently define the

\infty
-category of diagrammatic
n
-computads
\cramped{\textup{Cptd}}_{(\infty,n)}
as a reflective

\infty
-subcategory of
\textup{P}(\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}})
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{P}(\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{P}(\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\textup{Cptd}}_{(\infty,n)}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}

Using
\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
over
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
is preferable in applications
where we want to produce an
n
-diagrammatic computad from combinatorial data,
such as a
homotopy.io
signature.
Our aim for now is to show how
n
-diagrammatic computads can be used to
label manifold diagrams, for which meshes are more immediately useful.

Example 4.4.1.3
.

Given the generating data for plain, braided or symmetric monoidal categories,
we can construct a diagrammatic computad in dimension
2
,
3
or
4
, respectively,
so that the labelled manifold diagrams are labelled string diagrams.
More generally, each signature in the proof assistant
homotopy.io
with generators
up to dimension
n
canonically defines a diagrammatic
n
-computad.

Observation 4.4.1.4
.

Let us denote by
Act
the wide subcategory of
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
consisting
of the active bordisms. The universal property of localisation of
\infty
-categories
guarantees that we have an equivalence between the
\infty
-categories

\textup{P}(\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}})[\textup{Act}^{-1}]\simeq\textup{P}(\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}[\textup{Act}^{-1}])

Here
\textup{P}(\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}})[\textup{Act}^{-1}]
is the reflective localisation of

\textup{P}(\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}})
at the maps that are the image of an active bordism
under the Yoneda embedding. This is precisely the reflective subcategory
of
\textup{P}(\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}})
whose objects satisfy the isotopy condition.

In Definition
4.4.1.1
we have named the property that allows
us to glue along atomic covers of diagrammatic
n
-meshes the sheaf condition.
However, the covers do not form a topology on
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
directly:
The reflective subcategory
\textup{P}(\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}})
satisfying
only the sheaf condition is not an
\infty
-category of sheaves.
This is corrected by the isotopy condition: The atomic covering diagrams
form a topology on the localisation
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}[\textup{Act}^{-1}]
.

Lemma 4.4.1.5
.

Let
f:{M}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{N}
be a bordism of diagrammatic

n
-meshes and
{A}
an atom of
{M}
. Then there exists an
atom
{B}
of
{N}
such that
f
fits into a diagram of
diagrammatic
n
-meshes of the form

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{nf}({A})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{nf}({S})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{nf}({B})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{A}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{S}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{N}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{N}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}

and the middle row consists of active bordisms that normalise to equivalences.

Proof.

We construct the diagram piece by piece as follows.
We begin by using the active/inert factorisation to obtain the square

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{A}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{S}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{N}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}

By Proposition
4.3.1.4
the bordisms of diagrammatic
n
-meshes are submersive.
Because the bordism
{A}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{S}
is active by construction and
{A}

is already an atom, it follows that
{A}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{S}
normalises
to an equivalence

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{nf}({A})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{nf}({S})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{A}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{S}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{N}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}

We see that
\textup{nf}({S})\simeq\textup{nf}({A})
is an atom and therefore

{S}
refines a framed basic.
It follows that there exists at least one an atom
{B}
of
{S}

such that
{B}
refines the same framed basic as
{S}
.
We therefore have an equivalence
\textup{nf}({S})\simeq\textup{nf}({B})

which completes the diagram in the claim.
∎

Lemma 4.4.1.6
.

Let
f:{M}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{N}
be an active bordism of diagrammatic

n
-meshes and
{B}
an atom in
{N}
.
Then there exists an atom
{A}
of
{M}
such that
f
fits into
a diagram of diagrammatic
n
-meshes of the form

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{nf}({A})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{nf}({S})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{nf}({B})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{A}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{S}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{B}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{M}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{N}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{{N}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}

and the middle row consists of active bordisms that normalise to equivalences.

Proposition 4.4.1.7
.

The localisation
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}[\textup{Act}^{-1}]
at the active bordisms
of diagrammatic
n
-meshes has a topology that is generated by the atomic
covering diagrams

\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{M}})^{\textup{op}}\longrightarrow(\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}})_{/{M}}

for each diagrammatic
n
-mesh
{M}\in\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
.
In particular
\cramped{\textup{Cptd}}_{(\infty,n)}
is an
\infty
-topos of sheaves.

Proof.

By
[
Lur08a
, where]
a Grothendieck topology on an
\infty
-category
\mathcal{C}

is exactly a Grothendieck topology on the homotopy
1
-category
\textup{h}(\mathcal{C})
.
It therefore suffices to show that the covering diagrams induce a topology
on
\textup{h}(\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}[\textup{Act}^{-1}])
.
In particular, we show that they define a coverage:
For every map
\varphi:[{M}]\to[{N}]
in
\textup{h}(\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}[\textup{Act}^{-1}])

and every atom
{B}
in
{N}
there is an atom
{A}

of
{M}
so that
\varphi
restricts to a map between the atoms

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{[{A}]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{[{B}]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{[{M}]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{[{N}]}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi}

Any map
\varphi:[{M}]\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}[{N}]
can be written as a zigzag of maps
in
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
starting at
{M}
and ending at
{N}
in
which the backwards maps are active bordisms.
We can therefore reduce to the case that
\varphi
is induced by an individual
map in
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
.
When
\varphi=[f]
for some bordism of diagrammatic
n
-meshes
f:{M}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{N}
,
the coverage property then follows by Lemma
4.4.1.5
.
In the case that
\varphi=[g]^{-1}
for some active bordism of diagrammatic

n
-meshes
g:{N}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}{M}
we can similarly apply Lemma
4.4.1.6
.

Therefore, the atomic covers of diagramamtic
n
-meshes form a topology
on the homotopy
1
-category
\textup{h}(\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}[\textup{Act}^{-1}])
and consequently
also a topology on the localisation
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}[\textup{Act}^{-1}]
.
Then
\cramped{\textup{Cptd}}_{(\infty,n)}
is the topological localisation of the
\infty
-category
of presheaves
\textup{P}(\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}[\textup{Act}^{-1}])
and therefore an
\infty
-topos
of sheaves.
∎

4.4.2
The Diagrammatic Space of Labelled Manifold Diagrams

Given any diagrammatic
n
-computad
\Sigma
we define an
n
-diagrammatic space

\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(\Sigma)
consisting of extended manifold diagrams with labels in
\Sigma
.
For the purposes of this construction we represent the
presheaf
\Sigma
as a right fibration
\Sigma:\mathcal{C}\to\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
.

Construction 4.4.2.1
.

Let
\Sigma:\mathcal{C}\to\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
be a right fibration
representing a space-valued presheaf on
\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
.
Consider the diagram of simplicial sets

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma}

where the square is a pullback square.
Then
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)
is the simplicial set of
extended meshed
n
-manifold
diagrams with labels in
\Sigma
.
The composite of the top row of the diagram is projection map
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.

Lemma 4.4.2.2
.

Let
\Sigma:\mathcal{C}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
be a right fibration.
Then the projection map
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}

is a cocartesian fibration.

Proof.

Since
\Sigma:\mathcal{C}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is a right fibration, it is in particular
a categorical fibration. The map
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is a cocartesian
fibration by Lemma
4.3.2.3
and a map is
cocartesian if and only if
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}\to\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
sends it to
an equivalence.
The claim then follows Lemma
2.1.3.19
.
∎

Observation 4.4.2.3
.

Suppose that
\Sigma:\mathcal{C}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is a right fibration.
Then the cocartesian fibration
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}

induces a functor of
\infty
-categories

\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)(-):\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}\longrightarrow\textup{Cat}_{\infty}.

Given any closed
n
-mesh
{X}
the
\infty
-category

\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X})
is represented by the quasicategory
that arises from taking the pullback of simplicial sets

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[0]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{X}}

In §
4.3.2
we have seen that we have an alternative presentation of the
n
-diagrammatic space of
extended
n
-manifold diagrams
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(-)
, as defined originally in §
4.2.6
,
using
n
-diagrammatic meshes: For every closed
n
-mesh
{X}
there is an equivalence
between the space
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}({X})
and the classifying space
\textup{k}(\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X}))
.
By analogy, we define the space
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X})
of extended
n
-manifold diagrams
with labels in
\Sigma
by taking the classifying space of the meshed version.

Definition 4.4.2.4
.

Let
\Sigma:\textup{M}^{n,\textup{op}}_{\textup{d}}\to\textup{S}
be a presheaf.
For every closed
n
-mesh we define the space of
extended
n
-manifold diagrams
on
{X}
with labels in
{X}
as the classifying space

\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X}):=\textup{k}(\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X}))

This definition extends to a functor

\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(-)(-):\textup{P}(\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}})\longrightarrow\textup{Fun}(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n},\textup{S}).

Theorem 4.4.2.5
.

Let
\Sigma
be a
n
-diagrammatic computad.
Then the functor

\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(\Sigma):\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}\longrightarrow\textup{S}

is an
n
-diagrammatic space.

Proof.

This follows from Lemma
4.4.2.11
and Lemma
4.4.2.12
below.
∎

In order to prove this we build upon the previous result from Theorem
4.2.5.1
that unlabelled
n
-manifold diagrams form
an
n
-diagrammatic space
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}
:
We verify the Segal condition for
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\Sigma)

by first gluing together the unlabelled
n
-manifold diagrams and then using the sheaf condition on
\Sigma
to glue together the labels as well.
The isotopy condition on
\Sigma
ensures that labels in
\Sigma
can be transported along isotopies of
n
-manifold diagrams.
We spend the remainder of this section with the technical details.

Observation 4.4.2.6
.

Suppose that
\Sigma
is an
n
-diagrammatic computad that is presented by a
right fibration
\Sigma:\mathcal{C}\to\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
.
For every closed
n
-mesh
{X}

we have a forgetful map

\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X})\to\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})

that throws away the labels.
This map does not in general induce a Kan fibration between the Kan fibrant replacements

\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X}))\longrightarrow\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})).

In particular, we can not lift all isotopies of extended
n
-manifold diagrams
that have new cells emerge from infinity, outside the confines of the closed
n
-mesh
{X}
.

We solve this issue by introducing a labelled
n
-manifold diagrams that are not extended,
so that we avoid any non-trivial geometry outside the closed
n
-mesh.

Construction 4.4.2.7
.

Let
\Sigma:\mathcal{C}\to\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
be a right fibration.
For any closed
n
-mesh we define the simplicial set

\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X})

of
meshed
n
-manifold diagrams on
{X}
with labels in
\Sigma

by taking the pullback of simplicial sets

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}

Then the space
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X})

of
n
-manifold diagrams on
{X}
with labels in
\Sigma

is the Kan fibrant replacement
\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X}))
.

Lemma 4.4.2.8
.

Let
\Sigma:\mathcal{C}\to\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
be a right fibration that
represents an
n
-diagrammatic computad.
Then for every closed
n
-mesh
{X}
the induced inclusion map

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X}))}}

(4.5)

is an equivalence of Kan complexes.

Proof.

Let
i:\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})\hookrightarrow\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})

denote the inclusion map. By Corollary
4.3.4.4

there exists a retraction
r
of
i
together with a natural transformation

\varepsilon:i\circ r\to\textup{id}
.
By taking the pullbacks along
i
and
r

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r^{\prime}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i^{\prime}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i}

we then have an inclusion map
i^{\prime}
with a retraction
r^{\prime}
.
Morever, by taking the pullback

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[1]\times\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[1]\times\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varepsilon^{\prime}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varepsilon}

we have a natural transformation
\varepsilon^{\prime}:i^{\prime}\circ r^{\prime}\to\textup{id}
.
When we then apply
\textup{Ex}^{\infty}
to
i^{\prime},r^{\prime},\varepsilon^{\prime}
we see that

\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X}))
is a deformation
retract of
\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X}))
.
∎

Lemma 4.4.2.9
.

Let
\Sigma:\mathcal{C}\to\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
be a right fibration that
represents an
n
-diagrammatic computad.
Then for every closed
n
-mesh
{X}
the forgetful map

\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X}))\longrightarrow\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X}))

is a Kan fibration.

Proof.

Suppose we have a lifting problem

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Lambda^{i}[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X}))}}

Then there exists a
t\geq 0
such that the lifting problem factors
through the
t
h stage
\textup{Ex}^{t}
of the filtered colimit that defines the functor
\textup{Ex}^{\infty}
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Lambda^{i}[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Ex}^{t}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[k]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Ex}^{t}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X}))}}

By adjunction the lifting problem is then equivalent to

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Sd}^{t}(\Lambda^{i}[k])}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Sd}^{t}(\Delta[k])}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})}}

To solve this lifting problem we must find a filler for the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Sd}^{t}(\Lambda^{i}[k])}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Sd}^{t}(\Delta[k])}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}}}

(4.6)

which extends the labelling of the meshed
n
-manifold diagram.

Since the right fibration
\Sigma:\mathcal{C}\to\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}

represents an
n
-diagrammatic computad,
it is fibrant in the
Act
-local contravariant model structure
on
\textup{sSet}_{/\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}}
representing presheaves on the localisation

\textup{P}(\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}[\textup{Act}^{-1}])
.
Then by the dual of
[
Nui
, Lemma 2.5.]
we have
that the map
\Sigma^{\prime}:\mathcal{C}^{\prime}\to\textup{Act}
obtained by the pullback

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}}}
Act
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{\prime}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma}

is a Kan fibration.
The map
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})\to\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
factors through the inclusion

\textup{Act}\hookrightarrow\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
and so the lifting problem (
4.6
) factors through the pullback

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Sd}^{t}(\Lambda^{i}[k])}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Sd}^{t}(\Delta[k])}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X})}}
Act
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{\prime}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma}

(4.7)

The inclusion
\textup{Sd}^{i}(\Lambda^{i}[k])\hookrightarrow\textup{Sd}^{i}(\Delta[k])

is a Kan equivalence, and so we have a lift in (
4.7
).
∎

Lemma 4.4.2.10
.

Let
f:\mathcal{I}^{\triangleleft}\to\textup{sSet}^{[1]}
be a diagram
which satisfies the following conditions.

1.

For each
i\in\mathcal{I}
the map
f(i):E(i)\to B(i)
is a Kan fibration between Kan complexes.

2.

The diagram
B:\mathcal{I}^{\triangleleft}\to\textup{sSet}
is a homotopy limit diagram.

3.

For any vertex
x\in B(\bot)_{0}
let

F_{x}:\mathcal{I}^{\triangleleft}\to\textup{sSet}

be the diagram which sends
i\in\mathcal{I}^{\triangleleft}
to the fibre

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F_{x}(i)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{E(i)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\{x\}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{B(i)}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X(i)}

Then
F_{x}
is a homotopy limit diagram.

Then
f
is a homotopy limit diagram.

Proof.

Let
L:\textup{sSet}\to\textup{S}
the localisation functor which inverts the Kan equivalences
and
\textup{cod}:\textup{S}^{[1]}\to\textup{S}
the codomain fibration.
Since we assumed
B:\mathcal{I}^{\triangleleft}\to\textup{sSet}
to be a homotopy limit diagram, the composite
L\circ B
is a limit diagram in
S
.
Therefore, by
[
Lur23
,
Corollary 02KR
]

the diagram
L^{[1]}\circ f
is a limit diagram if and only if
it is a
cod
-limit diagram.
For each
i\in\mathcal{I}^{\triangleleft}
we take the pullback of simplicial sets

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{E^{\prime}(i)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{E(i)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{B(\bot)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{B(i)}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f^{\prime}(i)}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f(i)}

(4.8)

By naturality we obtain a functor
f^{\prime}:\mathcal{I}^{\triangleleft}\to\textup{sSet}^{[1]}

as well as a natural transformation
f^{\prime}\to f
.
This descends to a natural transformation between the localisations

L^{[1]}\circ f^{\prime}\to L^{[1]}\circ f
.
Because every map
f(i):E(i)\to B(i)
is a Kan fibration
and all involved objects are Kan complexes,
the square (
4.8
) is a homotopy pullback.
A map in the arrow category
\textup{S}^{[1]}
is
cod
-cartesian if
it is a pullback square in
S
;
therefore the components of the induced natural transformation
L^{[1]}\circ f^{\prime}\to L^{[1]}\circ f
are
cod
-cartesian maps.
Moreover the component on the cone point
\bot\in\mathcal{I}^{\triangleleft}
is an equivalence.
By the dual of
[
Lur23
,
Proposition 031R
]

it follows that
L^{[1]}\circ f
is a
cod
-limit diagram if

L^{[1]}\circ f^{\prime}
is a
cod
-limit diagram.

Since
S
is complete, the codomain functor
\textup{cod}:\textup{S}^{[1]}\to\textup{S}

is a cartesian fibration.
The fibre of
cod
over a space
X\in\textup{S}
is the slice
\infty
-category

\textup{S}_{/X}
which is also complete.
Moreover, for any map of spaces
X\to Y
the contravariant transport functor

\textup{S}_{/Y}\to\textup{S}_{/X}
is given by pullback and therefore preserves
limits.
Then by

[
Lur23
,
Proposition 031S
]

it follows that
L^{[1]}\circ f^{\prime}
is a
cod
-limit diagram
if and only if
L^{[1]}\circ f^{\prime}
is a limit diagram in the slice

\infty
-category
\textup{S}_{/L(B(\bot))}
.
For each
i\in\mathcal{I}^{\triangleleft}
and vertex
x\in B(\bot)_{0}

the simplicial set
F_{x}(i)
is a Kan complex representing the homotopy
fibre of
f^{\prime}(i):E^{\prime}(i)\to B(\bot)
over
x

because
f^{\prime}(i)
is a Kan fibration (being a pullback of the Kan fibration

f(i)
).
Limits in
\textup{S}_{/L(B(\bot))}
are computed fibrewise,
and so
L^{[1]}\circ f^{\prime}
is a limit diagram in the slice
by the assumption that
F_{x}:\mathcal{I}^{\triangleleft}\to\textup{sSet}
is a
homotopy limit diagram for all
x\in B(\bot)_{0}
.
∎

Lemma 4.4.2.11
.

Let
\Sigma:\mathcal{C}\to\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
be a right fibration
representing an
n
-diagrammatic computad.
Let
{X}
be a closed
n
-mesh and

U:\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})^{\triangleleft}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}

its cell covering diagram.
Then the following diagrams
\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})^{\triangleleft}\to\textup{sSet}

are homotopy limit diagrams:

(1)

\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(U(-))

(2)

\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(U(-)))

(3)

\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(U(-)))

(4)

\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)(U(-)))

(5)

\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)(U(-)))

In particular
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(\Sigma)(-)
satisfies the Segal condition of an
n
-diagrammatic space.

Proof.

By Theorem
4.2.5.1
the functor
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(-)
defines an
n
-diagrammatic space.
Therefore, (1) is a homotopy limit by the Segal condition.
By Lemma
4.3.2.6
the map
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
is the free left fibration generated by the cocartesian fibration
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
.
This implies that (1) and (2) are equivalent as diagrams of spaces.
Now by Lemma
4.4.2.8
the diagrams (2) and (3) are equivalent as well.
Therefore, (3) is a homotopy limit diagram.

Let
{M}
be a diagrammatic
n
-mesh that represents a point in

\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X}))
.
For every
i\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})^{\triangleleft}
we denote by
{M}_{i}

the image of
{M}
via the restriction map

\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}({X}))\longrightarrow\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(U(i)))

This defines a covering diagram

V:\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})^{\textup{op},\triangleright}\to\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}

with
V(i)={M}_{i}
and the induced inert maps in between.
For any
i\in\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})^{\triangleright}

we have a pullback square of simplicial sets

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Sigma(V(i))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma)(U(i)))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Delta[0]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Ex}^{\infty}(\cramped{\mathbb{D}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(U(i)))}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{M}_{i}}

By Lemma
4.4.2.9
the maps on the right of this diagram are Kan fibrations, and therefore the pullback is a homotopy pullback as well.
The diagram
\Sigma(V(-)):\cramped{\mathbb{P}}({{X}})^{\triangleleft}\to\textup{sSet}

is a homotopy limit diagram because
\Sigma
is an
n
-diagrammatic computad
and
V(-)
is a covering diagram.
Then Lemma
4.4.2.10
shows that (4) is a homotopy limit diagram.
Finally, by Lemma
4.4.2.8
the diagrams (4) and (5) are equivalent and so (5) is also a homotopy limit diagram.
∎

Lemma 4.4.2.12
.

Let
\Sigma:\mathcal{C}\to\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
be a left fibration representing a label system.
Then for any closed
n
-mesh
{X}
the induced square

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}(\Sigma)({X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}(\Sigma)(\square{{X}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}(\Sigma)(\partial{X})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}(\Sigma)(\partial\square{{X}})}}

is a pullback square of spaces.
In particular the map
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(\Sigma)(-):\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}\to\textup{S}

satisfies the regularity condition of an
n
-diagrammatic space.

Proof.

This can be shown analogously to Lemma
4.4.2.11
using that
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}^{n}(-)
is an
n
-diagrammatic space
by Proposition
4.2.6.8
.
∎

4.4.3
Free
(\infty,n)
-Categories via Manifold Diagrams

Construction 4.4.3.1
.

For every
n
-diagrammatic computad
\Sigma
we have constructed
an
n
-diagrammatic space
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\Sigma)
of
n
-manifold diagrams
labelled in
\Sigma
.
By the equivalence
\operatorname{Seg}^{\textup{r}}(\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n})\simeq\operatorname{Seg}(\Delta^{n})

the
n
-diagrammatic space
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\Sigma)
induces an
n
-uple Segal
space, and after applying the localisation functor
\operatorname{Seg}(\Delta^{n})\to\textup{Cat}_{(\infty,n)}

an
(\infty,n)
-category
\mathbb{F}(\Sigma)
.
This process extends to a functor

\mathbb{F}:\cramped{\textup{Cptd}}_{(\infty,n)}\to\textup{Cat}_{(\infty,n)}
.

For an
n
-diagrammatic computad
\Sigma
we call
\mathbb{F}(\Sigma)

the
free
(\infty,n)
-category
generated by
\Sigma
.
To justify this terminology, we use this section to demonstrate that

\mathbb{F}
has a right adjoint
\mathbb{U}
.

Lemma 4.4.3.2
.

The following diagram of
\infty
-categories commutes:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{P}(\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{P}(\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{P}(\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{P}(\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n,\textup{op}})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathfrak{t}_{!}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\cdot)}

Proof.

Let
\Sigma:\mathcal{C}\to\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
be a right fibration which represents
a space-valued presheaf on
\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
.
The equivalence
\textup{P}(\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}})\to\textup{P}(\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}})
sends
\Sigma
to
the right fibration
\Sigma^{\prime}:\mathcal{C}^{\prime}\to\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
constructed
as the pullback of simplicial sets

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{M}^{n}_{\textup{d}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{\prime}}
{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}

We can then form a commutative cube of simplicial sets

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{Tw}(\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n})\times_{\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n}}\mathcal{C}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{Tw}(\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma^{\prime})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Conf}^{n}_{\perp}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathfrak{m}\circ\Sigma^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathfrak{t}\circ\Sigma}

in which the front and back square are pullback squares of simplicial sets.
The dashed diagonal map is induced by the universal property of the pullback.
Since both
\textup{Conf}^{n}\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{M}}}^{n}
and
\operatorname{Tw}(\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n})\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n}

are categorical fibrations, the front and back square are homotopy pullback squares.
The solid diagonal maps are categorical equivalences, it follows that also the
dashed map is a categorical equivalence.
This induced equivalence then is the top horizontal map in the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma^{\prime})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{Tw}(\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n})\times_{\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n}}\mathcal{C}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n,\textup{op}}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}

where the vertical maps are cocartesian fibrations.
The free left fibration associated to
\cramped{\mathbb{E}}_{\textup{M}}^{n}(\Sigma^{\prime})\to\cramped{\bar{\textup{M}}}^{n}
represents the functor
\cramped{\mathbb{D}}^{n}(\Sigma^{\prime})
.
Meanwhile, the free left fibration induced by

\operatorname{Tw}(\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n})\times_{\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n}}\mathcal{C}\to\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n,\textup{op}}

represents the presheaf
\mathfrak{t}_{!}(\Sigma)
.
It follows that the square in the claim commutes.
∎

Proposition 4.4.3.3
.

The functor
\mathbb{F}:\cramped{\textup{Cptd}}_{(\infty,n)}\to\textup{Cat}_{(\infty,n)}
has a right adjoint.

Proof.

We write
Act
for the wide subcategory of active maps in
\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
and denote the
localisation map by
L:\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}}\to\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}}[\textup{Act}^{-1}]
.
We then consider the chain of adjunctions

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{P}(\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{P}(\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}}[\textup{Act}^{-1}])}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{P}(\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{P}(\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{Cat}_{(\infty,n)}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{!}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathfrak{t}_{!}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathfrak{t}^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\dashv}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\dashv}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\dashv}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\dashv}

(4.9)

Suppose that
\Sigma
is an
n
-diagrammatic computad,
then
\Sigma
sends active maps to equivalences by the isotopy axiom.
Therefore, the adjunction unit
\Sigma\to(L^{*}\circ L_{!})(\Sigma)
is an equivalence.
In particular the top row of (
4.9
) restricts to
the functor
\mathbb{F}:\cramped{\textup{Cptd}}_{(\infty,n)}\to\textup{Cat}_{(\infty,n)}
.

It remains to show that the composite
L^{*}\circ L_{*}\circ\mathfrak{t}^{*}

sends
n
-diagrammatic spaces to
n
-diagrammatic computads;
then the restriction defines the right adjoint
\mathbb{U}
of
\mathbb{F}
.
Let
\mathcal{F}
be a presheaf on
\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n}
that is an
n
-diagrammatic space.
Then the Segal condition directly implies the sheaf condition for
\mathfrak{t}^{*}\mathcal{F}
.
However,
\mathfrak{t}^{*}\mathcal{F}
does not in general satisfy the isotopy condition
and therefore fails to be a diagrammatic computad.

We rectify this by applying the coreflector
L^{*}\circ L_{*}

which sends
\mathfrak{t}^{*}\mathcal{F}
to its maximal subobject

\Sigma\hookrightarrow\mathfrak{t}^{*}\mathcal{F}
in
\textup{P}(\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}})

so that
\Sigma
satisfies the isotopy condition.
We verify that
\Sigma
still satisfies the sheaf condition and therefore
is a diagrammatic computad.

Let
\Sigma^{\prime}
be the smallest subobject of
\mathfrak{t}^{*}\mathcal{F}
that contains

\Sigma
so that
\Sigma^{\prime}
satisfies the sheaf condition.
When we show that
\Sigma^{\prime}
also satisfies the isotopy condition, we must have

\Sigma\simeq\Sigma^{\prime}
because
\Sigma
was chosen to be the maximal
such subobject of
\mathfrak{t}^{*}\mathcal{F}
.
We proceed to show that
\Sigma^{\prime}
sends active bordisms to equivalences
in increasing generality.

1.

When
A\in\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
is an atom, the inclusion

\Sigma(A)\hookrightarrow\Sigma^{\prime}(A)

must already be an equivalence. Whenever
\alpha:A\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}B
is an active bordism between atoms, the induced map
\Sigma(\alpha):\Sigma(B)\to\Sigma(A)
is an equivalence
since
\Sigma
satisfies the isotopy condition.
It then follows that
\Sigma^{\prime}(\alpha)
must also be an equivalence since it fits into the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Sigma(B)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Sigma(A)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Sigma^{\prime}(B)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Sigma^{\prime}(A)}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma(\alpha)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{\prime}(\alpha)}

2.

Let
\alpha:S\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}A
be a degeneracy bordism in
\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}}

where
A
is an atom. We cover
S
with a family of atoms
\{B_{i}\}_{i}

and take the active/inert factorisation

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{B_{i}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{S}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{A_{i}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{A}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{i}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha}

The bordism
\alpha_{i}:B_{i}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}A_{i}
is again a degeneracy
bordism and so the diagrammatic
n
-truss
A_{i}
is an atom.
Therefore,
\alpha_{i}
is an active map between atoms and so by the previous
step we know that the induced map
\Sigma^{\prime}(\alpha_{i}):\Sigma^{\prime}(A_{i})\to\Sigma^{\prime}(B_{i})

is an equivalence.
Since
\Sigma^{\prime}
satisfies the sheaf condition by construction, the map
\Sigma^{\prime}(\alpha)

decomposes as the limit

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Sigma^{\prime}(A)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Sigma^{\prime}(S)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\lim_{i}\Sigma^{\prime}(A_{i})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\lim_{i}\Sigma^{\prime}(B_{i})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{\prime}(\alpha)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lim_{i}\Sigma^{\prime}(\alpha_{i})}

A limit of equivalences is again an equivalence and so
\Sigma^{\prime}(\alpha)

is an equivalence as well.

3.

Now let
\alpha:A\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}S
be any active map in
\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}}

so that
A
is an atom. By the definition of
\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
we then have
an equivalence between the normal forms

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{S}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{nf}(A)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\textup{nf}(S)}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\equiv}

In particular
\textup{nf}(S)
is also an atom and the vertical maps
in the diagram are degeneracy bordisms into an atom.
Applying the functor
\Sigma^{\prime}
we obtain a diagram of spaces

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Sigma^{\prime}(\textup{nf}(S))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Sigma^{\prime}(\textup{nf}(A))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Sigma^{\prime}(S)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Sigma^{\prime}(A)}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}

where the vertical maps are equivalences by the previous step.
Therefore,
\Sigma^{\prime}(\alpha)
is an equivalence.

4.

Finally, let
\alpha:R\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}S
be any active bordism in
\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
.
Then the atoms
\{A_{i}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}R\}_{i}
which cover
R
induce a covering

\{S_{i}\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}S\}_{i}
via the active/inert factorisation:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{A_{i}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{R}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{S_{i}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{S}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{i}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha}

Because
\Sigma^{\prime}
satisfies the sheaf condition, the map

\Sigma^{\prime}(\alpha)
is equivalent to its decomposition for the
chosen covers

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Sigma^{\prime}(S)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Sigma^{\prime}(R)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\lim_{i}\Sigma^{\prime}(S_{i})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\lim_{i}\Sigma^{\prime}(A_{i})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{\prime}(\alpha)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lim_{i}\Sigma^{\prime}(\alpha_{i})}

By the previous step each
\Sigma^{\prime}(\alpha_{i})
is an equivalence.
It then follows that
\Sigma^{\prime}(\alpha)
must be an equivalence as well.

The presheaf
\Sigma
on
\textup{T}^{n}_{\textup{d}}
resulted from applying the composite
functor
L^{*}\circ L_{*}\circ\mathfrak{t}^{*}
to the presheaf
\mathcal{F}

representing an
n
-diagrammatic space.
Therefore, the bottom row of (
4.9
) restricts
to a functor
\mathbb{U}:\textup{Cat}_{(\infty,n)}\to\cramped{\textup{Cptd}}_{(\infty,n)}
that is right adjoint
to
\mathbb{F}
.
∎

Observation 4.4.3.4
.

Let us unpack what the functor
\mathbb{U}:\textup{Cat}_{(\infty,n)}\to\cramped{\textup{Cptd}}_{(\infty,n)}
does
on some
(\infty,n)
-category
\mathcal{C}
presented as an
n
-diagrammatic space.
Suppose that
A\in\cramped{\dot{\textup{T}}}^{n}
is an (unlabelled) atom and

a:A\to\mathcal{C}
a cell of shape
A
in
\mathcal{C}
.
The
algebraic codimension
of the cell
a
is the maximum

0\leq d\leq n
such that
a
factors through a degeneracy bordism

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{B}}

where
B
is an atom of singular depth
d
.
When
A
is equipped with labels
\ell
in
[n]
so that
(A,\ell)

is a diagrammatic
n
-truss, then the maps
(A,\ell)\to\mathbb{U}(\mathcal{C})

correspond to maps
A\to\mathcal{C}
with the restriction that each for each
subatom
B\mathrel{\vtop{\halign{#\cr\hfil$\mapstochar\mkern 5.0mu$\hfil\cr$\to$\cr}}}A
the algebraic codimension of the induced subcell in
\mathcal{C}

is bounded above by the label.
This restriction is enforced by the coreflector
L^{*}\circ L_{*}
applied
in Proposition
4.4.3.3
.
In particular, every cell in
\mathcal{C}
has multiple versions as a generator
in the diagrammatic computad
\operatorname{U}(\mathcal{C})
.
For instance, an object
x
of
\mathcal{C}
is represented as a
0
-cell,
as the identity
1
-cell
\textup{id}:x\to x
, as an identity
2
-cell

\textup{id}:\textup{id}_{x}\to\textup{id}_{x}
, etc.
